strategies.name: Cashback portals and shopping rebates
strategies.summary: Earn a percentage back on online purchases you would make anyway by clicking through cashback portals first.
strategies.howItWorks: Cashback sites (Rakuten, TopCashback, Quidco, ShopBack, iGraal, Cashrewards) earn affiliate commissions from merchants and pass most of it to you. You install the browser extension, shop through it, the merchant confirms the order after the return window, and the portal pays you by PayPal or bank. Earnings depend on your own spending (typically 1-10% back) plus referral bonuses for inviting friends. Not a business, but a near-automatic rebate.

payout.minimumPayout: Rakuten US $5 confirmed cash back; TopCashback US no stated minimum; ShopBack ~S$10 (unverified)
payout.frequency: Rakuten quarterly (15 Feb/May/Aug/Nov); TopCashback on demand once available
payout.notes: Cashback is pending 30-90 days until the merchant confirms (TopCashback: varies per retailer). Rakuten balances under $5 roll to the next quarter. ShopBack minimum not confirmed on an official page.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; in most jurisdictions purchase rebates are not taxable income (referral bonuses may be).

availability.notes: Major portals serve US, UK, Canada, Germany, France, Japan (Rakuten points), Australia, Singapore, Malaysia, Philippines, Thailand, Taiwan, Indonesia, South Korea (ShopBack); thinner in Africa/Central Asia.

automationPlan: Price-comparison script checks best portal rate
strategies.evidence: Rakuten advertises billions in cumulative cash back paid to members; TopCashback and ShopBack publish member payout totals.

skills: remembering to click through before buying; extension automates it

unitEconomics.unit: per $100 of purchases routed through a portal
unitEconomics.notes: Typical retailer rates 1-10% of purchase value; $3 per $100 is a median blend (estimate). Pays only on spending you would make anyway.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). No fixed cost; first payout waits for 30-90 day merchant confirmation and quarterly payout cycles.

marketConditions.notes: Portals keep paying because merchants pay them affiliate commissions, but rates have been trimmed and tracking is fragile (ad blockers, cookie loss). Profit is tiny but nearly certain; $100/month requires ~$3,000/month of routed spending. The real failure mode is buying things you did not need to chase cashback.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Not priced by you: compare portals per purchase and stack with card rewards.
profitPath: Month 0: join 1-2 portals, install the extension (cost $0)
Month 1-3: cashback pending until merchants confirm
Month 3-6: first quarterly payout (expected $10-$40)
Month 6-12: steady $5-$20/month on normal spending

strategies.name: Share idle gaming PC compute with Salad
strategies.summary: Run the Salad desktop app so your idle GPU/CPU performs containerized cloud workloads; redeem balance for PayPal cash or gift cards.
strategies.howItWorks: Salad resells distributed consumer GPU capacity to AI companies (image generation, transcription, batch inference). You install the app on a Windows gaming PC; when idle, it runs workloads and credits your Salad balance. You redeem from the storefront, choosing PayPal where supported (gift cards otherwise). Unlike Vast you do not set prices; it is consumer-grade and simpler, but pays less.

payout.minimumPayout: Storefront reward price (small PayPal denominations; check storefront)
payout.notes: PayPal rewards are bought from the Salad Storefront and delivered by a third-party vendor within ~24h (USD; converted to 14 currencies). Exact minimum PayPal denomination is only visible when logged in (unverified). Gift cards do not count as a bank path.

legality.notes: Legal; Salad is fiat-based.

availability.notes: Official supported-PayPal-country list covers 32 of 50 reference countries; NOT supported: Armenia, Ukraine, Nigeria, Tunisia, Ghana, Sri Lanka, Zambia, Angola, Lebanon, Bangladesh, Uganda, Zimbabwe, Kyrgyzstan, Cambodia, Thailand, Libya, Iraq, Nepal (there, gift cards only, which fails the bank-path rule).

automationPlan: Auto-redeem when balance reaches PayPal reward amount
strategies.evidence: Salad's support documents PayPal redemption flow; Trustpilot users report PayPal payouts (mixed).

equipment: gaming PC with a modern NVIDIA GPU

unitEconomics.unit: per 100 hours of idle machine time
unitEconomics.notes: Earnings vary by GPU and demand, roughly $0.05-$0.25/hour (estimated; Salad publishes no per-hour rates); cost = electricity (~0.3 kW x 100 h x $0.15/kWh). Reward-store denominations net out any platform cut.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). No fixed cost; electricity counted per unit.

marketConditions.notes: AI inference demand keeps Salad busy, but earnings per hour fell as more gamers joined. Profit is small and depends on electricity price and GPU tier; high-tariff countries often net zero after power. Hardware wear is the hidden cost.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Not priced by you; run only when electricity is cheap and redeem as soon as the minimum PayPal denomination is reached.
profitPath: Month 0: install app and let it chop (cost $0)
Month 1: first redemption to PayPal ($5-$20)
Month 2-6: check that earnings exceed power cost
Month 6-12: steady $10-$30/month net on a mid-range GPU

strategies.name: Passive data-sharing panels (Nielsen Computer & Mobile Panel, MobileXpression, Savvy Connect)
strategies.summary: Install a research company's metering app and earn a fixed yearly reward for letting it measure your browsing and app usage.
strategies.howItWorks: Audience-measurement firms recruit panelists who install a meter on phones or computers. Nielsen pays up to about $50–$60 a year per device in points plus prize draws; MobileXpression gives weekly credits; SavvyConnect (SurveySavvy) pays $3 per device type per month. Rewards are redeemed for PayPal cash or gift cards. It is fully passive after installation, the sums are small and certain, and the trade-off is privacy: everything the device does is recorded.

payout.notes: SavvyConnect (official): $3 USD for each type of device per month. Nielsen's panel site and MobileXpression's site returned no readable content, so their reward amounts (reported as about $50/year per device in points for Nielsen) remain unverified.

legality.notes: Legal: you consent to measurement of your own devices. Do not install on employer devices or devices used by others without consent.

availability.notes: Nielsen panels run in the US, UK, Germany, Australia and a few others; MobileXpression and SavvyConnect are US-only.

automationPlan: Fully passive after install; keep the meter running.
Automate reward redemption reminders and payout logging.
risks: Total loss of browsing privacy on that device
Panel acceptance depends on demographic quotas
strategies.evidence: Nielsen has run paid audience panels for decades and states the reward amounts on its panel sites.

unitEconomics.notes: SavvyConnect pays $3 per device type per month (official page); Nielsen Computer & Mobile Panel rewards (about $50/year per device reported) are estimated because Nielsen's pages could not be read.

breakEven.notes: No fixed costs, so every paid unit is profit; break-even equals the time to the first payout. First redemption after 1-3 months of points.

marketConditions.notes: Audience-measurement firms still need metered panels, but acceptance depends on demographic quotas and most programmes are US-only. The real cost is privacy. profitLikelihoodPercent here is the chance of any steady net profit (no costs are involved), calibrated to the catalog's survey-panel anchor; nobody reaches $100/month.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Not applicable.
profitPath: Month 0: apply and install meters (cost $0)
Month 1-2: accumulate points
Month 3-6: first redemption: $3-10/month
Month 6-12: plateau

strategies.name: Passive bandwidth sharing (Honeygain, Pawns.app)
strategies.summary: Run an app that resells your spare internet bandwidth as a residential proxy network and pays per GB shared.
strategies.howItWorks: Proxy companies route customers' traffic (price monitoring, ad verification, scraping) through your home IP. You install the app and leave it running. A typical income is about $1-3 per device per month, so reaching Honeygain's $20 minimum can take many months; Pawns pays from $5. You are legally exposed because unknown third parties' traffic leaves your IP, and Honeygain's terms make you responsible for checking that your ISP allows it.

methods: Honeygain: PayPal (USD) or crypto via JumpTask
payout.frequency: on request once the threshold is reached
payout.notes: Honeygain processes payouts in 2-3 business days. Its terms void earnings after 6 months without sharing or payouts, and above-threshold earnings expire after 24 months. PayPal may charge fees.

legality.notes: Legal in itself, but it often breaches residential ISP terms; Honeygain's terms require you to check your ISP contract and accept risks such as blocklisting. Avoid it on employer, shared or metered networks. Honeygain excludes sanctioned regions (incl. occupied Ukrainian regions), not whole reference countries.

availability.notes: Available in most countries. Earnings are much lower in low-demand geographies.

strategies.evidence: Honeygain's official payout page and terms document the $20 threshold, PayPal/JumpTask methods, 2-3 day processing and expiry rules. Pawns.app's site states payouts from $5. Reviews report $1-3/month per device.

equipment: always-on computer or phone on an unmetered home connection

unitEconomics.notes: Reviews report $1-3 per device per month; electricity is treated as zero because the device is already on.

breakEven.notes: No fixed costs, so every paid unit is profit; break-even equals the time to the first payout. Reaching the $5 Pawns minimum takes about 2-3 months; Honeygain's $20 can take a year.

marketConditions.notes: AI scraping has increased demand for residential proxies, but supply of sharers has grown faster, so per-GB rates keep falling. Earnings depend heavily on your country and IP reputation, and ISPs or security vendors can flag the IP. Essentially nobody reaches $100/month; profit likelihood here means ever receiving a net payout.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Not applicable; rates are fixed by the app.
profitPath: Month 0: check ISP terms, install on owned devices (cost $0)
Month 1-3: accumulate to the $5 Pawns threshold
Month 3-6: first payout; $2-5/month
Month 6-12: stays at $1-15/month; stop if your IP gets blocklisted

strategies.name: High-yield savings, money-market funds and government bills
strategies.summary: Earn near-risk-free interest on idle cash via high-yield deposit accounts, money-market funds or treasury bills.
strategies.howItWorks: You move cash from a zero-interest account into an insured high-yield savings account, a government money-market fund, or buy short-dated government bills directly (TreasuryDirect, Tesouro Direto, NS&I, Singapore T-bills, Nigerian/Kenyan T-bill auctions). The bank or government pays interest because it is borrowing your money. Returns scale with capital; a baseline, not a business.
platforms: Online banks (Marcus, Ally, Chase UK, Trade Republic)

payout.notes: Savings interest posts monthly; T-bills pay at maturity (4-52 weeks).

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; Islamic equivalents (profit-sharing deposits, sukuk) exist.
complianceRequirements: stay under deposit-insurance limits per bank

availability.notes: Some interest-bearing option exists in every reference country. USD rates checked Nov 2026: US Treasury bill auctions in Oct 2026 cleared at about 4.1-4.35% (13-week ~4.15-4.2%); the FDIC national average savings rate is only 0.38% (Oct 2026), so you must pick an online high-yield account or MMF. Local-currency rates are much higher in Brazil, Nigeria, Kenya, Argentina but with inflation/FX risk. Income = capital x rate (e.g. $10k at 4% = ~$33/month); capital is required and $1,000 yields only ~$3/month.

automationPlan: Auto-sweep idle balances above a threshold into HYSA/MMF
Rate-monitoring script to switch banks when rates drop
strategies.evidence: Interest is contractually paid; TreasuryDirect/Fiscal Data auction results (Oct 2026 bills ~4.1-4.35%) and FDIC national rates (savings avg 0.38%, rate cap 4.63%, Oct 2026) document yields.

tools: online high-yield savings account, money-market fund or TreasuryDirect (free)
skills: none beyond comparing rates and deposit-insurance limits

unitEconomics.notes: Annual interest on $1,000: ~2% in euro accounts (ECB deposit rate 2.50% since 16 Sep 2026), ~3.5% in GBP accounts (Bank Rate 3.75%, Sep 2026), ~4.0-4.3% in USD T-bills/HYSA (Oct 2026 auctions 4.1-4.35%), so $20-$45. Emerging-market local rates are higher but carry FX/inflation risk. Profit depends on capital, not effort: $1,000 earns ~$3/month; ~$30,000 is needed for $100/month.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). No fixed cost. The deposit is not spent and can be withdrawn, so startup recovery is not applicable; first interest posts within ~30 days.

marketConditions.notes: Profit is almost certain in nominal terms because interest is contractual and deposits are insured up to limits, but it scales only with the capital you bring, not with effort or skill. USD rates have been drifting down with policy cuts; after inflation the real return is near zero. Likelihood is for any positive net return; reaching $100/month needs roughly $30,000 at 4%.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Not priced by you: move cash to the best insured rate and re-check quarterly; ladder T-bills to lock rates if cuts are expected.
profitPath: Month 0: open an online HYSA/MMF and move idle cash (capital $1,000+, kept)
Month 1: first interest (~$3 per $1,000)
Month 3-6: automate a monthly sweep of surplus cash; income grows only with deposits
Month 6-12: optional T-bill ladder; expect ~$40 per $1,000 per year

strategies.name: Rent out a spare GPU rig on Vast.ai
strategies.summary: List an idle NVIDIA GPU machine on Vast.ai's marketplace and earn per-hour rental fees from AI/ML customers.
strategies.howItWorks: You install the Vast.ai host software on an Ubuntu machine with a modern NVIDIA GPU (RTX 3090/4090 class or better) and set hourly prices. Renters run Docker containers for AI training/inference and pay per hour; Vast takes a fee. Earnings depend on GPU demand, reliability score, bandwidth and your pricing; electricity is the main cost. RunPod's Community Cloud is closed to new hosts, so Vast is the main fiat-paying option.

payout.notes: No direct bank/ACH/wire/SWIFT from Vast; balances under $20 roll forward; invoices generated Fridays, generally paid the following Friday; first payout can take up to two weeks. Hosts must be able to receive B2B payments through their chosen provider.

legality.notes: Renting your own hardware's compute is legal; check residential electricity/ISP terms and local business registration.

availability.notes: Hosting is open globally; payout depends on Wise/PayPal/Stripe support in your country. capitalRequiredUsd assumes you already own the GPU.

risks: Electricity may exceed earnings for older GPUs
strategies.evidence: Vast.ai official host docs document the $20 minimum and weekly payouts; Vast publishes host-earnings articles; hosts report earnings on forums.

skills: network port forwarding and uptime monitoring
equipment: NVIDIA GPU rig you already own (RTX 3090/4090 or better)
accounts: PayPal/Wise or crypto payout per Vast options

unitEconomics.notes: Consumer GPUs rent at ~$0.15-$0.40/hour (data-centre GPUs higher); cost = electricity (~0.5 kW x 100 h x $0.15/kWh). Vast host-side fee ~25% is estimated (not published in the Vast host payment, earnings or FAQ docs). Hardware depreciation not included.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). No fixed cost if the rig already exists and runs on home internet; electricity is counted per unit.

marketConditions.notes: AI demand keeps GPU rental utilisation healthy, but a 2025-2026 supply glut pushed hourly prices down sharply, especially for older cards. Profit depends on cheap electricity (US, Canada, parts of Asia) and high uptime; in Germany/UK-level electricity prices margins can go negative. Buying a GPU just to rent it rarely pays back.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Undercut similar machines slightly to get occupancy and reliability ratings, then raise toward the market median.
profitPath: Month 0: install host software and pass verification (cost $0)
Month 1: first rentals; expected $20-$60
Month 2-6: tune pricing to keep 50%+ occupancy
Month 6-12: $30-$100/month net per consumer GPU

strategies.name: Sell unwanted gift cards for cash (CardCash, Raise, GCX)
strategies.summary: Convert gift cards you will not use into bank or PayPal cash at 70–92% of face value through regulated gift-card exchanges.
strategies.howItWorks: Gift-card exchanges buy unwanted cards outright (CardCash pays up to about 92% of face value) or let you list them for sale to other buyers (GCX). You enter the card number, accept the offer and are paid by ACH, PayPal or cheque after verification. Raise.com now focuses on selling discounted cards to buyers and states it 'operates separately from the GCX Marketplace', where reselling happens. This is a one-off source of cash rather than income, but it is near-certain and useful for turning gift-card-only rewards from other programs into money in a bank.

payout.notes: CardCash and GCX pages block automated reading, so rates, fees and timelines (reported: CardCash 70–92% of face value, ACH/PayPal/cheque, 1–5 business days after verification) are from third-party sources. Cardpool was dropped from the list (no longer operating).

legality.notes: Legal; exchanges perform fraud checks and require ID. Selling cards you did not legitimately obtain is fraud.

availability.notes: Primarily US (CardCash, Raise, GCX). UK has Cardyard; other countries have limited options.

automationPlan: Script to compare offers across exchanges.
Automate conversion of gift-card rewards from other programs (e.g., Microsoft Rewards, Fetch) into cash.
risks: Cards with zero balance are rejected and may trigger account closure
strategies.evidence: CardCash and Raise have operated since 2009–2013 and are the standard way US consumers liquidate gift cards; both publish payout methods and timelines.

unitEconomics.notes: Exchanges pay about 70-92% of face value (estimated from third-party reports; CardCash and Raise/GCX rate pages are bot-blocked or unpublished); the 18% fee is the median discount.

breakEven.notes: No fixed costs, so every paid unit is profit; break-even equals the time to the first payout. Paid 1-5 business days after verification; one-off cash.

marketConditions.notes: Gift-card exchanges are a mature US market; payout is near-certain for legitimate cards with a balance. Rates depend on brand popularity. Profit likelihood reflects converting a card you would not use; it is not recurring income.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Check offers on 2-3 exchanges and sell popular-brand cards first, since they fetch 85-92%.
profitPath: Month 0: collect unwanted cards and reward-program gift cards (cost $0)
Month 1: sell and receive ACH/PayPal
Month 2-6: convert gift-card rewards from other programmes as they arrive
Month 6-12: occasional one-off cash

strategies.name: License a Professional Voice Clone on the ElevenLabs Voice Library
strategies.summary: Record a high-quality voice dataset once, publish it as a Professional Voice Clone, and earn every time paid ElevenLabs users generate speech with it.
strategies.howItWorks: You record 30 min to 3 h of clean studio-quality speech and create a Professional Voice Clone (PVC), then share it in the public Voice Library with a description, tags and a notice period. Paying ElevenLabs users pick your voice for narration, ads, games and agents; ElevenLabs pays you per character generated by paid users. The work is front-loaded: after verification the voice earns with no further recording. Distinct, well-described niche voices (accents, ages, styles) earn more than generic ones.

payout.frequency: automatic every 6-8 days once threshold is met
payout.notes: Only usage by paid users counts. Payouts run automatically via Stripe Connect every 6-8 days once earnings pass the threshold ($10 in most countries). A paid plan is not required to receive payouts, but creating a Professional Voice Clone requires the Creator plan or higher.

legality.notes: Licensing your own voice is legal everywhere in the reference set; you may only clone your OWN voice (identity verification enforces this).
complianceRequirements: US tax withholding on US-customer usage

availability.notes: Depends on Stripe Connect payout support for your country; unsupported countries cannot receive payouts.

automationPlan: Agent writes the voice description, tags and use-case copy
Agent monitors the earnings dashboard and usage trends
Agent drafts promo posts/demos linking the voice (optional)
manualSteps: Record clean audio of your own voice
Buy one month of Creator plan to create the PVC
Stripe Connect KYC and bank linking
fullCycle: Auto payout to bank via Stripe
risks: Earnings concentrated in top voices; most earn little
Rates set by notice period, not by you
Your voice may be used in content you dislike (within ElevenLabs ToS)
strategies.evidence: ElevenLabs blog (May 2026, updated Sep 2026) reports voice creators have earned over $22M with 10,400+ creators paid; the official payouts help page documents the $10 threshold and 6-8 day automatic Stripe payouts.

tools: ElevenLabs Creator plan ($22/mo; first month $11, needed one month to create the PVC)
skills: basic audio recording and noise cleanup

unitEconomics.notes: Royalties are paid per character generated by paid users at ElevenLabs-set rates; figures are monthly royalties per shared voice (estimated from the $22M/10,400+ creators disclosure: heavily skewed). Platform share is already deducted. ElevenLabs does not publish per-character rates; the payout rate depends on the notice period chosen; payouts go out every 6-8 days above a ~$10 threshold.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). No recurring cost after the PVC is created (a paid plan is not needed to receive payouts). Break-even is the month royalties first exceed $10.

marketConditions.notes: Distinctive niche voices (specific accents, ages, narration styles) earn most; the library now holds many thousands of voices, so generic voices get little use. Usage grows with AI audiobooks and voice agents, but ElevenLabs controls rates and discovery. Failure mode: a technically fine voice that ranks low and earns a few dollars a month.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: You do not set prices directly; choose a longer notice period (higher rate tier) only if your voice is distinctive, and optimise the description and sample for discovery.
profitPath: Month 0: record 1-3 hours, create and verify PVC, share in library (cost $22)
Month 1-2: first royalties; $0-$20
Month 3-6: refine description/samples, add a second style; $5-$50/month
Month 6-12: passive royalties; $15 median, $100+ for distinctive voices

strategies.name: Dividend index investing via robo-advisors or index funds
strategies.summary: Invest regularly in diversified index ETFs via a robo-advisor and collect dividends plus long-run growth.
strategies.howItWorks: Robo-advisors (Betterment, Wealthfront, Nutmeg, Scalable Capital, StashAway, Syfe, Wahed, Bamboo/Risevest, Groww) automatically buy and rebalance low-cost index ETFs for a 0.25-0.75% fee. Companies in the index pay dividends (~1.5-4% yield), which you can withdraw or reinvest. Income is passive but scales with capital and carries market risk; it is not a quick money maker.

payout.minimumPayout: Usually none; some platforms $1-$100 minimum withdrawal
payout.notes: First dividend arrives at next quarterly distribution. Betterment (Nov 2026): 0.25%/year with $200+/month deposits or $24k+ balance, otherwise $5/month, which eats small balances.

legality.notes: Investing in domestic funds is legal everywhere (hence 100%). The listed countries restrict only the foreign robo-advisor route under capital controls - use domestic or Sharia-compliant funds there.

availability.notes: Local robo-advisors or index funds exist in most reference countries; the global platforms cover US/UK/EU/SG/MY/AU. Wahed operates in several Muslim-majority countries.

risks: Platform shutdowns (assets are custodied, but transfers take time)
strategies.evidence: S&P SPIVA scorecards show most active funds underperform indices over 10-15 years; robo platforms publish dividend distributions and AUM.

tools: robo-advisor (e.g. Betterment 0.25%/yr with $200+/month deposits or a $24,000+ balance, else $5/month) or a zero-fee broker with index ETFs
skills: understanding volatility and long horizons; no stock picking needed
accounts: investment account + KYC and tax ID
linked bank account for automatic deposits

unitEconomics.notes: Total return per $1,000 per year: long-run equity average ~7% ($70) of which dividends ~1.5% ($15); a bad year can be -20%. Cost = 0.25% management fee ($2.50). Profit depends on capital, not effort: $1,000 yields ~$1/month in dividends; a $5/month flat fee on small balances eats most of it.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). No fixed cost if you avoid flat-fee plans. Capital is invested, not spent, so startup recovery is not applicable (but the balance can fall).

marketConditions.notes: Low-cost index investing keeps winning against active funds (SPIVA), and robo-advisors have cut fees, but returns depend entirely on capital and market direction. Over any single 12-month window equities are positive roughly 3 years in 4, so likelihood is ~70% for any net gain; cash dividends of $100/month need ~$80,000 invested. Failure modes: selling in a drawdown, flat monthly fees on tiny balances, currency risk.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Not priced by you: choose the lowest total expense (fund OER + platform fee) and automate monthly deposits.
profitPath: Month 0: open a robo/index account and invest $500-$1,000 (kept as an asset)
Month 1-3: set up automatic monthly deposits; first quarterly dividend
Month 3-6: reinvest dividends; ignore volatility
Month 6-12: expected ~$70 per $1,000 per year in total return, highly variable

strategies.name: Recover money you are already owed (unclaimed property, class-action settlements, refunds, overpaid tax)
strategies.summary: Search official unclaimed-property registries, settlement claim sites and refund schemes for money that is legally yours and claim it online.
strategies.howItWorks: Governments hold dormant bank balances, uncashed cheques, deposits and insurance proceeds in unclaimed-property registries that anyone can search free (US: each state's registry and MissingMoney.com; UK: My Lost Account, Gretel; Canada: Bank of Canada; Australia: ASIC MoneySmart). Class-action settlements publish claim forms where eligible consumers get cash. Many people are also owed tax refunds, energy or telecom overpayments, or forgotten pension pots. This is not income, but it is money in a bank account with no risk and a short online form, and it is one of the highest-probability 'payouts' for anyone who has never looked.

payout.notes: Government registries are free; never pay a finder fee above a few percent. Settlement payouts can take months after the claims deadline.

legality.notes: Claiming your own property is legal everywhere. Filing settlement claims you are not eligible for is fraud; only claim where you genuinely qualify.
complianceRequirements: only claim what you are eligible for

availability.notes: Formal unclaimed-property registries exist in the US, UK, Canada, Australia, and several EU and Asian countries; class-action claim systems are mainly US.

automationPlan: Script to search official registries for your name and past addresses on a schedule.
AI agent to watch settlement lists and flag ones matching products/services you used.
Pre-fill claim forms from a stored profile (you review and submit).
fullCycle: Payment by cheque or bank transfer
risks: Nothing may be owed to you
strategies.evidence: US states hold tens of billions in unclaimed property and return billions each year; the NAUPA-run MissingMoney.com is the official multi-state search.

tools: My Lost Account / Bank of Canada / ASIC MoneySmart (free)

unitEconomics.notes: Class-action settlements commonly pay $5-100 per claimant; unclaimed-property balances vary widely (estimate).

breakEven.notes: No fixed costs, so every paid unit is profit; break-even equals the time to the first payout. Registry claims take weeks; settlement payouts can take months after the deadline.

marketConditions.notes: NAUPA says about 1 in 7 Americans has unclaimed property, and AI tools make it easy to match yourself to open settlements. This is recovery of money already owed, not income, and nothing may be owed to you. Never pay finder services more than a few percent.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Not applicable.
profitPath: Month 0: search registries for every past name and address (cost $0)
Month 1-3: file claims; first payments arrive
Month 3-6: file eligible settlement claims as they open
Month 6-12: occasional small payouts

strategies.name: Rent spare disk space and bandwidth as a Storj storage node
strategies.summary: Run a Storj storage node on a spare hard drive and earn monthly USDC stablecoin payouts for stored data and egress; convert to fiat via an exchange.
strategies.howItWorks: Storj's decentralized S3-compatible cloud pays node operators for disk space used and download bandwidth. You run the node (Docker) on an always-on machine with a 1TB+ drive and open port. Earnings are calculated in USD and paid monthly in USDC on Ethereum (Storj no longer pays in STORJ tokens); the zkSync L2 option was sunset on 1 Sep 2026, so all payouts go via Ethereum L1 and are only sent when the gas fee is under 25% of the amount. New nodes have part of earnings held back during the first months. Sia (hostd) requires Siacoin collateral, a buy-in; prefer Storj.

payout.minimumPayout: Dynamic: payout skipped if gas fee exceeds 25% of amount (e.g. $68.56 minimum at a $17.14 fee)
payout.notes: Unpaid balances roll over to the next month. zkSync payouts ended 1 Sep 2026. Fiat conversion requires a regulated exchange in your country; pooling all your nodes on one wallet helps clear the threshold.

restrictedIn: Morocco (2017 crypto ban still formally in force)
Angola (2024 crypto-mining ban; applicability to storage nodes unclear)
legality.notes: Running the node is legal everywhere; receiving and converting crypto (including stablecoins) is banned or effectively prohibited in about 6-7 reference countries, giving ~86% coverage. Ecuador, Jordan and Lebanon restrict crypto as payment/banking but do not ban holding it. Country legal status is from general knowledge, not re-verified this session.

availability.notes: Nodes work anywhere with stable internet; fiat off-ramp needed.

fullCycle: Receive USDC once above gas threshold
risks: L1 gas threshold can delay small payouts for months
strategies.evidence: Storj's official node payout docs (storj.dev) describe monthly USDC payouts, the 25% gas-fee threshold rule and the zkSync sunset. paymentProbability lowered from 5 to 4 because small nodes may need several months to clear the L1 threshold.

skills: port forwarding and keeping the node online 99%+
accounts: regulated crypto exchange account to convert to fiat

unitEconomics.notes: Storj pays $1.35 per TB-month stored and $1.00 per TB egress (rates as of 1 Sep 2026); with typical egress ~$1.5/TB-month blended, rounded to $1 median. Fee = estimated exchange/withdrawal costs; Ethereum gas can delay payouts.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). Fixed cost = electricity for an always-on low-power box (~$2/month); a new node fills slowly (vetting takes months).

marketConditions.notes: Storj reduced node payouts in 2024 and a new node fills only ~0.5-1 TB per year, so income is a few dollars a month. It is only worth it on hardware that is already running; buying drives to farm never pays back. Crypto conversion adds friction. Verifier: median price per TB-month lowered from $2 to $1 to match the published $1.35/TB storage rate.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Not priced by you; maximise uptime and stored data, and pool nodes on one wallet to clear the payout threshold.
profitPath: Month 0: set up node on an existing drive (cost $0)
Month 1-6: vetting; payouts below threshold roll over
Month 6-12: $2-$8/month as the node fills
Month 12+: convert USDC to fiat once a year to minimise fees

strategies.name: Selling used goods online (eBay, Vinted, Mercari, local classifieds)
strategies.summary: Sell items you own or source cheaply (thrift, garage sales) on second-hand marketplaces such as eBay, Vinted, Mercari or Facebook Marketplace.
strategies.howItWorks: Start by decluttering your own items for immediate cash, then optionally source underpriced goods from thrift stores, estate sales or free listings. AI can write titles/descriptions and price from sold comps. Buyers pay through the platform; you ship (or meet locally) and the platform releases funds after delivery. Vinted charges the buyer a protection fee so sellers keep the item price; eBay US charges 13.6% + $0.30-0.40 per order in most categories (250 free listings/month); Mercari US fees have changed repeatedly, so check its current fee page.

payout.notes: Funds released after delivery/buyer confirmation (Vinted ~2 days after delivery, unverified). Mercari US: free direct deposit once per day or Instant Pay to debit card for $3 (max $600/month). eBay payout timing not confirmed on an official page (help page blocked).

legality.notes: Selling your own used goods is legal everywhere. Regular resale is a business; tax above thresholds (DAC7, 1099-K).

availability.notes: eBay operates in ~190 markets; regional platforms (Vinted EU/UK, Mercari US/JP, Carousell SEA, OLX/Jiji Africa/Asia/LatAm) cover almost every reference country. PHYSICAL STEP: photographing and shipping items.

automationPlan: AI photo cleanup and listing generation from photos
manualSteps: Packing and shipping or local handover
strategies.evidence: Vinted reports tens of millions of members; eBay has ~130M active buyers; full-time resellers document $2k-$10k/month publicly.

tools: eBay / Vinted / Mercari / Facebook Marketplace apps (free)
AI listing generator from photos (free tiers)

unitEconomics.notes: Median $25 item; cost $5 covers thrift sourcing and packing (items you already own cost $0); eBay final-value fee ~13% + $0.40, Vinted charges buyers not sellers, Mercari ~10%.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). No fixed cost; first sale usually within days.

marketConditions.notes: Second-hand demand keeps growing and AI listing tools (photo-to-listing) cut time per item sharply in 2025-2026. Decluttering your own home is almost always profitable; scaling via thrift sourcing works for people with good eyes for brands. Failure modes: running out of stock to sell, low-value items that are not worth the time, returns and scam buyers.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Price at the median of recent sold listings to sell within a week; use offers/auction for slow items and raise prices on fast-selling categories.
profitPath: Month 0: list 20-30 items you own (cost $0)
Month 1-2: first sales; expected $100-$300
Month 3-6: source from thrift/garage sales in 1-2 categories that sold fastest
Month 6-12: $100-$500/month net at 5-10 hours/week

strategies.name: Bank account sign-up and switching bonuses
strategies.summary: Collect cash bonuses banks pay for opening a new current/checking account and meeting a direct-deposit or switch requirement.
strategies.howItWorks: Offers are country-specific and change monthly. Examples checked Nov 2026: in the US, Chase pays $400 for a new Total Checking account with $1,000+ of direct deposits within 90 days (offer ends 27 Jan 2027, paid within 15 days); in the UK, CASS switch bonuses range GBP 175-300 (Barclays up to GBP 300, Santander GBP 240, HSBC GBP 220, First Direct GBP 210, Lloyds/NatWest GBP 200). Canada and Germany run similar but smaller offers. You open the account, route a payroll or qualifying deposit, meet card/debit conditions, receive the bonus, then keep or close the account after the clawback window. Banks pay because customer lifetime value exceeds the bonus.

methods: bonus credited to the new bank account
payout.minimumPayout: Fixed bonus per offer (e.g. US $400 Chase; UK GBP 175-300)
payout.notes: Chase pays within 15 days of meeting requirements; UK switch bonuses typically within weeks of the switch. Many banks claw back if the account is closed within ~6 months. Requires an existing salary/pay-in of roughly $1,000-$2,000 to route (not spent), hence capitalRequiredUsd 0.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere (standard retail promotion); bonuses are usually taxable interest income.

availability.notes: Country-specific: meaningful recurring offers exist mainly in the US, UK, Canada, Germany and Australia (~5-8 of 50 reference countries). Residency, a local address and often a salary paid in are required. Examples above are dated Nov 2026 and expire; always check the bank's own offer page.

automationPlan: Scrape/RSS-monitor public bonus trackers (Doctor of Credit, MSE) and filter by eligibility
Calendar automation for direct-deposit dates, minimum-balance and earliest-close dates
manualSteps: Closing accounts after the hold period
risks: Each bank pays a given person once
strategies.evidence: Chase's official offer page (Nov 2026) lists a $400 new-checking bonus; MoneySavingExpert (updated 30 Oct 2026) lists seven UK switch bonuses of GBP 175-300.

tools: Doctor of Credit / MoneySavingExpert bonus trackers (free)
skills: reading bonus terms (direct-deposit, hold period, clawback)
basic cash-flow planning; AI can summarise terms but cannot open accounts
accounts: new bank account per offer + KYC
existing salary/direct-deposit source that can be redirected

unitEconomics.notes: US offers $200-$900 (Chase ~$300-400), UK switch offers GBP 175-300; cost covers occasional monthly fees or lost interest on minimum balances (estimate).

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). No fixed cost; first bonus typically posts 45-150 days after opening.

marketConditions.notes: Banks still pay to acquire primary-account customers, so offers persist, but only residents of a few countries (US, UK, CA, DE) with a payroll deposit can play. Supply of fresh offers per person is finite (once-per-lifetime or 12-24 month rules), so income is lumpy and runs out. Failure modes: clawback for early closure, missed direct-deposit requirement, ChexSystems denials. Likelihood here means any positive net within 12 months for eligible residents; a steady $100/month is only reached by people churning 4+ offers a year.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Not priced by you: rank open offers by bonus per required deposit and hold time, and take the easiest high-value offers first.
profitPath: Month 0: pick 1-2 eligible offers from a tracker and open accounts (cost $0)
Month 1-2: route direct deposit, meet requirements; nothing paid yet
Month 3-6: first bonuses post (expected $200-$600 total); start the next offers
Month 6-12: close only after clawback windows; repeat with new banks (expected $100-$150/month averaged)

strategies.name: Real-estate virtual staging and listing photo editing
strategies.summary: AI-assisted virtual staging, day-to-dusk, decluttering and floor-plan redraws for agents and photographers.
strategies.howItWorks: Agents pay per image to make empty or messy rooms sell. Generative inpainting and staging tools do most of the work; you fix perspective, lighting and artifacts and keep structural features truthful. Market to agents and real-estate photographers who batch orders weekly. Staged images must be disclosed as virtually staged in listings.

payout.notes: Upwork: variable 0-15% freelancer service fee set per contract since May 2025 (pre-May-2025 contracts 10%), per Upwork's SEC 10-Q; Upwork help pages block automated fetch. Fiverr: 20% seller fee and 14-day clearance (7 days for Top Rated) are widely reported but Fiverr's help center blocked fetch, so not confirmed from the official page.

legality.notes: Legal; taxable. Do not alter permanent features (views, damage, room size); many MLS and consumer-protection rules require disclosing virtual staging.

availability.notes: Upwork/Fiverr pay out in nearly all reference countries via Payoneer/bank.

automationPlan: AI staging/declutter pipelines with style presets
strategies.evidence: BoxBrownie, a large vendor, publicly prices virtual staging at $30/image (48h) and edits from $2, showing steady paid demand; AI cuts delivery cost far below that.

accounts: Upwork freelancer account + ID verification (proposals cost Connects, ~$0.15 each)
PayPal or Payoneer linked to a bank account

unitEconomics.notes: Estimate anchored on BoxBrownie's public $30/image staging price; freelancers sell $10-$40; fee blends Fiverr 20% and Upwork 0-15%. Fiverr (20%) and Upwork (variable 0-15% since 2025) fee figures are estimated: their official fee pages were bot-blocked when checked in Nov 2026.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only; startup cash is not amortised. Months include ramp-up to the first order.

marketConditions.notes: AI staging apps now sell directly to agents for a few dollars per image, which caps freelance prices, but agents and photographers still pay for realistic, artifact-free results and batch reliability. Demand follows housing transaction volumes, which remained subdued in 2025-2026 in several markets. Winners partner with real-estate photographers who resell staging to many agents.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Offer a free first image to photographers and agents, then volume pricing per image with 24h turnaround and photographer reseller discounts.
profitPath: Month 0: 10 before/after samples, gigs and a simple price sheet (cost $0)
Month 1-2: first batches, expected $50-$200
Month 3-6: 1-3 photographer partners sending weekly batches
Month 6-12: 40-150 images/month

strategies.name: Sell old phones, laptops and games to buyback sites (Decluttr, Gazelle, Swappa, Back Market)
strategies.summary: Get an instant online quote for used electronics, post them in with a free label, and receive a near-guaranteed bank or PayPal payment within days.
strategies.howItWorks: Buyback services quote a price by model and condition, send a prepaid shipping label, inspect the device and pay by PayPal, direct deposit or cheque. Decluttr (US/UK) also buys games, DVDs and books by scanning barcodes. Swappa and Back Market are marketplaces with buyer protection where you set the price and typically earn 20–40% more than buyback quotes. It is a one-off, not recurring, but the probability of being paid is close to certain and most households have unused devices.

payout.notes: Gazelle (owned by ecoATM; official site): quote, free shipping, payout via PayPal or check. Decluttr (reported: paid the day after inspection by direct deposit or PayPal) and Swappa (reported: PayPal at sale) block automated reading, so their terms are unconfirmed.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; you must own the items and wipe personal data. Not a business unless done at scale (then resale registration and tax apply).

availability.notes: Decluttr: US/UK. Gazelle, Swappa: US. musicMagpie: UK. Back Market: US, UK, EU, Japan, Australia. Local equivalents exist in most countries.

automationPlan: Script to fetch quotes from several buyback sites and pick the best.
AI can draft marketplace listings from photos.
strategies.evidence: Gazelle (an ecoATM brand) still runs 'Sell to Us' trade-ins paid by PayPal or check; Decluttr, Swappa and Back Market publish seller payout terms.

unitEconomics.notes: Buyback quotes for recent phones and laptops; buyback sites pay postage and take their margin in the quote (marketplaces such as Swappa or Back Market net 20-40% more but charge seller fees).

breakEven.notes: No fixed costs, so every paid unit is profit; break-even equals the time to the first payout. Paid within days of inspection; this is one-off cash, not recurring income.

marketConditions.notes: Refurbished-phone demand is stable, but buyback quotes fall quickly as devices age, so selling sooner pays more. Payment is near-certain apart from downward re-quotes after inspection. Profit likelihood reflects the one-off sale; monthly profit is zero once your unused devices are gone.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Compare quotes across 3+ sites and sell before a new model launch; list higher-value devices on Swappa or Back Market for more than the buyback quote.
profitPath: Month 0: inventory unused devices, compare quotes (cost $0)
Month 1: ship and get paid: $50-600 one-off
Month 2-6: sell remaining household items
Month 6-12: no recurring income unless you start reselling (a different strategy)

strategies.name: Receipt scanning and shopping-data apps paid in cash (Receipt Hog, Ibotta, Shopmium, CoinOut)
strategies.summary: Photograph grocery receipts or link store accounts and receive small cash rewards to PayPal or bank for purchases you were making anyway.
strategies.howItWorks: Market-research apps buy anonymised purchase data by rewarding receipt uploads. Receipt Hog pays points for any receipt and cashes out to PayPal; Ibotta pays cash rebates on specific products to PayPal or bank; Shopmium (France, UK, Belgium, US) pays rebates to PayPal or bank. Nothing changes in how you shop; a weekly photo session yields a few dollars a month. Avoid gift-card-only apps (Fetch) if you want money in a bank.

payout.notes: Ibotta (help centre): withdraw to bank, PayPal or gift cards after reaching $20, redeeming one offer and, for new accounts, waiting 7 days and verifying a phone number. Receipt Hog (run by Numerator): coins redeem for PayPal or Amazon cards; minimum not shown on the official page. Shopmium: refunds are sent within 2 business days of a request; payout method and minimum not confirmed.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; you are selling your own purchase data under the app's privacy policy.

availability.notes: Ibotta, Receipt Hog and CoinOut: mostly US. Shopmium: France, UK, Belgium and US. Checkout 51: Canada. Narrow availability.

automationPlan: Auto-upload e-receipts by linking store accounts or forwarding receipt emails where the app supports it.
strategies.evidence: Ibotta is a public company that reports paying users over $2 billion in cash rewards; Receipt Hog (Numerator) has paid via PayPal since 2012.

tools: Receipt Hog, Ibotta, Shopmium, CoinOut apps (free)

unitEconomics.notes: A weekly receipt session yields a few dollars a month; Ibotta rebates add more if you buy listed products.

breakEven.notes: No fixed costs, so every paid unit is profit; break-even equals the time to the first payout. Ibotta's $20 minimum is the slowest; Receipt Hog and Shopmium pay sooner.

marketConditions.notes: Purchase-data buyers keep these apps funded and payouts are reliable, but availability is mostly US (Shopmium FR/UK/BE/US, Checkout 51 Canada). profitLikelihoodPercent here is the chance of any steady net profit (no costs are involved), calibrated to the catalog's survey-panel anchor; nobody reaches $100/month without large household spending.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Not applicable; never buy products only for a rebate.
profitPath: Month 0: install apps, link PayPal or bank (cost $0)
Month 1-2: reach the first minimum
Month 3-6: $5-10/month
Month 6-12: plateau at $2-30/month

strategies.name: Productized data cleaning, PDF-to-Excel conversion and data-entry gigs
strategies.summary: Fixed-price gigs that clean, dedupe, reformat or extract data from client files, done mostly by scripts and LLMs with a human check.
strategies.howItWorks: List fixed-scope gigs: PDF/scan to Excel, CSV cleanup, CRM dedupe, sheet merges. Small businesses pay because the work is tedious. A pipeline (OCR, pandas, LLM extraction) does most of each order; you spot-check and deliver. Repeat buyers send monthly batches.

payout.notes: Fiverr: 20% fee, 14-day clearance. Upwork: variable 0-15% freelancer fee (2025 change). Not re-confirmed Nov 2026: Fiverr/Upwork help pages block automated checks.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; taxable. Personal data in files triggers GDPR-type duties.

availability.notes: Fiverr/Upwork pay out almost everywhere via Payoneer; PayPal receiving missing in some (e.g. Bangladesh).

validation rules and diff reports before delivery
templated order replies and delivery messages

PayPal or Payoneer linked to a bank account

ChatGPT Plus (~$20/mo) and Canva Pro (~$15/mo) prices are estimated: their pricing pages were bot-blocked.

The median starter nets under $100/month by month 12; failure modes are zero visibility for new gigs and underpricing.

Month 1-2: first 5-15 small orders at $10-$30, expected $50-$200 gross

strategies.name: Collect YouTube Content ID revenue on your own music when others use it
strategies.summary: Register exclusively-owned recordings in YouTube Content ID via a distributor so ad revenue from third-party videos using them is paid to you.
strategies.howItWorks: You release original music through a distributor that offers Content ID (DistroKid's annual per-release 'Social Media Pack' extra, CD Baby Social Video Monetization). YouTube fingerprints the audio and, when any uploader's video uses it, monetizes that video and routes a share of ad revenue to you. Works best for tracks creators reuse (lo-fi, stream background music). Only recordings you own exclusively qualify.

payout.minimumPayout: Distributor-dependent (often no minimum aside from method fees)
payout.notes: Revenue reaches you roughly 2-3 months after views. DistroKid includes Content ID in its annually charged per-release Social Media Pack and passes on ad revenue minus 20% (you keep 80%), shown in the DistroKid Bank tab.

legality.notes: Claiming content you exclusively own is legal; claiming public-domain, royalty-free or others' material violates YouTube policy and can be fraud.
complianceRequirements: exclusive rights to entire recording (no samples, loops from libraries or public-domain elements)

availability.notes: DistroKid and CD Baby accept artists worldwide; YouTube ads run globally.

automationPlan: Automate releases and Content ID opt-in through distributor upload
Monthly script to reconcile claim revenue reports
risks: Low revenue unless tracks are widely reused
Disputes/reputation damage if claims hit licensed users
Incompatible with non-exclusive stock licensing of the same track
Distributor may remove ineligible tracks permanently
strategies.evidence: DistroKid's official help article documents Content ID via the Social Media Pack with a 20% cut; Content ID is a standard monetization line in distributor statements.

tools: DistroKid (~$25/yr) with Social Media Pack (~$5/yr per release) or CD Baby

unitEconomics.notes: Claimed-video revenue is often shared with other claimants and only monetised views pay; ~$0.20-$1.50 per 1,000 claimed views is a rough market range (estimate). DistroKid keeps 20%.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). Fixed cost = distributor renewal amortised (~$3/month).

marketConditions.notes: Pays meaningfully only for tracks that creators actually use (popular background music, viral sounds). YouTube and distributors tightened Content ID eligibility in 2025-2026 to curb abusive claims and AI-generated tracks, and many creators avoid claimed music. Most catalogues earn cents.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Not priced by you; maximise usage by whitelisting creators who credit you and promoting tracks to creator communities.
profitPath: Month 0: distribute 3-10 exclusive tracks with Content ID ($30)
Month 1-3: claims appear; revenue lags 2-3 months
Month 3-6: first payouts (expected under $10/month)
Month 6-12: invest only if one track gets traction

strategies.name: Public-data scraping tools and monitoring reports (Apify Store Actors, paid report subscriptions)
strategies.summary: Publish ToS- and robots.txt-compliant scrapers as paid Actors on Apify Store, and sell recurring monitoring reports built from public data.
strategies.howItWorks: Many businesses want structured public data (listings, prices, job posts, tenders, regulatory filings). On Apify Store you publish an Actor priced per result or event. Users run it on Apify's infrastructure; Apify deducts platform costs, keeps 20% of the profit and pays you monthly after KYC. The same pipelines can feed a paid weekly report (e.g. tender or price tracker) sold through a subscription tool. Most ongoing work is maintenance when target sites change.

payout.minimumPayout: not stated in Apify's public docs (KYC required)
payout.notes: Apify takes 20% (of revenue for rentals; of profit after platform costs for pay-per-result/event). Its current developer docs list only pay-per-event and pay-per-usage models, consistent with rentals being phased out. Payout methods, thresholds and the ~11th-of-month invoice date come from earlier docs and were not re-confirmed.

legality.notes: Scraping public, non-personal data is lawful in most jurisdictions when it respects ToS, robots.txt and database rights. Personal data falls under GDPR and similar laws.
complianceRequirements: no personal data or authentication bypass

availability.notes: Apify pays worldwide outside sanctioned countries. Report subscriptions depend on Stripe/Gumroad support.

automationPlan: Coding agents write and repair Actors
strategies.evidence: Apify's official help article and docs describe the 20% commission, monthly payouts and identity verification (KYC). Apify's partner page reports top independent creators earning over $10k MRR.

tools: Apify platform (free plan with monthly credits)
skills: maintaining scrapers when sites change (AI agents help a lot)

unitEconomics.notes: Store Actors commonly charge $0.50-5 per 1,000 results; Apify deducts about $3 of platform usage and then 20% of the remaining profit (so effective fee is about 17% of price, margin 68%).

breakEven.notes: No fixed costs, so every paid unit is profit; break-even equals the time to the first payout. Platform costs are deducted per run, so there is no fixed bill; first payout comes the month after first paying users.

marketConditions.notes: AI agents now call Apify Actors via MCP, which adds demand, and coding agents make Actors fast to build. Winners pick underserved, compliant data sources and keep them reliable; the failure mode is a scraper nobody finds or one that breaks. Median month-12 net profit was lowered below $100 so it agrees with a profit likelihood under 50% (most starters never reach $100/month).

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Launch slightly below competing Actors with a free trial quota, then raise prices once reviews and reliability stats are strong; bundle a weekly paid report for non-technical buyers.

Month 1-3: first users; $0-50/month
Month 3-6: add Actors, fix breakages fast, improve SEO of Store listings: $50-300/month
Month 6-12: a hit Actor can reach $1,000+/month; most portfolios settle at $50-300

Brand owners add you as a Brand Registry user rather than sharing logins. Sell per-ASIN packages and monthly catalog retainers.

Fiverr: 20% seller fee and 14-day clearance (7 days for Top Rated) are widely reported but Fiverr's help center blocked fetch, so not confirmed from the official page.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; taxable. Must not create fake reviews, keyword-stuff against style guides, or make unsubstantiated product claims.

availability.notes: Upwork/Fiverr pay out in nearly all reference countries via Payoneer/bank.

infographic templates auto-filled from spec sheets

PayPal or Payoneer linked to a bank account

strategies.name: Sell labeled AI-generated stock images, vectors and video on Adobe Stock and Freepik
strategies.summary: Generate commercially-useful stock assets with image/video models and license them on the few major agencies that explicitly accept labeled generative-AI content.
strategies.howItWorks: Adobe Stock and Freepik accept generative-AI submissions if they are labeled as AI, contain no real people/brands/artist names, and meet quality rules. An agent can research high-demand gaps (search trends, seasonal themes), generate batches, upscale, write titles/keywords and upload via FTP/CSV. Buyers (designers, marketers) license assets; you receive a royalty per download. Volume and keyword quality drive income; acceptance rates for AI content are strict.

payout.minimumPayout: Adobe Stock $25 (first payout only after 45 days since first sale); Freepik/Magnific $25 / EUR 50
payout.notes: Adobe: request payout once $25 is reached; PayPal global, Payoneer outside the US, Skrill most countries. Freepik's contributor program now runs under the Magnific brand: pay-per-download from subscriber revenue, invoices generated 2 months after the minimum is reached, paid between the 10th and 15th. New Freepik/Magnific contributors must pass a 150-200 asset first review.

complianceRequirements: generator ToS must grant commercial rights

availability.notes: Adobe Stock contributors worldwide with PayPal/Skrill; Freepik via PayPal/Payoneer, which cover most reference countries.

manualSteps: Create contributor accounts and pass ID check
Spot-check quality and IP risk before upload

High rejection rates, possible account limits for spammy volume

strategies.name: Paid survey panels (Swagbucks, Branded Surveys, Toluna, YouGov, PrizeRebel)
strategies.summary: Join several established market-research panels and cash out small balances to PayPal; the money is small but the payout is close to guaranteed.
strategies.howItWorks: Market-research firms pay panel members for opinions. Each survey pays roughly $0.50–$5 and takes 5–20 minutes. Joining 3–5 panels at once keeps a steady flow of qualifying surveys. Balances are cashed out to PayPal (or bank on some panels) once a low minimum is reached, typically $5–$10. This is labor, not passive income, and the hourly rate is poor, but the payment itself is reliable.

payout.notes: Branded Surveys (official site): 500 points = $5 minimum, via PayPal, bank transfer or Tango gift cards. Swagbucks (help centre): PayPal cash arrives in 2–5 business days; the first PayPal redemption needs matching names and a confirmed bank on PayPal; the SB minimum was not stated on the pages checked. PrizeRebel (official site): PayPal, Bitcoin and gift cards; minimum not confirmed. YouGov/Toluna: PayPal/vouchers shown, thresholds not confirmed on official pages.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere in the reference set. Panels ban multiple accounts, VPN use and automated answering.

availability.notes: Swagbucks help centre: live in most countries in the Americas, Europe and Asia and some in Africa. Branded Surveys: US, Canada and UK residents only (official). Toluna and YouGov run country panels in many markets. Survey Junkie is reported as US/Canada/Australia only (not re-checked). Mobrog runs in 70+ countries with a €5 minimum paid via PayPal/Skrill (unverified).

automationPlan: Automate reminders: a daily script that lists new surveys from panel email notifications.
Automate payout logging: parse PayPal payout emails into the earnings ledger.
manualSteps: Sign up for 3–5 panels with the same email and PayPal
Fill profile questionnaires fully (they drive survey invites)
Take surveys; cash out at minimum
strategies.evidence: Swagbucks publicly states it has paid members over $1 billion in rewards; YouGov, Toluna and Branded Surveys are long-running panels owned by established market-research groups.

tools: 3-5 panels: Swagbucks, Branded Surveys, Toluna, YouGov, PrizeRebel (free)

unitEconomics.notes: Surveys pay $0.50-5 for 5-20 minutes; with disqualifications effective pay is $2-6/hour.

breakEven.notes: No fixed costs, so every paid unit is profit; break-even equals the time to the first payout. First cash-out once a $5-10 minimum is reached.

marketConditions.notes: Panels pay reliably, but buyers worry about bots and AI-written answers, so fraud checks and disqualifications have increased and some research is shifting to synthetic respondents. profitLikelihoodPercent here is the chance of any steady net profit (no costs are involved), calibrated to the catalog's survey-panel anchor; only about 10% reach $100/month, typically US/UK members doing an hour a day across several panels.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Not applicable; skip surveys under $3/hour and prioritise panels that pay for profile surveys and do not screen out late.
profitPath: Month 0: join 3-5 panels, complete all profile questionnaires (cost $0)
Month 1-2: $10-30/month
Month 3-6: focus on the 2 best-paying panels: $20-50/month
Month 6-12: plateau at $20-120/month depending on hours

strategies.name: Crowdtesting and paid bug hunts (Testbirds, test IO, uTest, Testlio)
strategies.summary: Join crowdtesting platforms that pay per approved bug or per completed test cycle on real apps and websites.
strategies.howItWorks: Companies pay crowdtesting vendors to test releases on many real devices. Testers pick test cycles, follow instructions, report bugs with reproduction steps and screenshots, and are paid per approved bug (commonly $5–$50 by severity) or a flat fee per cycle. Payment goes to PayPal or Payoneer monthly. It is structured, well-paid-per-hour work compared with surveys, and bug approval rates improve quickly with experience.

payout.notes: Testlio (official): freelancers are paid hourly, approved payments sent weekly via Payoneer or PayPal, open to all non-sanctioned countries. uTest's payment FAQ is behind login and test IO/Testbirds pages could not be read, so their schedules (reported as twice-monthly/monthly via PayPal/Payoneer) remain unconfirmed.

legality.notes: Fully authorised testing under contract; legal everywhere. Projects are under NDA.

availability.notes: Testlio works with freelancers from any non-sanctioned country; uTest and Testbirds also recruit globally. Payout through PayPal/Payoneer covers nearly all reference countries.

automationPlan: AI can draft bug reports from your notes and screenshots (you verify and submit).
Scripts can run automated checks (link checkers, accessibility scans) that surface candidate bugs for manual confirmation.
manualSteps: Execute test cycles on your devices
strategies.evidence: Applause/uTest has a community of over a million testers and publishes payout schedules; Testbirds and test IO have paid testers since the early 2010s.

tools: uTest, test IO, Testbirds, Testlio portals (free)
AI for drafting bug reports (free tier)

unitEconomics.notes: Bug payouts are commonly $3-50 by severity; Testlio pays hourly instead. 1 hour per approved bug includes duplicates and rejected reports.

breakEven.notes: No fixed costs, so every paid unit is profit; break-even equals the time to the first payout. First payout after the first approved cycle and the platform's monthly or weekly run.

marketConditions.notes: Companies still pay for testing on real devices, but AI-driven test automation absorbs simple regression checks and bug rates have not risen. Testers with many devices and fast, high-quality reports climb ratings and get paid test-case work; beginners lose time to duplicate bugs. profitLikelihoodPercent here is the chance of receiving any real net-positive payout within 12 months (typical income is under $100/month), calibrated to the catalog's survey-panel anchor.

strategies.name: YouTube editing, thumbnails and short-form repurposing for creators and brands
strategies.summary: Turn long videos/podcasts into edited uploads, Shorts/Reels/TikToks with captions, and click-worthy (non-misleading) thumbnails on retainer.
strategies.howItWorks: Creators, coaches and B2B companies with long-form video pay for consistent output. AI clipping finds highlights, auto-captions and reframes to vertical; you finish edits, pacing and thumbnails. Sell monthly packages (e.g. 4 long edits + 20 shorts). You only edit footage the client owns; posting happens from the client's accounts.

payout.minimumPayout: Fiverr: $1 PayPal / $20 bank transfer via Payoneer / $10 Payoneer account; Upwork: per withdrawal method

Fiverr help center (checked in a browser Nov 2026): freelancers earn 80% of the purchase amount including extras and tips (20% fee); earnings become withdrawable 14 days after the order completes (shorter for Top Rated, Seller Plus and Pro; Early Payout skips clearance for a 1% fee). Fiverr withdrawal minimums/fees: PayPal $1 (no fee, ~24 h), bank transfer via Payoneer $20 ($1 fee, 1-7 business days), Payoneer account $10 ($3 fee); max $5,000 per withdrawal.

legality.notes: Legal; taxable. Use licensed music/assets only; no misleading thumbnails or fake engagement.

availability.notes: Upwork/Fiverr pay out in nearly all reference countries via Payoneer/bank.

fullCycle: Build 3 sample edits from own/CC footage
strategies.evidence: Video editing and short-form repurposing are large, persistent Fiverr/Upwork categories; Contra is commission-free for freelancers. Volume figures not verified.

PayPal or Payoneer linked to a bank account

The bottom tier is crowded and AI auto-clippers sold directly to creators undercut simple clip packages. Editors who retain 2-4 clients reach meaningful income within a year.

Month 3-6: 2-3 clients, templates and AI clipping to cut hours
Month 6-12: 3-5 retainers

strategies.name: Audiobooks via Virtual Voice, Google Play auto-narration, INaudio and ACX
strategies.summary: Turn your books into audiobooks (AI narration where allowed) and earn audiobook royalties.
strategies.howItWorks: If you own ebook rights, you can create audio editions: Amazon KDP Virtual Voice (AI, US, invite/beta), Google Play Books auto-narrated audiobooks (English, Spanish, French, German, Hindi, Brazilian Portuguese; free "for a limited time"), and Voices by INaudio (formerly Findaway Voices) which distributes AI-narrated audio with disclosure to many retailers. ACX/Audible proper still requires human narration (or the narrator's own Voice Replica). Retail buyers and subscription services pay; distributors pass royalties monthly.

payout.notes: Most audio royalties paid 30-60 days after month end.

legality.notes: Legal across the set; requires audio rights to the text.

availability.notes: Virtual Voice US-only/invite; ACX only for US/UK/CA/IE rights holders; Google Play and INaudio cover far more countries.

risks: Low audio demand for weak books
strategies.evidence: Audible lists 'Virtual Voice' titles publicly; Google Play has offered free auto-narration to publishers since 2020.

tools: Google Play Books auto-narration (free for a limited time)
skills: owning audio rights to an existing ebook

unitEconomics.notes: Retailers and distributors keep most of list: author typically receives ~40-52% depending on channel (Google Play ~52%, INaudio 80% of retailer net). Median $12 sale nets ~$5 (estimate). Google Play 52% share and free auto-narration (limited time) verified on Google's page.

breakEven.notes: No startup cash or fixed cost, so break-even = first payout received. Requires an existing ebook; AI narration replaces the $2,000-$5,000 cost of human narration.

marketConditions.notes: Authors who already sell ebooks benefit most, since the audio edition rides on existing demand. AI narration made audio editions nearly free in 2024-2026, so many more titles are entering audio and prices are softening; Audible/ACX still mostly requires human narration. Audio rarely sells a book with no existing audience.

strategies.name: Collect songwriter publishing royalties (PRO registration, The MLC, Songtrust, live-performance reporting)
strategies.summary: Register your compositions with a performing-rights organization, The MLC and/or a publishing administrator to collect performance and mechanical royalties that distributors do not pay.
strategies.howItWorks: Streaming distributors pay only master royalties; the composition side (performance and mechanical) is collected by PROs (ASCAP/BMI/PRS/SOCAN etc.), The MLC for US streaming mechanicals, or an admin like Songtrust worldwide. You register songs, splits and ISWCs, and report live and livestreamed setlists through PRO online performance-reporting programs. Money that would otherwise go unclaimed flows to you.
platforms: ASCAP / BMI / PRS for Music / local PRO

payout.minimumPayout: PRS: £30 (UK) / £60 (international); The MLC pays monthly; others vary by society
payout.notes: Verified: The MLC is free and distributes monthly; Songtrust charges a one-time $100 fee plus 15% of performance / 20% of mechanical royalties. ASCAP is free to join as a writer, and ASCAP OnStage pays royalties for live sets at ASCAP-licensed venues, with claims due one quarter after the performance quarter (classical/recital and non-licensable events are excluded); payment by direct deposit. PRS for Music charges a one-off £100 joining fee (£30 under 25; MCPS is a separate £100), pays once earnings exceed £30 UK / £60 international, and lets members register live performances in the dashboard. BMI fees and BMI Live rules could not be fetched (bmi.com returned 403); livestream eligibility under OnStage is not stated.

legality.notes: Collective rights management is legal in all reference countries; most have a national CMO, though local societies vary in efficiency.
complianceRequirements: PRS has a £100 joining fee; ASCAP and The MLC are free

availability.notes: Every reference country has access to at least one PRO (local or foreign); The MLC accepts anyone owed US mechanicals. Payout is direct deposit to bank.

automationPlan: Script bulk song registration data (titles, ISRC/ISWC, splits)
Scheduled matching checks of unclaimed works
strategies.evidence: The MLC distributes monthly; ASCAP says it is free to join as a writer and pays OnStage live-performance royalties; PRS paid out £1.07bn in 2025, with nearly 7,000 members paid for the first time.

tools: PRO member portal (ASCAP/BMI free; PRS GBP 100)

unitEconomics.notes: Composition royalties are roughly $0.0003-0.0008 per stream combined (estimate); figures assume direct PRO/MLC registration (Songtrust would take 15-20%).

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost. No cash if you choose free PROs (PRS charges GBP 100). Royalties lag 6-12 months behind plays.

marketConditions.notes: This only captures money your music already earns; it pays meaningfully only for catalogues with hundreds of thousands of streams or regular live performances. US mechanical rates are rising under Phonorecords IV, but AI-generated tracks dilute streaming pools. Failure modes: tiny catalogues earning cents, mis-registered splits.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: No pricing; maximise by registering every song in every relevant society and reporting every live set.
profitPath: Month 0: join a PRO and The MLC, register catalogue (cost $0)
Month 1-6: report live sets and fix registrations; no payments yet
Month 6-9: first statements, often under $10
Month 9-12: steady small monthly MLC and quarterly PRO payments

strategies.name: License your unused video/footage archive as AI training data
strategies.summary: Sell rights to raw or unpublished video you own to AI companies through data brokers like Troveo, who pay per minute.
strategies.howItWorks: AI video model labs buy licensed footage; brokers (Troveo, Calliope Networks) aggregate creator archives and pay roughly $1-$4 per minute depending on quality and format. You must own the footage and have releases for identifiable people. An agent can inventory and tag archives, strip unwanted segments, prepare metadata and handle uploads. One-off or recurring payments as new footage is added.

payout.frequency: per licensing deal; no fixed schedule
payout.notes: Troveo pays only after your content is licensed, the AI client is invoiced and pays; non-US licensors submit W-8BEN. Troveo does not publish per-minute rates; the ~$1-$4/minute range comes from press reports.

legality.notes: Legal if you own copyright and have releases; check that footage doesn't include others' likenesses or copyrighted music.
complianceRequirements: privacy law for people in footage

availability.notes: Troveo pays international licensors via Tipalti bank transfer; exact country list not published.

automationPlan: Agent catalogs archive and computes minutes by category
risks: Prices may fall as supply grows
strategies.evidence: Troveo's content-owner page states $50M+ paid to creators globally; Bloomberg (Jan 2025) reported YouTubers selling unused footage to AI firms.

unitEconomics.notes: Press reports cite ~$1-$4 per minute paid to creators; brokers do not publish rates; prices shown are net to creator (estimate). Troveo's payout article confirms payment only when footage is licensed, with no fixed schedule and no published rate.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). No costs; payment arrives only after a lab licenses the footage.

marketConditions.notes: People with large archives of owned, release-cleared footage (B-roll, drone, nature) are paid; Troveo reports $50M+ paid. Supply is rising and synthetic data may reduce prices. Failure mode: no archive, or content rejected over releases/quality.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Not price-set; prioritise high-value formats (4K, drone, unusual locations) and negotiate non-exclusive licences.
profitPath: Month 0: inventory archive (cost $0)
Month 1-2: submit; $0
Month 3-6: first licence payment; $50-$500 one-off
Month 6-12: add new footage; $30 median average

strategies.name: Credit card sign-up bonuses and rewards optimisation
strategies.summary: Earn welcome bonuses (cash or points) by meeting minimum-spend on new credit cards using normal expenses, paid off in full monthly.
strategies.howItWorks: Offers are country-specific. Example checked Nov 2026: the US Capital One Venture card gives 75,000 miles (about $750 in travel) after $4,000 of purchases in the first 3 months, with a $95 annual fee. UK, Canadian and Australian issuers offer smaller points packages. You route only existing spending through the card and pay the full statement each month, so there is no interest. Points/cashback are redeemed as statement credit, bank transfer or travel. Issuers pay because interchange fees and future revolving balances from the average customer fund it.
platforms: US issuers (Chase, Amex, Capital One, Citi)

payout.notes: Bonus usually posts 1-2 statement cycles after meeting minimum spend. Minimum spend (e.g. $4,000 in 3 months) must come from normal expenses, so capitalRequiredUsd is 0 only if you already spend that much.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; in the US cash rewards from spending are generally treated as rebates (not income), bank-account-style bonuses may be taxable.

availability.notes: Country-specific: lucrative bonuses are concentrated in the US, Canada, UK and Australia; elsewhere card rewards are small. Requires a credit file, so new arrivals and thin-file applicants are usually declined. Offers change frequently; check issuer pages.

automationPlan: Track spend progress and deadlines automatically via bank export/APIs
Monitor public offer trackers for elevated bonuses
fullCycle: Choose offer matched to normal spend
Hit minimum spend with regular expenses
risks: Interest and debt if balance not paid
Credit score dips from hard pulls
strategies.evidence: Capital One's official Venture page (Nov 2026) lists 75,000 bonus miles for $4,000 spend in 3 months; Doctor of Credit tracks current US offers.

tools: Doctor of Credit / issuer comparison pages (free)
skills: credit discipline: pay every statement in full
tracking minimum-spend windows and issuer rules (e.g. 5/24)

unitEconomics.notes: Cash-equivalent value of typical welcome offers ($200 cash to 60-75k points valued ~1c); cost = average annual fee not waived (estimate).

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). No fixed cost if you choose no-fee or first-year-waived cards; bonus posts 1-2 statement cycles after minimum spend.

marketConditions.notes: Issuers keep paying large bonuses in US/UK/CA/AU, but 2025-2026 rules (once-per-lifetime language, 5/24, family restrictions) keep tightening. Winners already have organic spend of $1,500+/month and perfect repayment habits. One month of carried balance at 20-30% APR wipes out the bonus; outside the four core markets bonuses are small or absent.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Not priced by you: only apply for cards whose minimum spend you can meet from normal expenses, ranking by bonus value minus annual fee.
profitPath: Month 0: check credit report, choose one no-fee or fee-waived card (cost $0)
Month 1-3: meet minimum spend with normal bills, pay in full
Month 3-6: first bonus posts (expected $200-$600); apply for the next card after 3-6 months
Month 6-12: 2-3 bonuses a year, about $50-$100/month averaged; downgrade fee cards before renewal

strategies.name: Paid browser extensions with ExtensionPay/Stripe
strategies.summary: Build Chrome/Firefox/Edge extensions with a freemium or subscription model and charge users via ExtensionPay or your own Stripe/merchant-of-record checkout.

ExtensionPay adds a hosted payment/login flow on top of your Stripe account (5% per transaction + Stripe fees); alternatives are Lemon Squeezy/Paddle/Polar license keys. Payers are end users who want the premium features.

methods: or merchant of record (Lemon Squeezy/Paddle) -> bank/PayPal

legality.notes: Selling software is legal everywhere in the reference set.
complianceRequirements: Chrome Web Store developer program policies (no data harvesting)

Automated store publishing via Chrome Web Store API
