strategies.name: Sell new translations/annotated editions of public-domain works
strategies.summary: Create genuinely new, copyrightable editions (translations, annotations, illustrated or modernized versions) of public-domain texts and sell them.
strategies.howItWorks: You take public-domain texts (e.g. from Project Gutenberg), strip the Project Gutenberg name and license, and add original value: a new translation, notes, study guides, audio narration. Readers pay for the added value. KDP requires PD books to be differentiated and pays 35% royalty for PD content.

payout.notes: If you keep the Project Gutenberg name/trademark and charge a fee, the PG license requires a 20% royalty on gross profits (due within 60 days of each tax-return date); stripping all PG references and the license avoids this.

legality.notes: Copyright terms vary by country (life+50/70); verify PD status per country.

availability.notes: KDP pays in most countries.

strategies.evidence: Project Gutenberg's official license (sections 1.C and 1.E.8 and the trademark section) permits free reuse of US public-domain texts once all PG references are removed.

skills: editing AI-assisted translations to publishable quality

unitEconomics.notes: Ebooks $2.99-$6.99; KDP pays only 35% for primarily public-domain content and up to 70% for differentiated works (blended ~50%); paperbacks higher price but print cost. Hours = creation time spread over expected sales (estimate).

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). No fixed cost.

marketConditions.notes: AI made translation and annotation cheap, so KDP is flooded with public-domain editions and Amazon tightened AI-content disclosure and daily title limits in 2023-2025. Winners pick under-served languages or niches (classics for learners, bilingual editions) with real scholarly value. Most editions sell a handful of copies.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Launch at $0.99-$2.99 to collect reviews, then raise to $4.99+ for annotated or bilingual editions and add paperback.
profitPath: Month 0: produce one high-quality annotated or translated edition (cost $0)
Month 1-3: first sales; expected $5-$20/month
Month 3-6: publish 3-5 more in the same niche, build a series
Month 6-12: $20-$100/month from a catalogue of 10+ titles

strategies.name: Free AI-powered micro-tools website monetized by display ads and freemium
strategies.summary: A site of single-purpose AI tools (e.g. 'rewrite email in formal tone', 'generate alt text', 'CSV to chart') that captures search traffic and earns from ads and premium usage.
strategies.howItWorks: Each tool page targets a search query with real utility (not thin content). LLM APIs do the work; free usage is rate-limited, and a cheap subscription unlocks more. Revenue from display ads (AdSense, later Ezoic/Mediavine-type networks) and Stripe subscriptions. Coding agents can build new tools quickly from a template and monitor which pages rank.

payout.notes: API costs must stay below ad + subscription revenue per user.

legality.notes: Legal; follow AdSense policies (no auto-generated thin pages, no invalid traffic) and Google spam policies on scaled content.

availability.notes: AdSense pays in nearly all reference countries; Stripe for subscriptions where supported, else Paddle/Lemon Squeezy.

automationPlan: Coding agent generates tool pages from template
Automated keyword research and rank tracking
risks: Google updates against scaled AI content
AI answers in search reduce clicks
Hosting must be on a commercial plan: Vercel's free Hobby tier forbids ads/AdSense; use Vercel Pro, Cloudflare Pages or a VPS
strategies.evidence: Multiple indie AI tool sites publicly report ad + subscription revenue; AdSense payment thresholds documented by Google.

tools: Cloudflare Pages free hosting (Vercel's free Hobby tier forbids ads)

strategies.name: Niche blog / programmatic SEO site with display ads (AdSense -> Ezoic/Journey/Raptive)
strategies.summary: Publish genuinely useful pages that rank in search, monetized with display ads via AdSense, then Ezoic, Mediavine or Raptive as traffic grows.
strategies.howItWorks: You build a site on a cheap domain/host, generating templated-but-valuable pages from real datasets (programmatic SEO) and editorial articles with AI assistance. Visitors from Google/Bing see ads; AdSense pays from day one of approval, and at scale you move to premium networks (Ezoic: no pageview minimum; Journey by Mediavine: 1,000 Tier-1 sessions in 30 days; full Mediavine: $5,000+ annual ad revenue; Raptive: 25k monthly pageviews with 50%+ tier-1 traffic below 100k). Google's scaled-content-abuse policy penalizes mass low-value AI pages, so each page needs unique data or utility.

payout.notes: AdSense pays the 21st-26th of the month once the balance meets the threshold (official). Premium-network terms (Mediavine Net-65, Raptive Net-45) not re-verified.

legality.notes: Legal across the set; privacy/cookie consent law (GDPR/CCPA) required for EU/UK/CA traffic.

availability.notes: AdSense available in almost all reference countries; premium networks accept international publishers but want US/UK traffic.

automationPlan: Dataset ingestion + page templates generated by script
risks: Google core/spam updates can wipe traffic
strategies.evidence: Raptive and Mediavine pay thousands of independent publishers; SEJ reported Raptive's cut to 25k views to admit smaller sites.

tools: static hosting free tier (Cloudflare Pages/Netlify) or shared host
skills: basic HTML or static-site generator (AI coding agent can help)

strategies.name: Pinterest affiliate pinning
strategies.summary: Create original pins (images/video) that link to affiliate products or affiliate blog posts in visual niches.
strategies.howItWorks: Pinterest is a search engine for planning (home decor, recipes, crafts, fashion). You design original pins with keyword-rich titles that link either directly to affiliate products (allowed with disclosure) or to your own blog posts containing affiliate links, which is safer and diversifies. Pins have long shelf lives, so a consistent library compounds traffic. Payers are the merchants/networks behind the links (Amazon, LTK, Awin, etc.).

payout.notes: Pinterest itself does not pay; payout comes from the affiliate program.

You open an account, deposit or transfer the qualifying amount, hold it for the required period (often 30-365 days), then sell the free shares and withdraw to your bank. The broker pays to acquire assets under management. Rewards are usually securities; some need capital at market risk.

link conversion through the EarnKaro app/extension

strategies.name: Amazon KDP ebooks, paperbacks and low-content books
strategies.summary: Self-publish ebooks and print-on-demand books (incl. journals, planners, puzzle books) on Amazon for royalties.
strategies.howItWorks: You write or compile books (nonfiction guides, fiction, workbooks, puzzle/activity books) and upload to KDP; Amazon prints on demand and pays 35-70% ebook royalties, ~60% minus print cost on paperbacks listed at $9.99+ (50% below that), plus Kindle Unlimited page reads. Amazon requires you to disclose AI-generated text, images or translations (AI-assisted editing need not be disclosed) and caps new titles at 3 per day per account. Low-content books have little moat, so niche research and quality covers matter.

payout.minimumPayout: $0 for EFT (usually no minimum); $100 for wire/check on Amazon.com
payout.notes: Royalties paid ~60 days after the end of the month of sale (90 days for Expanded Distribution). AI disclosure rule is on KDP's content guidelines; the 3-titles/day cap was confirmed by KDP to the Authors Guild (2023) but is not on a KDP help page.

legality.notes: Legal across the set; must own rights to text and images.

availability.notes: KDP accepts publishers worldwide; EFT supported to many countries, others paid by wire/check.

automationPlan: Programmatic interior generation (puzzles, planners) and cover templates
manualSteps: Manual title upload in KDP UI (no public upload API)
strategies.evidence: Amazon publishes a monthly KDP Select Global Fund (tens of millions USD per month) paid to KU authors; Authors Guild documented the AI policy and 3/day limit.

tools: Kindle Create / Atticus alternative free tools
Publisher Rocket optional (skip for zero capital)
skills: writing or compiling a useful book

unitEconomics.notes: Paperback royalty is 60% of list minus print cost (~$3-$4 for a 120-150 page book) so Amazon keeps ~40%; a $9.99 paperback nets ~$2. Ebooks at $2.99-$9.99 pay 70% minus delivery (estimate from KDP royalty pages). Verified Nov 2026: paperback 60% royalty applies only at list prices of $9.99+ on Amazon.com (lower prices earn 50%); KDP example: $15 x 0.60 - $5.00 print cost = $4.00. Ebook 70% option deducts ~$0.06 average delivery. KU per-page (KENP) rate is not published on the KDP page (Sept 2026 KDP Select author earnings: $69.3M), so any per-page figure is estimated.

breakEven.notes: No startup cash or fixed cost, so break-even = first payout received. First sales typically within 1-3 months of publishing if keyword research is sound; EFT has no minimum in most marketplaces.

marketConditions.notes: Earners run catalogs of 20+ well-researched titles in a niche, or write series fiction for Kindle Unlimited. AI caused a flood of low-quality books, prompting Amazon's AI disclosure rule and 3-titles-per-day cap; low-content books (journals, puzzles) are near-commodity. Most single books sell a few copies a month.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Launch ebooks at $2.99-$4.99 and paperbacks at the lowest price that still nets $2+; raise prices once reviews accumulate and bundle series boxsets later.

strategies.name: Wide ebook distribution via Draft2Digital / PublishDrive (Apple, Kobo, Everand, libraries)
strategies.summary: Publish the same ebook to every non-Amazon store plus subscription and library channels through one aggregator, instead of Amazon-exclusive KDP Select.
strategies.howItWorks: You upload a finished, human-authored ebook once to an aggregator that ships it to Apple Books, Kobo (incl. Kobo Plus), Barnes & Noble, Everand, Tolino and library platforms (OverDrive, Hoopla, cloudLibrary, BorrowBox). Readers and libraries pay the stores; the aggregator forwards royalties monthly. Draft2Digital keeps about 10% of the retail price and charges new accounts a one-time $20 activation fee; PublishDrive charges a subscription instead and passes 100% of royalties (one ebook to Apple, B&N and Kobo is free). Libraries are a distinct payer (licences or pay-per-checkout).

payout.notes: D2D FAQ: payments go out monthly around the 15th once the threshold is met; stores pay D2D 30-60 days after month end. D2D fees: one-time non-refundable $20 activation fee for new accounts, plus $12/year maintenance for accounts earning under $100/year in sales (waived the first year; accounts with no titles in distribution exempt). PayPal fee 2.5% (cap $25 non-US) not rechecked.

legality.notes: Writing and selling original text is legal in all reference countries; royalties are taxable.
complianceRequirements: D2D rejects fully AI-generated content and AI nonfiction from non-credentialled authors

availability.notes: Payoneer and direct deposit cover all 50 reference countries; store reach varies by country.

Auto-sync price promos across stores via aggregator
Pull monthly sales reports into a dashboard

strategies.name: Pitch-deck design and startup financial models
strategies.summary: Productized pitch decks (story + design) and 3-statement/SaaS financial models for founders raising money.
strategies.howItWorks: Founders pay to look credible to investors. You sell fixed packages: deck rewrite + redesign (10-20 slides), and a driver-based financial model in Google Sheets/Excel. LLMs draft the narrative, market-size math and slide copy; templates and AI image tools speed design; a model template covers most SaaS/marketplace cases. You review numbers with the founder; projections are the founder's assumptions, not advice.

Fiverr: 20% seller fee and 14-day clearance (7 days for Top Rated) are widely reported but Fiverr's help center blocked fetch, so not confirmed from the official page.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; taxable. Do not give investment or securities advice or help solicit investors; label projections as client assumptions.

slide template library with brand-color auto-apply

strategies.name: Curated coupon and deal aggregator site

You only list codes merchants actually released; paying publishers are merchants via networks. Generic coupon SEO is heavily contested and Google penalises third-party coupon sections on unrelated sites.

manualSteps: Editorial check that deals are real
risks: Merchants cancel commissions for coupon sites

skills: light scripting for feeds (AI coding agents help)
accounts: Skimlinks or Sovrn Commerce publisher account

Pay is per word (Gengo's standard tier is a few cents per word) and payouts go to PayPal or Payoneer on a fixed schedule. Unbabel pays for post-editing machine translation per task. AI can pre-translate, but the platforms require human quality; using raw machine output is detectable and leads to removal. For bilingual people this is one of the most reliable small online incomes.

availability.notes: Global; payout via PayPal/Payoneer covers nearly every reference country.

Script alerts when jobs in your language pair appear (queues empty fast).
risks: Tests are hard to pass for popular pairs
Rates have fallen with machine translation

tools: machine-translation draft tools where allowed (free tier)

strategies.name: Rent a spare room on Airbnb (PHYSICAL)

availability.notes: Airbnb operates in nearly all reference countries.

equipment: spare room or property you are allowed to sublet

accounts: Stripe or Wise for direct invoices

Media kit and rate card auto-updated from stats

strategies.name: Niche 'AI employee' chatbot/voice agent sold per seat to a vertical
strategies.summary: Build a no-code AI agent (Voiceflow/Botpress) for one vertical (e.g. dental clinics, property managers) and sell it as a monthly subscription.
strategies.howItWorks: You pick a vertical with repetitive inbound questions or bookings, build an agent connected to their calendar/CRM/FAQ, and resell it as a done-for-you monthly service. Clients pay a setup fee plus per-seat or per-location monthly. Botpress has a formal partner program for agencies; Voiceflow targets agencies. Once one template works, cloning it for new clients is largely automated; sales remains human.

payout.notes: Common pricing $99-$500/month per client plus setup.

legality.notes: Legal; respect call-recording/consent and AI-disclosure rules (e.g. EU AI Act transparency, US state bot-disclosure laws, TCPA for outbound calls).

availability.notes: Tooling available globally; billing via Stripe or Wise/Payoneer invoices.

automationPlan: Template agent cloned per client via API
Agent ingests client docs into knowledge base
risks: Churn when vertical SaaS adds native AI
strategies.evidence: Botpress runs an official partner program for agencies selling AI agents as a service; many agencies publicly sell AI receptionists per month.

tools: Botpress (free tier to start; Plus $150/mo billed annually once clients pay for it) or Voiceflow (usage-based)

unitEconomics.notes: Agencies commonly charge $99-$500/month per location plus setup; cost = LLM/voice usage per client (estimate); fee = card processing.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). One client covers platform fees; setup fees often cover the startup cash. Fixed cost assumes the free/usage-based builder tier plus voice/LLM floor; upgrading to Botpress Plus adds ~$150/mo (estimated as a pass-through to clients).

marketConditions.notes: The 'AI automation agency' wave of 2024-2026 made this crowded; winners specialise in one vertical (dental, HVAC, real estate) and own a referral channel. Vertical SaaS vendors increasingly bundle native AI receptionists, pressuring prices. Failure mode: no sales skills, or churn after a hallucination incident. Median net at month 12 set to $80 to match the 20% profit likelihood.

Month 3-6: 2-3 paying clients; $250-$750/month
Month 6-12: templated onboarding, 4-10 clients; $300 median, $2,000+ top quartile

strategies.name: SaaS recurring-commission affiliate via tutorials and YouTube
strategies.summary: Teach people to use hosting, dev tools or AI tools and earn recurring or high one-time commissions on signups.
strategies.howItWorks: Create step-by-step tutorials (blog + YouTube + GitHub templates) that solve a concrete problem with a tool, e.g. 'deploy X on a VPS' or 'automate Y with an AI tool'. Viewers who sign up through your link generate commissions. Official 2026 terms: Kit (ConvertKit) pays 50% of a referral's first 12 months, plus 10% lifetime recurring once you refer 10 paying customers in a year; ElevenLabs pays up to 22% for 12 months; Semrush pays one-time $50-$300 per sale (up to $450 at higher tiers) plus $10 per trial with a 120-day cookie; Hostinger starts at 40% per sale. Notion's program (20% of first-year revenue) is currently not accepting new affiliates. Recurring revenue compounds as tutorials keep ranking.

payout.minimumPayout: Commonly $5-$50 depending on program (PartnerStack $5, e.g. Kit; Impact $10, e.g. Semrush)
payout.notes: Programs hold commissions for refunds before paying (Kit: 31-day hold, withdrawable from $5 around the 13th of each month via PartnerStack: Stripe, PayPal or direct deposit by region).

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; follow each program's rules.

availability.notes: Most SaaS programs accept affiliates worldwide and pay via PayPal/Stripe; a few exclude sanctioned countries.

automationPlan: AI drafts tutorial scripts and code samples; agent verifies the code runs
Auto-generate blog post from video transcript
Link management with UTM + per-program dashboards
Monitor tool pricing changes and update content
manualSteps: Recording or voicing videos (or AI voice with disclosure)
risks: Programs cut rates or end recurring terms
Trust damage if you shill weak tools
strategies.evidence: Official affiliate pages (Nov 2026): Kit 50% for 12 months + 10% lifetime after 10 referrals/year, 90-day cookie; ElevenLabs up to 22% for 12 months; Semrush $50-$300 per sale + $10 per trial, 120-day cookie, hosted on Impact; Hostinger at least 40% per sale. Notion is closed to new affiliates, a reminder that programs change.

tools: free trials of the tools you teach
AI script and editing helpers (free tiers)

unitEconomics.notes: Official 2026 terms: Semrush $50-300 per sale, Kit 50% of first 12 months, Hostinger 40%+ per sale; median assumes a ~$60 average first-year commission. Fee is PayPal payout (~2%).

marketConditions.notes: Winners are practitioners whose tutorials solve a concrete job and keep ranking on YouTube and Google for years. AI makes scripting and editing cheap, but AI search answers absorb some how-to traffic and programs like Notion's have closed to new affiliates. Failure mode: generic 'top 10 AI tools' content with no conversions.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Promote tools whose recurring commission covers 12+ months; once a tutorial converts, ask the vendor's partner manager for a higher tier or a custom discount code for your audience.
profitPath: Month 0: pick 3-5 tools you actually use, join their programs, publish 4 tutorials (cost $0)
Month 1-2: 2 tutorials/week with GitHub templates; expect $0-30
Month 3-6: update winners, add comparison and migration guides; expect $30-200/month
Month 6-12: recurring commissions stack; median ~$80/month, top channels $1k+

strategies.name: Spreadsheet templates and calculators (Excel / Google Sheets)
strategies.summary: Sell budget trackers, business dashboards, invoicing and planning spreadsheets as instant downloads.

Buyers pay for a ready-to-use tool rather than building it. Google Sheets copy links make delivery trivial. Avoid presenting outputs as personalized financial advice.

payout.minimumPayout: Per platform: Payhip $0 (instant), Etsy $0 weekly, Gumroad $100
payout.notes: Same as host platform.

tools: LLM chat for formulas and Apps Script

AI makes building far faster but also lets buyers generate simple sheets in Gemini/Copilot, so simple trackers are commoditised. Support load from non-technical buyers is a hidden cost.

strategies.name: Upload designs to POD marketplaces: Redbubble, TeePublic, Amazon Merch on Demand
strategies.summary: Upload artwork once; the marketplace handles traffic, production, shipping and customer service and pays you a royalty.
strategies.howItWorks: Unlike own-shop POD, you never touch orders or costs: Redbubble, TeePublic and Amazon Merch on Demand list your design on products in their own storefronts. You earn a margin/royalty per sale (Redbubble: artist margin minus tier-based platform/excess-markup fees, capped at $150 per period, Pro tier exempt; Amazon Merch: third-party reports say royalties moved to traffic-based tiers on June 1, 2026, with the default tier paying ~50% of the old royalty). Amazon Merch requires application approval and has upload tiers.

methods: TeePublic: PayPal or Payoneer only (Stripe used for identity verification)
payout.minimumPayout: Redbubble $10/£10/€10 (lowered from $20 on July 1, 2026); TeePublic: no minimum stated in help center (Payoneer minimum unverified); Amazon Merch: monthly deposit
payout.notes: Redbubble processes at the start of each month for orders shipped the previous month, landing by the 15th; TeePublic pays on the 15th for the previous calendar month's sales; Amazon Merch timing (~30 days after month end) not verified from an official page (Merch resources are login-only).

legality.notes: Legal; all physical production/shipping handled by platform, nothing physical for the seller.

availability.notes: Redbubble and TeePublic pay globally via PayPal/Payoneer; Amazon Merch accepts applicants from many countries but approval is selective.

automationPlan: AI drafts designs, titles and tags
Scripted trend/niche research from public data

tools: Redbubble / TeePublic / Amazon Merch on Demand (free)
accounts: Redbubble, TeePublic and (by application) Amazon Merch accounts

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost on the free tiers, so break-even is the first sale; months shown are the typical ramp to the first sale.

marketConditions.notes: Uploaders with thousands of designs or recognised niches still earn; Redbubble/TeePublic traffic has been declining and Redbubble's tiered account fees cut small-shop earnings. Amazon Merch's 2026 move to traffic-based royalty tiers roughly halved default royalties per third-party reports. AI design floods mean single designs rarely sell.

strategies.name: License data feeds/APIs built from lawfully licensed public data
strategies.summary: Clean, normalize and enrich open government/open-licensed data and sell API access or bulk feeds by subscription.
strategies.howItWorks: You pick open datasets with commercial-reuse licenses (government open data under OGL/CC-BY, company registries, weather, transit, sanctions lists) and turn them into a reliable, documented API or periodic CSV/Parquet feed. Developers and analysts pay for convenience, freshness and uptime. List on RapidAPI (PayPal payouts after card settlement, ~20-25% fee) or sell directly with Stripe-metered billing.

fullCycle: List on RapidAPI or own site

Winners own a niche dataset that is painful to normalise (regulatory filings, local registries). Most APIs get few or no paying subscribers.

strategies.name: Music streaming royalties via DistroKid / TuneCore
strategies.summary: Release original tracks (incl. AI-assisted production) to Spotify, Apple Music, YouTube Music and others for streaming royalties.
strategies.howItWorks: You produce tracks (ambient, lo-fi, focus, library-style music) and release via a distributor that delivers to DSPs and collects royalties. Spotify only pays on tracks with 1,000+ streams/12 months, filters spam uploads and bans unauthorized voice clones; Deezer tags fully AI tracks and excludes them from recommendations. DistroKid accepts AI-assisted music if you own the rights and it is not mass-generated spam. Real listening (playlists, sync, content creators) is what pays.

payout.notes: Stores report 2-3 months after streams occur.

legality.notes: Legal across the set; rights to samples/vocals required.
complianceRequirements: Own all rights; no voice clones of real artists
AI disclosure where DSP requests (DDEX AI credits)

availability.notes: DistroKid/TuneCore serve artists worldwide.

strategies.evidence: TechCrunch reported Spotify's Sept 2025 AI policy (labels, spam filter); millions of independent artists are paid by DistroKid.

tools: AI-assisted production tools with commercial rights

unitEconomics.notes: Blended DSP payout to rights holders is roughly $2-$5 per 1,000 streams on Spotify and higher on Apple/Amazon; DistroKid's annual plan keeps 0% (estimate; Spotify pays nothing on tracks under 1,000 streams/12 months).

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = $25/yr plan amortised to ~$2/month; break-even needs ~1,000 paid streams/month on tracks above Spotify's 1,000-stream threshold. Stores report 2-3 months late. Recovery assumes ~$3/month net at month 6.

marketConditions.notes: Over 100,000 tracks are uploaded daily, so editorial and algorithmic playlist placement decides everything. Spotify's 2025 AI/spam policy and Deezer's AI tagging target mass-generated tracks, and the 1,000-stream minimum zeroes out most catalog. Earners combine streaming with sync licensing and creator-music libraries.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Streaming rates are fixed by DSPs; use singles every 4-6 weeks to feed algorithms and route listeners to higher-margin channels (Bandcamp, sync, licensing).
profitPath: Month 0: produce 3-5 tracks, set up distributor (cost $25)
Month 1-3: release singles, pitch playlists, expected $0-$5
Month 4-6: first royalties arrive after 2-3 month lag
Month 6-12: keep a single every 4-6 weeks; typical result $1-$20/month

strategies.name: Paid user-research interviews and focus groups (Respondent, User Interviews, dscout)
strategies.summary: Get paid $30–$200+ for 30–60 minute remote interviews with product teams and researchers who need people matching a profile.
strategies.howItWorks: Companies recruit interviewees through platforms like Respondent and User Interviews. You fill a profile, apply to studies that match, and if selected join a video call or complete a diary study. Pay is set per study (Respondent: most sessions $50–$250 depending on length and seniority, senior B2B roles $400+). Payment is sent through Tremendous (PayPal, bank or gift card) after the session is verified. Selection is competitive, so apply to many studies; professionals with specific job titles are picked far more often.

payout.notes: Respondent (official participant page): paid via Tremendous, usually within 5–7 business days of the session; 'you'll never be asked to pay to participate'. User Interviews and dscout payout terms not re-checked.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere. Do not misrepresent your profile; platforms verify LinkedIn and ban fraud.

availability.notes: Respondent says its panel covers 150+ countries but highlights US, Canada, Australia, UK, Germany and France; many studies are restricted to specific regions.

automationPlan: Automate study discovery: a script that checks new studies and drafts screener answers from your saved profile (you submit).
Automate calendar booking and payout logging.
risks: Low selection rate for generic profiles
No-shows or unverified sessions are unpaid
strategies.evidence: User Interviews states participants have earned $60 million; Respondent publishes typical session pay of $50–$250 (senior B2B $400+) and focus groups of $75–$200 online.

unitEconomics.notes: Respondent lists most sessions at $50-250 (senior B2B $400+); 1.5 hours includes applying to screeners. Researchers pay the platform fee.

breakEven.notes: No fixed costs, so every paid unit is profit; break-even equals the time to the first payout. Selection rate is low for generic profiles, so the first session can take 1-3 months.

People with in-demand job titles (IT buyers, engineers, clinicians, finance) are picked often; generic consumer profiles are rarely selected. profitLikelihoodPercent here is the chance of receiving any real net-positive payout within 12 months (typical income is under $100/month), calibrated to the catalog's survey-panel anchor.

Month 1-2: apply to 20+ screeners; first $50-100 session
Month 3-6: 1-3 sessions/month: $50-250
Month 6-12: steady $60-450/month for matching professionals

strategies.name: Machine-translation post-editing (MTPE) and localization
strategies.summary: Post-edit machine/LLM translations into your native language for websites, apps, e-commerce listings and documents.
strategies.howItWorks: Businesses localizing content pay for fluent human review of machine output. You run MT/LLM, then edit for accuracy, tone and terminology. Work comes via Smartcat marketplace, Upwork, Fiverr and agencies. Native speakers of mid-demand languages have an edge.

legality.notes: Ordinary translation is legal everywhere. Certified/sworn/court translation requires a license in many countries; exclude it.
complianceRequirements: disclose MT use when client requires

availability.notes: Smartcat, Upwork and Fiverr pay out globally via Payoneer/PayPal/bank; demand depends on language pair.

automationPlan: QA checks (numbers, tags, terms) by script
strategies.evidence: Smartcat's marketplace advertises 500K+ linguists, lets buyers add a human post-editing review to AI output, and lets freelancers set their own per-word rates; MTPE is a standard industry service.

skills: native-level target language and strong source language

PayPal or Payoneer linked to a bank account

Fiverr (20%) and Upwork (variable 0-15% since 2025) fee figures are estimated: their official fee pages were bot-blocked when checked in Nov 2026.

strategies.name: Niche 'best X' directory with paid/featured listings

AI writes listing summaries and category pages
Self-serve Stripe checkout for featured slots

skills: a sellable skill (writing, design, dev, data entry, marketing)

conversion tracking consent (cookie banners in EU/UK)

AI ad copy and creative variants

Wise Business or Stripe account for invoicing (KYC)

Month 3-6: case study; 2-3 clients
Month 6-12: 3-8 clients on retainers

AI support chatbot and knowledge base for common issues

strategies.summary: Audit websites/apps/PDFs against WCAG 2.1/2.2 AA, deliver prioritized reports and fix code or documents.

Scanners find part of the issues; you add keyboard/screen-reader testing, write the report with LLM help, and fix code or tag PDFs. Monitoring retainers follow.

risks: automated tools find only part of issues, so skill matters

DOJ Title II rule (WCAG 2.1 AA): compliance dates extended by an April 20, 2026 interim final rule to April 26, 2027 (pop. 50k+) and April 26, 2028 (smaller). EU Accessibility Act covers e-commerce.

Wise Business or Stripe account for invoicing (KYC)

Credentials (e.g. IAAP CPACC/WAS) help win buyers; without them first sales are slow.

Automated SVN deploy to WordPress.org via GitHub Actions
Automated license/update delivery via Freemius SDK

strategies.name: Patent drawings and technical illustration
strategies.summary: Produce USPTO/EPO-compliant patent drawings and exploded/technical illustrations for patent attorneys, inventors and manuals.
strategies.howItWorks: Patent firms and inventors need black-and-white line drawings meeting strict office rules. You turn CAD exports, photos or sketches into compliant vector figures; scripts handle numbering and sheet layout, you ensure accuracy. Firms pay per sheet and repeat. Claim drafting is regulated legal work; you only illustrate.

payout.notes: Upwork: variable 0-15% freelancer service fee set per contract since May 2025 (pre-May-2025 contracts 10%), per Upwork's SEC 10-Q; Upwork help pages block automated fetch. Fiverr: 20% seller fee and 14-day clearance (7 days for Top Rated) are widely reported but Fiverr's help center blocked fetch, so not confirmed from the official page.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; taxable. Patent prosecution and claim drafting are reserved to registered practitioners in many countries; drawings by draftspersons are commonly outsourced.

availability.notes: Upwork/Fiverr pay out in nearly all reference countries via Payoneer/bank.

automationPlan: auto reference-numeral placement and figure labels
fullCycle: Make 3 sample sheets per office spec
strategies.evidence: USPTO MPEP 608 sets detailed paper/drawing standards (A4 or 8.5x11 sheets, high-contrast black lines), which is why firms outsource to specialists. Demand volume not quantified.

accounts: Upwork freelancer account + ID verification (proposals cost Connects, ~$0.15 each)
PayPal or Payoneer linked to a bank account

unitEconomics.notes: Estimate: patent drawing services commonly charge ~$25-$120 per sheet; fee blends Fiverr 20% and Upwork 0-15%. Fiverr (20%) and Upwork (variable 0-15% since 2025) fee figures are estimated: their official fee pages were bot-blocked when checked in Nov 2026.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only; startup cash is not amortised. Months include ramp-up to the first order. No fixed costs.

marketConditions.notes: Patent filings are steady and drawings must meet strict office rules, so firms keep outsourcing to reliable illustrators; AI tools help with tracing but cannot guarantee compliance. Established drafting firms and offshore studios set low prices. Winning requires accuracy and repeat relationships with law firms; marketplace-only sellers see sporadic orders.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Quote per sheet with a free compliance check and fast turnaround; offer firm-level volume pricing once a law firm sends repeat work.
profitPath: Month 0: 5 sample sheets to USPTO standard, gigs published (cost $0)
Month 1-3: first inventor orders, expected $50-$300
Month 3-6: pitch small IP law firms directly
Month 6-12: 1-3 firm clients with recurring sheets

strategies.name: Affiliate-network content site with programmatic SEO (Awin, CJ, Impact, Rakuten)
strategies.summary: Data-driven pages (comparisons, alternatives, 'X vs Y', location/spec pages) monetized with merchant programs from major networks.
strategies.howItWorks: Join networks such as Awin (absorbed ShareASale in 2025), CJ, Impact and Rakuten, get approved by merchants in one vertical (e.g. software, travel gear, home services), then generate many structured pages from a real dataset (specs, prices, features) with unique analysis per page. Merchants pay CPA/CPS commissions (typically 5-30%, cookie windows 30-90 days set per merchant).

payout.minimumPayout: Awin 20 GBP/EUR/USD (selectable; default 50); Impact $10; CJ and Rakuten thresholds not re-verified (commonly cited ~$50)

legality.notes: Legal everywhere in the reference set; Google spam policies (scaled content abuse) are a ranking risk, not a legal one.

availability.notes: Networks accept publishers from most countries; merchant approval is per program and often favours established sites. Some merchants only accept traffic from specific countries.

automationPlan: Ingest merchant product feeds/APIs into a database
Template + LLM generate pages with unique per-entity commentary
Auto-refresh prices, deals and dead links from feeds
Track EPC per page and prune losers

Official Impact help: $10 minimum threshold, payouts on the Tuesday/Thursday after threshold or on the 1st/15th. CJ's publisher page confirms two payouts per month. These are mainstream networks paying thousands of publishers.

skills: basic scripting (an AI coding agent covers most of it)
accounts: Awin, CJ, Impact and/or Rakuten publisher accounts + tax forms

marketConditions.notes: Programmatic sites that win are built on proprietary or hard-to-gather data with real per-page analysis. Google's 2024-2025 scaled-content-abuse and site-reputation policies deindex thin template pages, and AI answers reduce clicks. Common failures: merchant approval refusals for new sites, then a traffic spike followed by a core-update collapse.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Commissions are set by merchants; after you show volume, ask merchants for tiered or custom rates (often +2-5 points) and prioritise recurring or high-CPA offers.

Month 1-3: publish 200-1,000 pages with unique analysis; expect $0-20
Month 3-6: prune pages without impressions, enrich winners; expect $20-100/month
Month 6-12: negotiate rates, add comparison tools; median ~$50/month, top sites $1k+

strategies.name: Compliant B2B cold-email lead generation service
strategies.summary: Run opt-out-compliant B2B outbound email campaigns that book sales meetings for clients, paid per month or per qualified meeting.
strategies.howItWorks: B2B firms pay for booked meetings. You define the ideal customer, source business contacts from licensed data vendors, personalize emails with an LLM, and send low-volume campaigns from client domains with unsubscribe link and postal address. Replies are triaged and meetings booked. Honor opt-outs (US: 10 business days) and consent rules of each recipient country.

payout.notes: Net-7 to net-30 invoices; take 30-50% deposits. Stripe is not offered in many reference countries (stripe.com/global, Nov 2026: absent in e.g. the Philippines, Colombia, Argentina, Ukraine, Georgia, Armenia, Sri Lanka, Tunisia, Ecuador, Serbia; Nigeria, Kenya, Ghana and South Africa only via its extended network); Payoneer covers 190+ countries and territories.

restrictedIn: Germany (recipients: UWG s.7(2) no.2 requires prior express consent for email ads to any addressee, incl. businesses)
Netherlands (recipients: Telecommunicatiewet art. 11.7(1) consent also applies to legal persons)
Canada (recipients: CASL consent; implied only for conspicuously published addresses relevant to the recipient's role)
legality.notes: Restrictions are on recipients located in these countries, not on where the operator lives. US: CAN-SPAM has no B2B exception but is opt-out (honor within 10 business days). UK: ICO confirms PECR email consent rule does not cover corporate subscribers (companies, LLPs, Scottish partnerships); sole traders and some partnerships need consent or soft opt-in. Germany and Canada verified from statute; Netherlands from secondary sources (statute page not parsed). Other likely opt-in recipient markets (Italy, South Korea, Japan partially) not verified, so coverage kept at 88 (~44/50) rather than 94. Never email consumers or use scraped lists.
complianceRequirements: CAN-SPAM: honest headers, postal address, opt-out in 10 business days

availability.notes: Direct invoicing works almost everywhere; legality depends on recipient country, not operator country.

automationPlan: ICP filtering and enrichment from licensed data
fullCycle: Pick a niche with US/UK B2B targets
risks: fines (US up to $53,088 per violating email)
strategies.evidence: FTC CAN-SPAM guide: no B2B exception, opt-out within 10 business days, penalties up to $53,088 per email, so compliant outbound agencies operate legally in the US; ICO confirms UK corporate subscribers can be emailed without prior consent.

accounts: Upwork freelancer account + ID verification (proposals cost Connects, ~$0.15 each)
Wise Business or Stripe account for invoicing (KYC)

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only; startup cash is not amortised. Months include ramp-up to the first order. Your own prospecting stack costs ~$100/month before the first client.

marketConditions.notes: AI-written cold email flooded inboxes in 2024-2026, and Google/Yahoo/Microsoft bulk-sender rules plus stricter spam filtering cut reply rates sharply. Agencies that win run small, highly targeted campaigns in niches they know and charge for meetings that convert. Most new agencies fail to book meetings for their first client and lose them within 2-3 months.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Start with a pilot priced per qualified meeting to reduce client risk, then convert to a monthly retainer plus a per-meeting bonus.
profitPath: Month 0: domain, deliverability setup, prospecting your own clients (cost ~$100/month)
Month 1-3: 1 pilot client, expected $0-$800
Month 3-6: retain if meetings convert; add a second niche client
Month 6-12: 2-4 retainers for the minority who prove results

strategies.name: Micro-SaaS sold via merchant of record (Lemon Squeezy/Paddle/Polar/Stripe)
strategies.summary: Build a small niche web app and sell subscriptions globally through a merchant of record that handles tax/VAT.
strategies.howItWorks: Solve one painful problem for a niche (e.g. invoice parsing, social scheduler for a vertical, PDF tools). A merchant of record (Lemon Squeezy, Paddle, Polar) is the legal seller, collects VAT/sales tax and pays you, which enables sellers from countries Stripe doesn't support. Fees ~5% + 50c (Paddle/Lemon Squeezy) or ~4-5% (Polar). Payers are businesses/consumers paying monthly. Most micro-SaaS earn little; a minority reach $1k-$20k MRR.

payout.minimumPayout: Lemon Squeezy $50; Paddle $100/EUR100/GBP100; Polar none published; Stripe none
payout.notes: Lemon Squeezy: payouts on the 14th and 28th after a 13-day hold, bank (USD or local) or PayPal (USD). Paddle seller terms: paid on or before the 15th of the following month if the month's fee exceeds $100/EUR100/GBP100; bank (ACH/international, $15 per international transfer) or PayPal.

legality.notes: Legal software sale; MoR handles indirect tax.

availability.notes: Paddle sells into 200+ countries; Lemon Squeezy pays sellers in 'hundreds' of supported countries; Polar pays via Stripe Connect Express in 119 countries; Stripe direct in ~46 countries.

automationPlan: AI coding agent builds and maintains the app
risks: Most products never reach meaningful revenue
strategies.evidence: Lemon Squeezy and Paddle docs publish payout rules; Indie Hackers and public 'open startup' dashboards show many solo SaaS earning recurring revenue.

unitEconomics.notes: Indie SaaS commonly charges $9-$29/month; MoR fee ~5% plus $0.50 and ~$1 infra per customer (cost). Lemon Squeezy adds +1.5% for international and PayPal payments and +0.5% for subscriptions; Polar Starter is 5% + 50c.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). Two median customers cover fixed costs; most products take 6-12 months to reach a handful of paying users.

marketConditions.notes: Builders with distribution (an audience, SEO, or a niche community) win; AI coding agents made building trivial in 2025-2026, so launches exploded and features get copied fast. Stripe acquired Lemon Squeezy in 2024 and MoR options keep expanding, so payments are no longer the bottleneck; marketing is. Failure mode: a polished product with no channel to customers.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Charge from day one with a low founding price ($9-$19) and annual discount; raise prices for new customers every few months as features and testimonials accumulate.
profitPath: Month 0: interview 10 potential users, build MVP (cost $20 + $30/mo)
Month 1-2: launch on niche communities; $0-$50
Month 3-6: content/SEO and integrations; $30-$300 MRR
Month 6-12: annual plans and price increase; $50-$2,000 MRR for top quartile

strategies.name: Open Collective, Polar.sh and thanks.dev funding for OSS
strategies.summary: Collect OSS funding through a fiscal host (Open Collective), Polar.sh donations/subscriptions, or dependency-based corporate funding via thanks.dev, then pay yourself.
strategies.howItWorks: Open Collective: a fiscal host holds money transparently and you submit expenses/invoices for your work, paid via PayPal or Wise. Polar.sh: merchant of record that lets you sell sponsorships, paid access, license keys and donations for repos. thanks.dev: companies fund their whole dependency tree; registered maintainers receive an algorithmic share. Payers are companies and users who depend on your code.

payout.minimumPayout: Polar: no minimum published; Open Collective: per-expense, no fixed minimum
payout.notes: Polar pays out via Stripe Connect Express (Stripe payout fees apply); Open Collective hosts may charge a host fee (e.g. ~10%); thanks.dev requires maintainer registration. Polar/Open Collective fee figures not re-confirmed on official pages in Nov 2026.

legality.notes: Donations and invoices for maintenance work are legal; income taxable. Fiscal host handles some compliance.

availability.notes: Polar's official list has 119 Stripe Connect Express payout countries, covering 36 of 48 reference countries (missing: Brazil, Nepal, Uganda, Zambia, Malawi, Zimbabwe, Lebanon, Iraq, Libya, Ukraine, Georgia, Kyrgyzstan). Open Collective pays expenses via PayPal/Wise, which covers several of those gaps; thanks.dev payouts route via its partners.

automationPlan: Auto-submit monthly expense invoices from a template
Polar API/webhooks to deliver license keys and gated content
AI-generated transparency updates and changelogs for backers
risks: Funds may sit at org level (thanks.dev)
Open Collective Foundation host closed 2024 - pick an active host
strategies.evidence: Open Collective publicly lists transparent ledgers of paid expenses for thousands of collectives; Polar's docs describe Stripe Connect payouts across its supported countries; thanks.dev distributes funds from companies like Sentry to dependency maintainers.

tools: Open Collective via Open Source Collective host
skills: maintain an open-source project with real users
accounts: Polar account + Stripe Connect Express KYC
PayPal or Wise for expense reimbursement

unitEconomics.notes: Typical backer pledges $2-$25/month, company backers $100-$500; fee approximates a ~10% fiscal-host fee plus ~3% card processing on Open Collective (Polar Starter is 5% + 50c for organisations created after May 27, 2026, +1.5% for non-US cards). Open Collective host fee estimated; its pricing page is bot-blocked.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). No fixed costs; break-even equals the month of the first backer or first thanks.dev allocation.

marketConditions.notes: Collectives with corporate users and visible budgets win; thanks.dev and similar dependency-funding schemes pay small algorithmic shares spread across thousands of packages. The Open Collective Foundation host shut down in 2024 and Polar has refocused on selling products/subscriptions, so maintainers must pick hosts carefully. Failure mode: money sits in the collective balance and is too small to justify expense paperwork.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Publish a concrete budget (e.g. $500/month = 2 days of maintenance) and offer company tiers with logo placement; switch to paid support or license keys on Polar once demand is proven.
profitPath: Month 0: apply to Open Source Collective, register on thanks.dev, connect Polar (cost $0)
Month 1-2: add funding links and a budget page; expected $0-$10
Month 3-6: contact companies in your dependents list; expected $10-$50/month
Month 6-12: submit monthly expenses to pay yourself and add a paid tier on Polar; $15-$300/month if usage grows

strategies.name: Retail-audit and data-collection apps (Premise, Roamler, BeMyEye, Field Agent)
strategies.summary: Complete small paid tasks on your phone such as photographing shop shelves, checking prices or answering local surveys; paid to PayPal, Payoneer or mobile money, with wide coverage in Africa, Asia and Latin America.
strategies.howItWorks: Market-research and NGO clients pay for ground-truth data. Apps publish tasks near you (take a photo of a product display, confirm a store is open, report local fuel prices, answer a short survey) paying roughly $0.25–$10 each. Premise pays contributors via PayPal, Payoneer or Bitcoin depending on country; Roamler covers Europe and the US. Tasks require leaving the house, but payment is reliable and these apps are among the few that pay residents of lower-income reference countries directly.

payout.notes: Premise (official contributor site): 'paid instantly via Paypal, Payoneer, or Bitcoin', options depending on country; minimum not stated. Roamler €5 PayPal minimum not re-confirmed. Field Agent was dropped: fieldagent.net now redirects to Storesight, a B2B retail-intelligence platform. BeMyEye's site is now B2B-only; its contributor app status is unconfirmed.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; respect store photography rules and do not photograph people without consent.

availability.notes: Premise recruits in many lower-income countries (country list not published on the contributor page; reported 100+ including Kenya, Nigeria, Ghana, Philippines, Indonesia, India, Colombia, Mexico, Brazil). Roamler: Europe and a US programme.

automationPlan: Nothing in task execution; submissions are GPS- and photo-verified.
Automate task alerts and payout logging.

Task supply depends on client demand in your city
strategies.evidence: Premise's contributor site advertises instant PayPal/Payoneer/Bitcoin payouts and the company partners with large NGOs and CPG brands; Roamler still runs a 'For Roamlers' community programme in 2026.

unitEconomics.notes: Tasks pay roughly $0.25-10; $1 is a typical transport cost per task when it requires a short trip.

strategies.howItWorks: Create a tutor profile with intro video and set an hourly rate. Students find you via search, book a trial, then buy packages. Preply keeps the trial and 18-33% after; italki ~15%; Wyzant (US) 25%. Strongest demand: English, native languages, exam prep, math.

payout.notes: italki minimum withdrawal $30; Payoneer flat $3. Wyzant pays to US bank accounts only. Commission and withdrawal figures for Preply/italki/Wyzant could not be re-fetched this run (help centers block automated access); treat as approximate.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; contractor income. Wyzant tutors must be US residents.

strategies.name: Paid music and product reviewing on Slicethepie
strategies.summary: Listen to unreleased songs (and review fashion/video items) and get paid small amounts per written review.
strategies.howItWorks: Slicethepie plays you a track clip and you write a short critique and rating; better-quality reviews raise your star rating and per-review pay. Pay per review depends on star rating and is not published.

availability.notes: Open to reviewers worldwide subject to panel geo requirements; PayPal/Revolut/Airtm cover most reference countries.

Account locked if the balance reaches $100 unwithdrawn

strategies.name: Sell sheet music and licensed arrangements via ArrangeMe (Hal Leonard) and Musicnotes
strategies.summary: Publish originals, public-domain arrangements and licensed arrangements of popular copyrighted songs as sheet music sold across Hal Leonard's network.
strategies.howItWorks: You arrange songs for specific instruments/levels (easy piano, string quartet, SATB) in notation software and upload PDFs or interactive scores to ArrangeMe, which clears copyrighted songs from its approved list and distributes to Sheet Music Plus, Sheet Music Direct, MuseScore and partner retailers. Teachers, students and ensembles buy them. Musicnotes Marketplace is a parallel channel. AI transcription tools speed up drafts but humans must check notation.

payout.notes: Verified from ArrangeMe Terms: originals/public-domain arrangements 50% (52% Pro), copyrighted arrangements 10% (12% Pro) on Hal Leonard sites; 70% of receipts for subscriptions/extended network. Paid ~30 days after month end. Musicnotes Marketplace (help center): free Creator membership allows up to 10 uploaded arrangements (paid tiers for more); copyrighted songs must be on Musicnotes' licensed list; royalties are auto-calculated by song classification, but the rates are not published in the help center.

legality.notes: Legal: ArrangeMe obtains licenses for approved copyrighted songs; arranging unlicensed copyrighted songs outside such programs infringes copyright.
complianceRequirements: only arrange songs on the approved list or public domain/originals

availability.notes: ArrangeMe accepts sellers internationally; PayPal payout. PayPal receiving is limited in a few reference countries (e.g. Bangladesh, Libya, Iraq); Payoneer/Wise or local alternatives may be needed.

automationPlan: Use AI audio-to-MIDI/notation tools for first drafts
Script PDF generation, titling, difficulty tags and descriptions
Track best-selling songs/levels to choose next arrangements
strategies.evidence: ArrangeMe's published terms specify commission rates, $20 PayPal threshold and monthly payment; it is Hal Leonard's official self-publishing channel.

skills: arranging for specific instruments and levels

unitEconomics.notes: Hal Leonard sites list single arrangements at about $4-8. ArrangeMe pays 50% on originals/public-domain (fee 50%) but only 10% on copyrighted arrangements. Hours amortise arranging over expected sales.

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost. No cash outlay; the $20 PayPal minimum and month-end-plus-30-day lag push first cash to month 3-6.

marketConditions.notes: Sellers with large catalogues of easy-level arrangements of popular or seasonal songs earn steadily; single arrangements rarely sell. Copyrighted pop titles sell more but pay only 10%. AI transcription speeds drafting but also adds supply. Failure modes: tiny catalogue, competition with free MuseScore scores.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Price at the default $5-6 for single parts, slightly more for ensemble scores; build volume across 50+ titles and seasonal pieces rather than raising prices.
profitPath: Month 0: first 10 arrangements uploaded (cost $0)
Month 1-3: first sales, first payout once $20 accrues
Month 3-6: 30-50 titles, seasonal content; $20-60/month
Month 6-12: 80-100 titles; most earn $30-150/month

strategies.name: Amazon Associates niche review/comparison site
strategies.summary: Hands-on 'best X for Y' comparison content linking to Amazon products for a commission on qualifying purchases.
strategies.howItWorks: Pick a narrow buyer-intent niche (e.g. tools for a specific hobby), publish genuinely useful comparisons, buying guides and spec tables, and link products with your Associates tag. Amazon pays a category-based % of purchases made within the 24-hour click window. Rates are low: Amazon US's official fixed table runs 0-10% by category (most categories 1-4.5%, e.g. 3% home/toys, 2.5% PC, 1% grocery/health), and 2026 trade press reports further cuts for some publishers, so volume and real first-hand testing are what differentiate a site from AI-generated competitors.

payout.minimumPayout: $10 for gift card and direct deposit (US); higher for check; GBP 25 (UK); varies by store

strategies.name: Remote usability testing (UserTesting, Userlytics, Trymata/QuestionPro)
strategies.summary: Record yourself using websites and apps while thinking aloud. Product teams pay for each test.
strategies.howItWorks: Companies pay UX research platforms to recruit testers who match a demographic. You take a screener, and if you qualify you record a 10-20 minute screen-and-voice session, usually paid about $10, while live interviews pay $30-120. Screeners are competitive, so most of the time goes into qualifying. The feedback has to be genuinely yours.

payout.notes: UserTesting pays only via PayPal, usually 14 days after the test. Userlytics pays $10-50 per study, every 15 days after client approval (method not stated on its tester page). Trymata's tester page now redirects to QuestionPro UX; its tester payouts could not be confirmed.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere.

availability.notes: UserTesting recruits only in countries where PayPal operates. Its standard tester countries are the US, UK, DE, FR, CA, IN and AU. Userlytics recruits more broadly.

automationPlan: Auto-refresh notifications/email filters for new tests
Pre-written profile facts to answer screeners consistently
risks: Ratings drop if audio quality is poor
strategies.evidence: UserTesting's official 'get paid to test' page says PayPal is the only method and pays ~14 days after completion. Userlytics' tester page lists $10-50 per study, paid every 15 days. Reviews consistently report $10 per standard UserTesting test.

unitEconomics.notes: UserTesting shows each test's reward before you take it and no longer publishes a rate card; the $10 standard / $4 short-test figures are reported by testers (estimated). Userlytics lists $10-50 per study; live interviews pay $30-120 (estimated).

breakEven.notes: No fixed costs, so every paid unit is profit; break-even equals the time to the first payout. First pay arrives about 14 days after the first qualified test.

marketConditions.notes: The $10 test rate has not moved for years while tester supply has grown, so screeners fill within minutes. UX research budgets were cut in 2023-2024 and AI 'synthetic user' tools now replace some cheap unmoderated tests. Testers in the US/UK with professional profiles get the live interviews that make up most of the money; only about 15% reach $100/month. profitLikelihoodPercent here is the chance of receiving any real net-positive payout within 12 months (typical income is under $100/month), calibrated to the catalog's survey-panel anchor. Cross-catalog calibration: profitLikelihoodPercent lowered from 60 to 45 to sit with paid-research-interviews (45) and crowdtesting-bug-hunts (50); income can exceed $100/month, and the median starter nets only about $50.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Rates are fixed; improve earnings by keeping high ratings (clear audio, following tasks) which unlock more invites and live interviews.
profitPath: Month 0: sign up, pass the practice test (cost $0)
Month 1-2: 2-5 tests: $20-50
Month 3-6: alerts plus a consistent profile: $40-100/month
Month 6-12: chase live interviews ($30-120 each) to lift income above $100/month

strategies.summary: Hold brandable domains and offer them on monthly lease-to-own plans, earning installments until buyers own them.
strategies.howItWorks: You register or hand-pick brandable domains, then list them on Afternic, which inherited Dan.com's LTO system in 2024. Startups pay monthly installments; you keep ownership until fully paid, and if they default you keep the domain and payments. LTO max is $100,000 ($5,000 in California).

payout.minimumPayout: PayPal $25 (no fee); ACH $10 ($0.90 fee); eCheck $25 ($5); wire $25 ($15-26)
payout.notes: LTO commission: 25% standard or 15% with GoDaddy Aftermarket nameservers ($15 minimum), +5% if Afternic Boost is on, minus a term discount (0% for up to 12 months, 5% for 13-24, 10% for 25-36, 15% for 37-60). Down payments pay full commission. Eligible Buy-It-Now prices $495 to $5M.

legality.notes: Domain trading is legal; avoid trademarked names (UDRP risk).

availability.notes: Afternic serves sellers worldwide.

automationPlan: AI name generation and trademark screening
strategies.evidence: Afternic's official help center and Lease-to-Own page document commission tiers and payout methods; DomainNameWire documented Dan.com's 2024 migration of LTO to Afternic.

unitEconomics.notes: Typical lease-to-own deals $50-$200/month over 12-36 months; Afternic commission 25% (Basic) or 30% (Boost), 15-20% with GoDaddy nameservers, with lease-to-own discounts of up to 15% by term (20% used); cost = acquisition of the leased name.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). Fixed cost = renewals of ~30 domains (~$28/month); installments arrive monthly once a contract starts.

marketConditions.notes: LTO increases conversion for $2k-$10k names because startups prefer monthly payments, but you still need names buyers want, and most portfolios get no takers. AI name generators push buyers toward cheap available domains. Default by lessees is common, though the domain returns to you.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Offer 12-36 month terms at a total ~10-20% above the Buy Now price, with a low first installment to convert startups.
profitPath: Month 0: register/buy ~30 brandable names ($300)
Month 1-6: enable LTO on Afternic; no deals expected
Month 6-12: prune names before renewal
Month 12-24: first contract (if any) adds $50-$150/month

strategies.name: Paid Discord/Telegram or Skool community (Whop, LaunchPass, Skool)
strategies.summary: Charge a monthly fee for access to a gated chat community or Skool group around a niche skill or interest.
strategies.howItWorks: Run a focused community (interview prep, niche hobby, language practice) where members pay monthly for access, resources and your presence. Whop/LaunchPass bill via Stripe and auto-grant Discord/Telegram roles; Skool bundles forum, courses and gamification. Trading/betting 'signals' groups are excluded.

payout.notes: Whop processing 2.7% + $0.30 (+1.5% intl cards, +1% FX); payout fees: next-day ACH $2.50, wire $23, instant 4% + $2.50 (Whop's fees page lists no separate platform fee, as modelled in the unit economics; the ~3% fee in older guides is not applied). LaunchPass Premium $29/mo + 3.5% + Stripe (free tier $0/mo). Skool Hobby $9/mo + 10% or Pro $99/mo + 2.9%.

manualSteps: Seed initial members and be personally present
strategies.evidence: Skool's public leaderboard shows communities with thousands of paying members; Whop, Skool and LaunchPass publish official fee and payout docs. Availability raised to 75 because Whop's payout docs list 200+ countries.

Verifier: Whop fee corrected from ~10% to ~5% (docs.whop.com/fees); median month-12 net lowered from $120 to $60 to agree with a 15% chance of reaching $100/month.

strategies.howItWorks: Publish a Patreon page with 2-4 tiers and post exclusive content (files, tutorials, early access) on a schedule. Patrons are existing followers of your free work who pay to support you. Without an audience conversion is near zero; typically 1-5% of engaged followers convert.

payout.minimumPayout: Low/none (exact payout minimum not re-confirmed; PayPal payout fee ~1%)
payout.notes: Current standard plan: 10% platform fee plus payment processing, currency conversion and payout fees (patreon.com/pricing). Pages launched before Aug 2025 may keep legacy 5-12% plans. Payout minimums/fees per method could not be re-fetched (help center blocks automated access).

legality.notes: Legal everywhere in the reference set; income taxable.

availability.notes: Payouts via PayPal/Payoneer in most countries; Stripe deposit where supported.

automationPlan: AI-draft exclusive posts from public work
manualSteps: Build the audience that feeds the page
Make the core creative work patrons pay for

AI for drafting posts and perks

strategies.howItWorks: Create genuinely useful tools (solar savings calculator, B2B software selector quiz, 'do I need a lawyer for X' guide) that end in a clearly consented form or partner redirect. CPA/lead networks (e.g. MaxBounty) or vendor partner programs pay a fixed amount per qualified lead or signup ($5-$100+ depending on vertical). Incentivized or fake form fills are fraud.

strategies.name: Premium AI Discord bot via Discord App Subscriptions
strategies.summary: Build a useful AI-powered Discord bot (moderation, summaries, game master, translation) and sell premium tiers natively in Discord.
strategies.howItWorks: Discord lets verified apps sell subscriptions and one-time SKUs inside Discord. An AI bot that summarizes channels, translates, moderates or runs games can charge per server or per user. Coding agents can build and maintain the bot; usage costs (LLM API) must be below the subscription price. Discord pays out via Stripe after a monetization eligibility review.

payout.frequency: monthly, within 45 days after month end

Payouts are not automatic: Developer Support runs a payout eligibility review first. Native Premium Apps only for teams based in the US, UK or EU; others need external billing where Discord policy allows.

Agent writes listing copy for Top.gg

strategies.name: Sell an online course through Hotmart's built-in affiliate network
strategies.summary: Publish a course or digital training on Hotmart and let its marketplace of affiliates promote it for a commission you set.
strategies.howItWorks: Hotmart is a Brazil-born creator platform for courses and digital products, strongest in Latin America and Europe. You host the course in its member area, set the price and an affiliate commission, and list it in the affiliate marketplace. There, thousands of affiliates choose products to promote with their own traffic. That differs from Teachable or Udemy because sales can come from other people's marketing. Hotmart charges 9.9% plus a fixed USD/EUR 1.00 per sale (no monthly fee) and handles checkout, local payment methods and installments.

payout.minimumPayout: A minimum applies; amount set in the Help Center (not confirmed)
payout.frequency: on request after 30-day release (or automatic monthly transfer)
payout.notes: Hotmart's payments policy: 9.9% service fee plus a fixed USD 1.00 / EUR 1.00 / BRL 2.49 per sale (20% and no fixed fee on products up to BRL 10). Balances are released 30 days after payment approval by default; eligible creators outside Brazil can take a paid cash advance within 2 business days. Each manual withdrawal has a fee and a minimum amount, given only in the Help Center, which could not be read. Automatic monthly transfers carry no withdrawal fee. Transactions are in BRL (Brazil), EUR (EU) or USD (everyone else).

legality.notes: Selling courses is legal everywhere. Courses on regulated topics (finance, health) need care to avoid unlicensed advice.
complianceRequirements: consumer-law refund rules (Hotmart offers a guarantee period)

availability.notes: Strong in Brazil, Spanish-speaking LATAM and Europe. Hotmart publishes no list of payout countries; withdrawals go to a bank account in your own name.

automationPlan: AI-drafted course scripts, slides and sales page
Affiliate swipe files and email sequences generated once
fullCycle: Upload course and set price and commission
risks: Affiliates may use aggressive marketing that hurts your brand
Withdrawal fee and minimum not published in the policy text
strategies.evidence: Hotmart is one of the largest course platforms in LATAM. Its pricing page confirms per-sale fees with no monthly fee, and its payments policy sets out the 9.9% + fixed fee and the 30-day release.

tools: Hotmart members area and checkout (no monthly fee)
LLM for scripts and sales page copy
skills: course design and recording (AI covers drafts)

marketConditions.notes: Hotmart's affiliate marketplace is crowded with courses; top affiliates pick products with proven conversion and high commissions. Producers with their own audience win; newcomers rarely get affiliate traffic. AI makes course creation cheap, flooding the market and pushing buyers toward free AI tutoring. Month 2-3: first sales from own network, $50-200 total

strategies.name: Rent out your car on Turo (PHYSICAL)

Renters pay Turo; you receive a percentage of the trip price determined by the chosen protection plan. Works best in cities/airports with tourist demand.

payout.notes: US: Stripe initiates payout 3 business days after your first completed trip, then 3 hours after each later trip ends (partial payouts every 7 days for long trips), plus 3-5 business days bank processing. US hosts keep 70%, 80% or 90% of the trip price depending on the chosen earnings (protection) plan.

legality.notes: Peer-to-peer car sharing is legal in most countries, but personal auto insurance may exclude commercial use; some jurisdictions require commercial registration.

equipment: a car you own in an eligible market

strategies.name: Google Opinion Rewards
strategies.summary: Answer 1–3 question surveys from Google. On Android (39 countries) rewards are Google Play credit only; cash via PayPal exists only on the iOS app, whose country list Google no longer documents.

On Android the reward is Google Play credit (not withdrawable); on iOS rewards are paid to PayPal, so the bank path exists only through the iOS app. Income is tiny but near-certain where the app is available.

The survey landing page mentions 'Google Play or PayPal credit'; PayPal is the iOS reward, but the help centre no longer documents iOS availability or a cash-out minimum (historically $2).

The cash (PayPal, iOS) route is undocumented and historically limited to a few countries such as the US, hence the low availability score.

risks: Survey frequency depends on your location history and shopping

strategies.name: Remote session musician, vocalist, mixing and mastering gigs (AirGigs, SoundBetter, Fiverr)
strategies.summary: Sell remote recording (instrument/vocal tracks), mixing and mastering to artists through music-specific freelance marketplaces.
strategies.howItWorks: You list productized services (e.g. 'mix up to 24 stems', 'session guitar track', 'female topline vocal', 'mastering per song') on AirGigs, SoundBetter and Fiverr's music categories. Clients upload stems or references, you deliver files, and the marketplace releases payment on completion. AI-assisted tools (stem separation, assistive mixing/mastering) cut turnaround, but the core value is human ears and performance.

payout.notes: AirGigs: one-time $20 activation fee, 10-15% commission (min $8/order), 3-day clearing then daily PayPal withdrawals. Fiverr: 20% fee, 14-day clearance. SoundBetter (terms of use): clients fund jobs up front and funds are released when the client closes the job; the payment provider deducts a 'Platform Fee' that is shown in the proposal but not published as a percentage; Storefront sales carry a 10% commission plus a $9.99/month Storefront subscription; payouts run through a third-party processor (Stripe Connect named).

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; taxable service income. Work-for-hire / credit terms should be agreed in writing.
complianceRequirements: no use of client stems for other purposes

availability.notes: AirGigs pays via PayPal (Payoneer beta); Fiverr pays via Payoneer almost everywhere. PayPal receiving is limited in a few reference countries (e.g. Bangladesh, Libya, Iraq); Payoneer/Wise or local alternatives may be needed.

Automated stem prep, loudness metering and file packaging
AI-assisted first-pass mix/master then human refinement

strategies.name: Sell beat leases and exclusives on BeatStars / Airbit
strategies.summary: Produce instrumentals and sell non-exclusive leases (MP3/WAV/stems) and exclusive rights to rappers and singers via beat stores.
strategies.howItWorks: You produce instrumentals in popular genres (trap, drill, afrobeats, R&B) and list them on a beat store with tiered license contracts: cheap non-exclusive leases with stream caps, pricier stem/unlimited leases, and exclusive buyouts (the same mechanic covers 'ghost production' full-rights sales to DJs). Artists pay because they need affordable, ready-made production. Traffic comes from the marketplace search plus YouTube 'type beat' uploads that link to the store. Each beat can be leased many times until sold exclusively.

payout.minimumPayout: $0: direct store sales land in your own PayPal/Stripe; Airbit marketplace earnings have no minimum
payout.frequency: per sale (BeatStars, Airbit personal stores); monthly for Airbit marketplace
payout.notes: Verified (help centers, Nov 2026): BeatStars takes 0% of beat sales and funds go straight to the seller's connected PayPal/Stripe; a 12% Marketplace service fee is added to the buyer's price (sellers may opt to cover it), not charged on Pro Page/Blaze sales. Uploading and selling on BeatStars requires a paid Starter/Growth/Professional plan (pricing page showed Starter at $19.99/year during a promotion; free accounts are capped at 10 tracks). Airbit has a free account and Platinum ($19.99/mo or $7.99/mo billed annually); personal stores are zero-commission and pay instantly via PayPal/Stripe; marketplace earnings are paid on the last working day of the following month via Tipalti with no minimum threshold. Airbit's marketplace commission rate is not published. Airbit Content ID (Platinum only) pays 80%.

legality.notes: Selling licenses to your own compositions is legal everywhere; income is taxable. Beats using uncleared samples or AI output without rights cannot be licensed.

register works with PRO/publishing admin if desired

PayPal receiving is limited in a few reference countries (e.g. Bangladesh, Libya, Iraq), and Stripe is unavailable in many African and South Asian countries, so Airbit's Tipalti wire option may be the only route there. Zero-capital route is Airbit's free account; BeatStars needs a paid plan (about $20/year at promo pricing).

Batch-render tagged MP3 previews, WAVs and stem zips
Scheduled YouTube type-beat uploads via API linking to store
Contract PDFs generated by the platform automatically

strategies.name: YouTube Partner Program with an AI-assisted (faceless) channel

Advertisers pay Google; creators get 55% of long-form ad revenue and 45% of the Shorts pool share. Since July 2025 the 'inauthentic content' policy demonetizes mass-produced, template or repetitive videos, so volume farming fails.
