The 55% long-form share is not stated on the fetched YouTube help pages; treat as estimated.

breakEven.notes: No startup cash or fixed cost, so break-even = first payout received. The binding constraint is the YPP threshold (1,000 subs + 4,000 watch hours) plus the $100 AdSense minimum, typically 6-12 months for channels that make it.

marketConditions.notes: Winners are channels with a clear expert angle and strong packaging that publish consistently for a year or more. AI made production cheap, so supply exploded, and the July 2025 inauthentic-content policy demonetizes templated faceless output. Most channels never reach YPP; those that do often earn under $50/month until a breakout video.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Ad rates are set by advertisers; pick high-CPM topics (software, finance, B2B tools) and 8+ minute videos for mid-rolls. Once past 10k subscribers, add sponsor slots priced at ~$15-30 per 1,000 expected views and affiliate links.
profitPath: Month 0: pick a niche with search demand, set up channel and templates (cost $0)
Month 1-3: publish 2 original videos/week (~25 videos), expected $0
Month 4-8: double down on topics with highest click-through and retention; reach YPP if traction exists, first AdSense payout ~$100
Month 9-12: add affiliate links and a first sponsor; typical successful channel $50-300/month

strategies.name: Apply for open-source and creator grants/fellowships (FLOSS/fund, NLnet, Sovereign Tech, Emergent Ventures)
strategies.summary: Write short applications to foundations that pay maintainers and talented individuals to build public-good work.
strategies.howItWorks: Funders award non-dilutive grants for open-source maintenance or ambitious individual projects. FLOSS/fund (Zerodha, up to $1M/yr) gives $10k-$100k per project per year to established projects that publish a funding.json manifest, reviewed quarterly; NLnet gives EUR 5k-50k first grants via recurring calls (Restack, CodeSupply open with a 3 Nov 2026 deadline) to projects with a strong European dimension; Sovereign Tech Agency funds critical OSS infrastructure globally (Fund minimum EUR 50k of work) plus Fellowship/Standards programs; Emergent Ventures offers micro-grants. Payment is by bank transfer after selection and contracting.

payout.notes: STA contracts follow a compliance review of up to 8 weeks; FLOSS/fund requires tax-residency paperwork before disbursing. Emergent Ventures terms not re-verified (site blocks automated access).

legality.notes: Receiving grants is legal; may be subject to sanctions screening.

availability.notes: FLOSS/fund and Sovereign Tech Fund invest globally; NLnet's EU-funded calls require a strong European dimension (applicants usually from Horizon Europe-eligible countries); Emergent Ventures historically global.

automationPlan: AI-assisted research of calls and budget drafting (NLnet requires the proposal itself to be human-written)
strategies.evidence: FLOSS/fund allocated $1M in 2025 to projects like Blender, FFmpeg, KDE; NLnet and Sovereign Tech Agency publish open calls and funded-project lists.

accounts: bank account able to receive EUR/USD wires

unitEconomics.notes: NLnet awards ~EUR 5k-50k, FLOSS/fund $10k-$100k, Emergent Ventures $1k-$50k; hours = application effort per award at ~10-20% success (estimate). Grant money pays for the work you then must deliver.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). No fixed cost; grants pay in milestones over months.

marketConditions.notes: Funders favour maintainers with existing adoption and credible plans; AI-assisted applications increased volume in 2025-2026, lowering acceptance rates. Grant money is compensation for deliverables, so true profit is modest. Most applicants receive nothing in a given year.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Budget at your real hourly rate for clearly scoped milestones; start with small asks to build a funding track record.
profitPath: Month 0: identify 3-5 matching programmes, draft proposals (cost $0)
Month 1-4: submit and wait for review
Month 4-9: first award (if any) and first milestone payment
Month 9-12: deliver and reapply with track record

strategies.name: Twitch Extensions monetized with Bits
strategies.summary: Build interactive Twitch Extensions (polls, viewer games, overlays) where viewers spend Bits on actions; the developer gets a share of the Bits revenue.
strategies.howItWorks: Build a panel/overlay Extension with Bits products (1-10,000 Bits), such as triggering on-stream effects or viewer mini-games. Twitch splits Bits revenue 80% to the broadcaster and 20% to the developer. You get paid after completing Twitch's monetization onboarding (tax interviews and financial details). You earn only if many streamers install it.

payout.minimumPayout: Not stated for extension developers (unverified); Twitch's creator payout minimum is $50 ($100 for wire)
payout.notes: Twitch announced the 80% broadcaster / 20% developer Bits split in 2018; current docs say only that revenue is shared and do not restate the percentages. Docs recommend choosing 'Hold My Payments' at first. Unconfirmed: the payout minimum for extension developers and the current developer share of Bits (dev.twitch.tv monetization and Bits docs and the Twitch Developer Agreement page re-checked Nov 2026).

legality.notes: Legal. No chance-based paid mechanics (loot boxes, gambling). Must check the isBitsEnabled flag and follow Twitch Extension guidelines and review.
complianceRequirements: Twitch developer account and extension review

availability.notes: Bits work only on channels that can receive Bits. Developer payout countries are not listed on the docs. Estimate unverified.

automationPlan: Use AI coding agents to build the extension front end and EBS backend
Automated outreach and onboarding docs for streamers
risks: Very low adoption for most extensions
Extension reviews have been paused before
strategies.evidence: Official Twitch developer docs (fetched 2026-11) describe Bits in Extensions, revenue sharing with developers and the onboarding flow; Twitch's 2018 launch post gives the 20% developer share. Widely installed extensions show the model works at the top end, but most extensions earn little.

unitEconomics.unit: per 10,000 Bits spent in your extension
unitEconomics.notes: Viewers pay about $1.40 per 100 Bits; Twitch credits $0.01 per Bit, and the 2018 split gives the developer 20% ($20 per 10k Bits); current docs do not restate the split.

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost. No cash outlay; meaningful income needs many installing streamers.

marketConditions.notes: Very few extensions earn meaningful Bits; streamers rely on a handful of popular overlays. Failure modes: no installs and low Bits usage.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Price Bits products low (50-100 Bits) to encourage viewer use.
profitPath: Month 0-3: build and pass review (cost $0)
Month 3-6: recruit streamers; little revenue
Month 6-12: most earn $0

strategies.name: Paid academic research studies (Prolific, CloudResearch Connect)
strategies.summary: Get paid to take part in academic and market-research studies such as surveys, experiments and AI-evaluation tasks, with a minimum hourly pay rate enforced by the platform.
strategies.howItWorks: Researchers post studies with a set reward. Studies that match your profile appear first come, first served. Prolific enforces a minimum hourly reward for researchers. Bots and AI-written answers get you banned. Amazon MTurk permanently closed on 2026-09-30, so these platforms are the main remaining option.

payout.minimumPayout: Prolific £6/$6 (combined balance); Connect $5 PayPal (max $100/transfer) or $25 bank transfer (max $250)
payout.frequency: on demand (Prolific once per 24h; Connect once per day)
payout.notes: Prolific cash-outs reach PayPal within 24 hours; researchers have up to 22 days to approve a submission, and new or changed PayPal accounts get a 72-hour cool-off. The PayPal account country must match your residence or country of birth (US residents need a US PayPal).

legality.notes: Taking part in research for pay is legal everywhere. Account eligibility, not legality, is the limiting factor.

availability.notes: Prolific's help centre gates eligibility through PayPal country rules rather than publishing a country list here; third-party reports say it accepts mostly OECD countries plus South Africa and waitlists are common (country list not confirmed from an official page). Connect is US-centric.

manualSteps: Answer every study yourself; automated or LLM answers violate ToS
risks: Low study volume outside the US/UK
strategies.evidence: Prolific's help centre documents the £6/$6 cash-out, PayPal-only payouts within 24 hours and the 22-day approval window. CloudResearch's Connect page documents the $5 PayPal / $25 bank minimums. MTurk's own help page states it permanently closed on September 30, 2026. paymentProbability lowered to 7 because Prolific waitlists can delay entry for months.

skills: consistent honest answers (AI cannot do this; AI answers get you banned)
equipment: webcam and microphone for some studies
accounts: PayPal in your country of residence

unitEconomics.notes: Prolific enforces an hourly floor of £6/$8 and recommends at least £9/$12 (researcher help centre); studies paying near the floor are the norm and AI-evaluation studies pay at the upper end. Researchers pay the platform fee, so participant rates are net.

breakEven.notes: No fixed costs, so every paid unit is profit; break-even equals the time to the first payout. The main delay is the Prolific waitlist, which can run for months.

marketConditions.notes: MTurk's closure on 2026-09-30 moved both requesters and workers onto Prolific and Connect, so studies fill within minutes and waitlists are longer. AI labs now buy many AI-evaluation studies here, which adds demand, but platforms screen hard for LLM-written answers and ban offenders. Roughly 40% of active participants (mostly US/UK) reach $100/month; elsewhere study volume is thin. profitLikelihoodPercent lowered from 70 to 40 to match the ~40% who reach $100/month stated above (typical income here is $100/month, so the standard definition applies).

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Rates are set by researchers; maximise effective pay by taking studies above £9/$12 per hour, keeping a near-perfect approval rate and a complete profile so you qualify for higher-paying longitudinal and AI-task studies.
profitPath: Month 0: join Prolific (waitlist) and Connect, complete every profile question, link PayPal (cost $0)
Month 1-2: once admitted, about 1 hour/day yields $30-80/month
Month 3-6: keep approval near 100%, use alerts to catch studies first, unlock AI-task and longitudinal studies: $80-150/month
Month 6-12: plateau around $100-300/month; add paid research interviews for higher per-hour sessions

strategies.name: Freelance transcription and captioning (Rev, TranscribeMe, GoTranscript)
strategies.summary: Transcribe or caption audio/video files for per-audio-minute pay on transcription marketplaces.
strategies.howItWorks: Clients upload audio, and platforms split it into jobs that freelancers claim and transcribe or correct. Rev pays about $0.40-1.10 per audio minute, and TranscribeMe pays $15-22 per audio hour (average about $250/month). Most jobs now start from an ASR draft, which lowers pay per minute. Speed and accuracy decide your income. Entrance tests and waitlists are common.

payout.notes: Rev pays all approved work weekly via PayPal and currently has a waitlist. TranscribeMe's payout method is not stated on its jobs page.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere.

availability.notes: Mostly open to English speakers worldwide, provided PayPal works in your country. Rev has a waitlist.

risks: Pay rates falling because of ASR
strategies.evidence: Rev's official freelancer page lists $0.40-1.10 per audio minute (transcription) and weekly PayPal pay. TranscribeMe's official jobs page states $15-22 per audio hour with a $250 average and $2,200 top monthly earnings.

unitEconomics.notes: Rev pays $0.40-1.10 per audio minute and TranscribeMe $15-22 per audio hour; editing an ASR draft takes about 3 hours per audio hour for a beginner, so effective pay is $5-10/hour.

breakEven.notes: No fixed costs, so every paid unit is profit; break-even equals the time to the first payout. Weekly PayPal payouts once you pass the test.

marketConditions.notes: Speech recognition now produces near-final drafts, so most work is cheaper ASR clean-up and per-minute rates have fallen. Rev keeps a waitlist and job queues empty quickly. Fast, accurate typists with niche skills (legal, medical, foreign accents) still earn; beginners often quit at $5/hour. Median month-12 net profit was lowered below $100 so it agrees with a profit likelihood under 50% (most starters never reach $100/month). Cross-catalog calibration: profitLikelihoodPercent lowered from 45 to 35 to match content-mill-writing (35) and below crowd-translation-gengo (40), peers with the same declining, AI-squeezed per-unit pay.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Rates are fixed per job; raise effective pay by speed (hotkeys, foot pedal) and by qualifying for higher-paying difficult-audio or foreign-language queues.
profitPath: Month 0: pass entrance tests on 2-3 platforms (cost $0)
Month 1-2: $30-100/month while learning style guides
Month 3-6: improve speed and claim premium jobs: $100-300/month
Month 6-12: plateau; consider moving to captioning QA or specialist transcription

strategies.name: Sell 3D-printable STL models on Cults3D, Printables Store and Thangs
strategies.summary: Design functional or decorative 3D-printable models and sell the files per download on 3D-printing marketplaces.
strategies.howItWorks: You model and test-print functional or decorative objects (organisers, mounts, cosplay parts, replacement parts) and list STL/3MF files; hobbyists buy and print at home. Cults3D reportedly pays designers 80% of the sale; Printables Store charges a 20% fee (min. price $5, Stripe payouts); Thangs takes 30%/20%/15% for items under $5/$5-10/$10+ plus Stripe fees. Alternative: Bambu Lab's MakerWorld is free-download only, but models enrolled in its Exclusive Model Program earn Exclusive Points worth $0.066 each that can be cashed out per $100 earned (eligibility after 100 total prints on your account). Free uploads build followers who buy paid models; parametric OpenSCAD designs yield many variants.

methods: MakerWorld: Exclusive Points cash withdrawal -> bank (via payout provider; users report Airwallex wire)
payout.minimumPayout: Cults3D: threshold exists but amount unverified; Printables/Thangs: none stated (Stripe); MakerWorld: $100 of Exclusive Points per withdrawal
payout.frequency: Cults3D on request (unverified); Thangs monthly; Printables per Stripe schedule; MakerWorld on request (manual review ~1 week)
payout.notes: Thangs fees and Stripe-only payout confirmed on its help center (Stripe payout fee 0.25% + $0.25, currency conversion 2% non-US). Printables 20% fee / $5 minimum price confirmed on Prusa blog. MakerWorld cash rules confirmed on Bambu Lab blog (Oct 2024); regular MakerWorld points are NOT cash (points store only), and Printables Prusameters are NOT cash. Cults3D share/minimum/methods unverified (site returns 403).

legality.notes: Selling original 3D designs is legal everywhere; do not sell files of trademarked characters or replicas of copyrighted products; weapons files are prohibited by platforms and illegal in some countries.

availability.notes: Thangs payouts limited to its Stripe country list (~21/50 reference countries incl. US, UK, Canada, EU members, Japan, Korea, Taiwan, India, Indonesia, Malaysia, Philippines, Mexico, Argentina, Morocco, Singapore). Printables pays only via Stripe (limited list). Cults3D reportedly pays via PayPal (45/50 reference countries, unverified). MakerWorld cash-outs go to a bank account via its payout provider (country coverage unverified).

automationPlan: LLM drafts listings and print settings
Cross-post to all stores (MakerWorld exclusives cannot be sold elsewhere under the exclusive licence)
manualSteps: Physical test print of each model (needs access to a 3D printer)
risks: Untested AI-generated meshes fail to print and draw refunds
strategies.evidence: Prusa's Dec-2023 blog post documents the Printables Store (20% fee, Stripe, $5 min price). Thangs help center publishes its fee tiers and Stripe country list. Bambu Lab's Oct-2024 blog documents MakerWorld Exclusive Points cash rewards ($0.066/point, per $100). Cults3D's 80% designer share is reported by press (Fabbaloo) but its payout page could not be fetched.

unitEconomics.notes: Median $6 functional/decorative model; ~20% platform fee (Thangs charges 20% on $5-9.99 sales, 30% under $5, 15% at $10+; Cults3D/Printables similar) plus ~$0.50 card processing (estimated).

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost on the free tiers, so break-even is the first sale; months shown are the typical ramp to the first sale.

marketConditions.notes: Printer ownership keeps growing (Bambu Lab), but MakerWorld and Printables' free-download culture means most users never pay; designers with followings sell paid files and earn from MakerWorld points. Text-to-3D AI is not yet good enough for functional parts, so craft still matters.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Give away several useful free models to build followers, price paid models at $3-8 and bundles at $15-25.
profitPath: Month 0: design and test-print 5 free + 3 paid models (filament ~$10)
Month 1-3: post free models, first paid sales
Month 3-6: release weekly; $10-60/month
Month 6-12: median ~$20/month; popular designers $500+

strategies.name: Facebook Content Monetization + Instagram creator payouts
strategies.summary: Earn from Reels, long video, photos and text posts on Facebook (plus Stars/subscriptions) and Instagram gifts/subscriptions/bonuses.
strategies.howItWorks: Meta merged in-stream ads, ads on Reels and Performance bonus into a single Facebook Content Monetization program. A professional-mode profile or Page posting original content is invited (Meta's help page says the program is currently invitation-only; you can register interest in the Monetization tab), and earns a share of ad revenue plus bonuses by engagement. Instagram pays via Gifts on Reels, Subscriptions and invite-only bonuses. Meta's 2025 crackdown on 'unoriginal content' removes reach and monetization from reposted/aggregated material, so content must be your own.

payout.notes: Paid around the 21st of the following month once >= $100; the threshold/timing is not stated on Meta's content monetization help page and was not re-verified.

legality.notes: Legal across the set; ad income taxable.
complianceRequirements: Partner Monetization Policies + Content Monetization Policies

availability.notes: Meta publishes no single country list; coverage is broad in Americas/Europe/parts of Asia, partial in many African/South Asian markets. Check Business Suite > Monetization.

automationPlan: Cross-posting own original videos via Meta Graph API / Business Suite scheduling
risks: Program changes frequently and is invite-gated
strategies.evidence: Meta reports paying creators billions per year across Facebook/Instagram; 2025-26 guides document the merged Content Monetization program and payouts.

unitEconomics.unit: per 1,000 views on monetized Reels/videos (payout to creator)
unitEconomics.notes: Meta does not publish rates; creators report from a few cents to ~$3 per 1,000 views depending on country and ad inventory (estimate; rounded to integers). Rate is already net of Meta's share.

breakEven.notes: No startup cash or fixed cost, so break-even = first payout received. The program is invitation-only and pays once the balance reaches the $100 threshold (threshold not re-verified).

marketConditions.notes: Pages with original, consistently posted video in large-audience niches (humor, food, local news, how-to) are the ones invited. Meta's 2025 unoriginal-content crackdown removed reposting farms, and invitation-only access means many diligent creators never get in. Instagram payouts are mostly Gifts, Subscriptions and invite-only bonuses.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: No price setting for ad share; once invited, add Facebook/Instagram Subscriptions at $2.99-$4.99/month for exclusive content and sell brand posts at roughly $10 per 1,000 followers.
profitPath: Month 0: switch to professional mode, register interest in Monetization tab (cost $0)
Month 1-3: post 5+ original Reels/week, expected $0
Month 4-8: if invited, enable monetization; first $100 payout
Month 9-12: add Subscriptions and brand deals; typical invited creator $20-200/month

strategies.name: Print-on-demand via Printful/Printify connected to Etsy or Shopify
strategies.summary: Sell your designs on apparel/mugs/posters in your own Etsy or Shopify store; Printful/Printify print and ship each order, zero inventory.
strategies.howItWorks: You upload designs to Printful or Printify, which sync products to your Etsy or Shopify store. When a customer buys, the POD provider charges your card the base cost and prints/ships directly (PHYSICAL STEP handled by the provider, not you). You keep retail minus base cost and marketplace fees; a $28 tee nets roughly $11 on Etsy with a standard provider and no ads (less with premium providers or ad spend).

payout.minimumPayout: Per sales-channel rules (Etsy: none on weekly schedule; Shopify Payments: none)
payout.notes: Printful/Printify charge you the base cost + shipping per order (no monthly fee); profit arrives via the sales channel. Etsy new-seller funds are held ~14 days.

legality.notes: Legal; PHYSICAL fulfilment and shipping is outsourced to the POD provider. Consumer-protection/returns rules apply.

availability.notes: Printful/Printify connect to Etsy and Shopify globally. Etsy Payments covers ~26 of ~50 reference countries; Shopify Payments only 41 countries (mostly EU/OECD), though Shopify stores elsewhere can use PayPal or local gateways. Shopify also costs a monthly subscription after the trial.

automationPlan: API sync creates products on Printful/Printify and pushes to store
risks: Thin margins; ad spend can exceed profit
Card charged before customer funds clear
strategies.evidence: Printful's Etsy integration page states it is free with no monthly fee and charges only per order (example: $35 tee, $7.50 base + $4.50 shipping + $3.50 Etsy fees); Shopify help center lists Shopify Payments countries.

tools: Printify Free (Premium $24.99/month billed yearly or $39 monthly, not assumed) or Printful (no monthly fee)
Etsy ($0.20/listing) or Shopify (from ~$39/month Basic, not assumed here)
accounts: credit/debit card to pay POD base costs

unitEconomics.notes: Median $28 tee with free shipping: $8.77 base (Printify pricing-page calculator, Unisex Jersey Short Sleeve Tee, Free plan; premium providers cost more) + ~$4.75 US shipping (estimated, not published on Printify's public pages) + $0.45 Etsy fixed fees = $13.97 cost; 9.5% Etsy transaction + processing. Net ~$11 per shirt.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost ~$5/month in Etsy listing renewals (Shopify would add ~$39/month and require ~5 extra sales). Startup $30 = sample orders + initial listings.

marketConditions.notes: Winners run many niche designs and paid ads with tight margins or have their own audience; base costs and shipping rose in 2025-2026 (tariffs, postal changes), squeezing the ~$8-11 per-shirt margin. AI designs made POD easier to start and much more crowded, and trademark takedowns remain a common shop killer.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Price at $26-30 for tees with free shipping to match the market; use limited-time sales sparingly, and raise prices on proven designs or move them to premium blanks.
profitPath: Month 0: connect Printify to Etsy, order samples, list 20 designs (cost $30)
Month 1-2: add 10 designs/week; first sales likely by month 2 ($0-40 net)
Month 3-6: expand winners into new products/colours; $20-150/month net
Month 6-12: optional small ad tests on proven designs; median ~$60/month net

strategies.name: Publish print-on-demand board and card games on The Game Crafter
strategies.summary: Upload a board/card game design; The Game Crafter prints and ships each order and pays you 70% of the markup.
strategies.howItWorks: You design a card or board game, upload art files, set a retail price above TGC's manufacturing cost, and list it in their shop. TGC manufactures and ships each copy (physical step done by the platform, not you). Royalty = 70% of (price - cost); e.g. $15 price - $8 cost = $7 profit, you get $4.90. Payouts run every Monday after a 30-day hold. Contests on TGC and print-and-play versions help gain traction.

payout.notes: Royalties default to shop credit unless a valid PayPal email is set. Publishing requires buying a copy of your own game and waiting 10 days (contest entries exempt).

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; avoid gambling mechanics and licensed IP.

availability.notes: PayPal payout reaches 45/50 reference countries. Physical product is printed/shipped by TGC (marked PHYSICAL but no seller handling).

automationPlan: AI-assisted card art and rules drafting
Scripted card generation from spreadsheets (e.g. nanDECK)
manualSteps: Ordering one physical copy of your game (required before publishing to the shop, then a 10-day wait)
strategies.evidence: TGC help center documents 70/30 profit split, weekly payouts and PayPal method.

unitEconomics.notes: Median $20 game with ~$10 manufacturing cost; TGC keeps 30% of the ~$10 profit (= 15% of price), you get ~$7. TGC's 70/30 profit split confirmed on its royalties help page.

breakEven.notes: Startup $30 = proof copy. Month-6 net ~$10 means ~3 months to recover.

marketConditions.notes: Few print-on-demand games sell more than a handful of copies; designers who win TGC contests or build a community on BoardGameGeek and Reddit do best. Manufacturing and shipping costs rose in 2025-2026, squeezing a margin that is already ~$7 on a $20 game. AI art lowers production cost but does not solve discovery.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Price just above manufacturing cost plus a small margin to win early buyers and contest votes; raise price once reviews arrive, and offer a free print-and-play version as a funnel.
profitPath: Month 0-2: design, playtest, order proof (cost $30)
Month 2-4: publish; first sales
Month 4-8: marketing; $5-30/month
Month 8-12: median ~$10/month

strategies.name: License original music through stock/sync libraries (Pond5, AudioJungle, Musicbed, Artlist)
strategies.summary: Upload original instrumentals to non-exclusive stock music marketplaces, and apply to curated sync libraries, earning per-license royalties.
strategies.howItWorks: You compose/produce royalty-free-friendly background tracks (corporate, cinematic, lo-fi) and upload them non-exclusively to Pond5 and Envato AudioJungle, where video creators buy licenses. Pond5 pays a 30% royalty share on music for non-exclusive artists. Curated libraries (Musicbed, Artlist Original) are invite/application-only but pay larger sync fees or buyouts. Income compounds with catalog size.

payout.notes: Songtradr's open Marketplace closed 1 Sep 2026 (moved to invite-only), so it is excluded.

legality.notes: Licensing your own copyrighted works is legal everywhere; income is taxable. Fully AI-generated audio is restricted or banned by many libraries.
complianceRequirements: own 100% of composition and master (no uncleared samples)
disclose AI use per library policy

availability.notes: Pond5/Envato accept contributors in most countries; payout via PayPal/Payoneer limits a few (e.g. PayPal receive limits in Bangladesh, Nepal, Libya, Iraq).

automationPlan: Script metadata/keyword/description generation per track with an LLM
Batch-render stems, loops and 15/30/60s cutdowns from each master
Bulk upload via CSV/FTP where supported
risks: Oversupplied market; most tracks never sell
Do not register non-exclusive tracks in Content ID (causes false claims on buyers)
strategies.evidence: Pond5's official Sell Your Media page states the 30% music royalty and $25 minimum with 15th-of-month payout; Musicbed reports $155M+ royalties paid to artists all time.

skills: metadata/keywording; AI-generated music is banned or restricted on most libraries
accounts: Pond5 / AudioJungle contributor accounts + tax forms

unitEconomics.notes: Stock licenses typically $20-$50 with the artist keeping ~40-50% non-exclusive (estimated; Pond5 page bot-blocked); sync placements pay more. Hours = production time per track divided by expected sales (estimate).

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). Fixed cost is an optional sample subscription.

marketConditions.notes: Catalogue-heavy composers with hundreds of tracks earn steady royalties; newcomers face libraries of millions of tracks plus subscription libraries (Artlist, Epidemic) that cut per-license prices. AI music generators (Suno, Udio) flooded the low end in 2025-2026; libraries reacted with AI bans, which protects humans but raises review bars. Failure mode: uploading 20 tracks and seeing a handful of sales a year.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Use library-default prices on non-exclusive sites; reserve exclusive curated libraries (Musicbed/Artlist) for your best work and price custom sync on request.
profitPath: Month 0: produce 10-20 tracks and upload with strong metadata (cost $0-$13/mo)
Month 1-6: first sales; expected $0-$50/month
Month 6-12: keep adding 5-10 tracks/month in proven genres
Month 12+: catalogue of 100+ tracks earning $50-$300/month

strategies.name: Newsletter ad network + Boosts (beehiiv Ad Network)
strategies.summary: Monetize a free newsletter with platform-sourced sponsors (paid per unique open or click, as each advertiser sets) and paid subscriber referrals.
strategies.howItWorks: On a paid beehiiv plan (Lite from $49/mo billed annually, $59 monthly; Ad Network 'not in trial; not in all regions') you are offered sponsor campaigns each billing cycle; you place the ad and get paid per unique open (CPM) or unique click (CPC), as set by each advertiser. Boosts pay you a fee per subscriber you recommend to other newsletters. Payers are advertisers and other publishers, distinct from reader subscriptions. Content can be AI-assisted curation, but advertisers drop low-engagement lists.

payout.notes: Paid on the 20th of each month for the prior month's ad units into your beehiiv Wallet; you withdraw manually to bank via Stripe Express (no PayPal/Wise). No minimum stated.

legality.notes: Legal across the set; must label sponsored content.

availability.notes: Payouts only via Stripe Express in Stripe-supported countries; beehiiv says the Ad Network is not available in all regions.

manualSteps: Pay for a paid plan (Lite or above)
strategies.evidence: beehiiv states creators have earned $37M+ from its ad network and guarantees eligible publishers at least one ad opportunity per cycle.

tools: beehiiv paid plan (Lite/Scale from $49/mo annual, $59 monthly)

unitEconomics.unit: per 1,000 unique opens of a sponsored placement (CPM)
unitEconomics.notes: Advertisers set CPM/CPC per campaign; $10-$50 per 1,000 unique opens is the commonly reported range (estimate). Offer amounts are shown as the publisher's payout. Boosts add ~$1-$3 per recommended subscriber. Verified: beehiiv Lite is $49/mo annual or $59/mo monthly and the Ad Network is open to all paid plans; beehiiv's own FAQ uses a $5 CPM example, so the low end was lowered from $10 to $5.

breakEven.notes: Cash $300 = ~6 months of a paid plan before ads start (Ad Network excluded from trial); fixed $49/month needs ~2,000 sponsored opens/month to cover. Startup recovery assumes ~$20/month net at month 6.

marketConditions.notes: Publishers in business, finance, tech and local-news niches with 5k+ engaged subscribers capture most Ad Network spend. A paid plan is required from day one, so small lists run at a loss for months. AI made curation newsletters easy to start, raising competition for readers; advertisers drop lists with weak clicks.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Accept network campaigns while small; once at 5k+ subscribers with 40%+ opens, sell direct sponsorships at $20-$40 CPM and keep Boosts on for subscriber-acquisition income.
profitPath: Month 0: start on free plan, build format and first 300 subscribers (cost $0)
Month 1-3: upgrade to paid plan, grow via Boosts/referrals to ~1,500 subs (cost $49-59/month), expected $0-$30
Month 4-8: run 2-4 ad network placements/month; cover the plan fee
Month 9-12: add direct sponsors; profitable lists reach $100-$500/month

Sell the L$ on the LindeX for a USD balance, then withdraw it with a Process Credit request through Tilia/Thunes. Linden Lab set the LindeX sell fee at 5% from March 2023 (official blog bot-blocked; confirmed via ModemWorld's report of the announcement). The Marketplace commission (10% since 2020) was not re-verified.

complianceRequirements: Tilia identity verification and billing info

Script vendor systems and automatic redelivery (LSL)
Use AI to write Marketplace listings; schedule sales

Fees and limits on L$ conversion

AI product captions in local languages

strategies.name: Construct and sell crossword puzzles to newspapers
strategies.summary: Build original crosswords and submit them to newspaper puzzle editors who pay a flat fee per published puzzle.
strategies.howItWorks: You construct themed crosswords with free or paid construction software and word lists, then submit to outlets like The New York Times, Universal and the LA Times that accept freelance puzzles. Editors buy puzzles that meet strict specs. Pay is a flat fee per puzzle. Software automates grid filling; theme ideas and clueing are the human part.

strategies.name: Dual-license your open-source library (AGPL/GPL + paid commercial license)
strategies.summary: Publish useful code under a copyleft license and sell commercial licenses to companies that cannot comply with AGPL/GPL obligations.
strategies.howItWorks: You build a library/tool businesses want to embed (PDF, charting, sync engine, CLI), release it under AGPL/GPL and offer a commercial license that removes copyleft obligations, sold with license keys. Companies pay because their legal teams forbid shipping AGPL code in proprietary products. Sell via Polar (merchant of record, automatic license keys) or Stripe plus Keygen for license validation. You must hold copyright to all code, so require a CLA from contributors.

payout.notes: Polar (merchant of record) fees: Starter 5% + 50c, Pro 3.8% + 40c, Growth 3.6% + 35c, Scale 3.4% + 30c (orgs created before 27 May 2026 keep 4% + 40c), plus 1.5% for non-US cards; Stripe payout costs ($2/month active, 0.25% + $0.25 per payout, 0.25-1% FX) pass through. Keygen has a free Dev tier (100 active licensed users, 10 releases) and a free self-hosted CE.

legality.notes: Copyright licensing is legal everywhere; Polar as merchant of record handles sales tax/VAT.
complianceRequirements: own copyright to all code (CLA for contributors)

availability.notes: Polar/Stripe payouts cover ~45 countries; elsewhere use Paddle/Lemon Squeezy-style MoRs.

automationPlan: Coding agents build and maintain the library and docs
Automated license-key issuance on purchase via Polar benefits
CI checks for license headers and CLA bot
manualSteps: Enterprise sales questions and custom contracts
risks: Most projects never reach paying adoption
strategies.evidence: Long-running dual-license businesses: iText (AGPL+commercial), Artifex Ghostscript, Qt, MySQL historically; Sidekiq Pro/Enterprise show developers pay for commercial licenses.

skills: building a library companies depend on
B2B sales; AI helps with code and docs

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). Fixed cost is just a domain (~$2/month).

marketConditions.notes: Works for projects with real enterprise adoption (PDF, charting, DB drivers) where legal teams avoid AGPL. AI coding assistants now generate permissive alternatives for small libraries, shrinking demand at the low end. Most new projects never gain the adoption that triggers license purchases.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Start with a simple per-company annual price ($500-$1,500) and a free tier for small firms; add per-seat/enterprise tiers once inbound requests arrive.

Month 3-6: add a commercial license page and CLA
Month 6-12: first inbound requests if adoption exists ($0-$1,500)

strategies.name: Agency-assigned tutoring as a contractor (GoStudent, Varsity Tutors)
strategies.summary: Tutor school students that a tutoring company matches to you, at a per-session rate the company sets. The company handles acquisition, parents and billing.
strategies.howItWorks: Tutoring companies sell lesson subscriptions to parents and assign the students to freelance tutors. You don't market yourself or set prices. You take students in your subjects, teach on the company's classroom tool and log sessions. GoStudent (Europe) pays a base rate of up to GBP 16 per 50-minute lesson, with volume raises (+1.00 per lesson after 150 lessons in 6 months, +1.50 after 300). Varsity Tutors (US) pays per session twice a week.

payout.notes: GoStudent's tutor help center: base rate up to GBP 16 per 50-minute session, depending on availability, subjects and monthly sessions completed. Earnings are paid in full the next month with no minimum, between the 12th and 17th; transfers can take up to 7 days to arrive. Session feedback must be submitted within 24 hours or the session is not paid. No-shows pay a flat 6.50. Volume raises: +1.00 per lesson after 150 lessons in 6 months, +1.50 after 300. Varsity Tutors' twice-weekly pay and USD 15-40/hr come only from third-party sources; its tutor pages block automated fetches.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; you are an independent contractor and handle your own tax.

availability.notes: GoStudent runs sites for the UK, DE, AT, FR, IT, ES, TR, PL, NL and GR and says anyone over 18 can apply, but it names no residence rule. Varsity Tutors contracts with US residents only and reportedly excludes several US states (unverified).

risks: Low per-hour pay compared with independent tutoring

accounts: GoStudent or Varsity Tutors contractor account

AI homework help reduces demand for basic subjects, while exam prep holds up. Failure modes: unpaid sessions after missed feedback deadlines, fines for no-shows, and few assigned students in low-demand subjects.

Textbroker US pays per word by quality rating (3 stars 1.1¢, 4 stars 1.6¢, 5 stars 5.5¢; DirectOrders from 2.2¢) with payouts processed twice a week; Verblio pays per accepted piece and lets writers invoice weekly. strategies.name: Freelance teacher at an online language school with a set curriculum (Lingoda)

You choose time slots, the school fills them, and you teach without writing a curriculum or finding students. Unlike Preply or italki you don't set prices or compete on a marketplace. Lingoda wants C2 language level, a teaching certificate and 2-3 years of experience, and runs on freelance contracts.

payout.notes: Lingoda's jobs page confirms the freelance model and says teachers are 'paid on time'; its teacher-referral page (Nov 2026) confirms teachers are paid via a monthly teaching invoice. Still unconfirmed: the per-class pay rate (third-party sources report about USD 8-13 per hour or EUR 11 per class), the payment method (bank transfer assumed) and any minimum payout.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; freelancers must be legally able to invoice in their country.

availability.notes: Job listings say 'Remote - all countries' as long as you can legally freelance. Some languages require native-level skill.

strategies.evidence: Lingoda's official jobs page confirms the freelance model and requirements and describes a teacher-relations team that 'ensures every teacher is paid on time'.

tools: school-provided Zoom classes and CEFR materials

unitEconomics.notes: Lingoda does not publish pay (its jobs page gives no rate); TEFL.org reports about $8-13 (GBP 6.33-10.30) per hour-long class, so $8-13 is estimated and unverified.

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost. Assumes you already hold the required certificate; if not, a TEFL course costs $150-1,500 and should be counted as startup cash.

marketConditions.notes: For qualified teachers this is reliable but low-paid work. AI conversation apps and cheaper marketplace tutors pressure language-school subscriptions in 2025-26, which reduces open slots. Failure modes: rejection for missing credentials, class cancellations and slots not filling. Fact-check: median month-12 net lowered from $400 to $90 so it agrees with the 40% profit likelihood (fewer than half of starters clear $100/month, so the median starter cannot).

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: No pricing control; increase income by offering popular time slots, multiple levels and high reliability scores.
profitPath: Month 0: application, demo, contract (cost $0 if already certified)
Month 1-2: first classes, about $100-300/month
Month 3-6: 30-40 classes/month, about $350-500/month
Month 6-12: steady part-time schedule; $400-1,000/month

strategies.name: Generalist AI training / RLHF work (DataAnnotation, Outlier, legacy Remotasks)
strategies.summary: Write and rate chatbot responses, rank outputs and fact-check AI answers for model-training contractors. Pay is hourly, starting around $25/hour for general work.
strategies.howItWorks: AI labs pay data vendors for human preference data. After you pass a writing and reasoning assessment, projects appear in your dashboard, and you are paid hourly or per task for rating, rewriting or red-teaming LLM output. The work is irregular, and projects can disappear without notice. Vendors usually forbid using AI to produce your answers, so this is human labour. Scale wound Remotasks into Outlier.

payout.minimumPayout: DataAnnotation: no minimum stated; Outlier: not stated
payout.notes: DataAnnotation pays via PayPal, delivered within a few days of a request. Outlier states it pays weekly; its PayPal/Airtm methods come from third-party reviews and were not confirmed on an official page.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere. These are independent-contractor arrangements, and worker classification is being litigated (reported 2025 class action against DataAnnotation).

availability.notes: Each project limits which countries it accepts. Outlier cites 50 countries and requires a valid ID and phone from your country of residence. DataAnnotation requires English fluency; its country list is not published (reported as US/UK/CA/AU/NZ/IE). Remotasks cut off several African and South Asian countries in 2024.

strategies.evidence: DataAnnotation's official FAQ lists starting rates of $25-50/hour (general) and $40-150+/hour (coding/STEM) paid via PayPal. Outlier's official site says contributors are paid weekly in 50 countries. Activation odds are low, hence paymentProbability 5.

skills: following long guidelines (AI drafting usually forbidden)
accounts: Outlier account + ID and phone from your country

unitEconomics.notes: DataAnnotation's FAQ lists $25-50/hour for general work; Outlier and non-US rates are often lower, hence the $15 low.

breakEven.notes: No fixed costs, so every paid unit is profit; break-even equals the time to the first payout. Many applicants are never activated, so break-even for them never arrives.

marketConditions.notes: AI labs still buy large volumes of preference data, but spend has shifted from generalists to credentialed experts and synthetic data. After Meta's 2025 investment in Scale AI, several labs pulled work from Scale, causing Outlier project droughts. Winners are fluent writers who pass the assessment and get onto steady projects; the common failure is silent non-activation or a sudden project end. Median month-12 net profit was lowered below $100 so it agrees with a profit likelihood under 50% (most starters never reach $100/month).

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Rates are set per project; move up by passing specialist qualifications (coding, maths, a second language), which unlock higher-rate projects.
profitPath: Month 0: apply to DataAnnotation and Outlier, take the assessments carefully (cost $0)
Month 1-2: if activated, $100-500/month at 5-10 hours/week
Month 3-6: take specialist qualifications to reach higher-rate projects: $300-1,000/month
Month 6-12: income depends on project supply; keep two platforms active to ride out droughts

strategies.name: Online and phone mystery shopping (MSPA-member firms)
strategies.summary: Evaluate a company's website, chat, email or phone customer service as a covert customer and file a structured report.
strategies.howItWorks: Brands hire mystery-shopping firms to audit their service. Some assignments can be done entirely online: placing a web inquiry, testing live chat, calling a call centre or completing an online ordering flow. You then fill in a detailed questionnaire. Pay is typically $5-25 per online or phone shop, and many shops reimburse purchases. Most shops still need in-person visits, so online-only volume is small. Never pay to join, and treat any 'deposit this cheque' request as a scam.
platforms: MSPA-member firms (e.g. Market Force, BestMark, Intellishop)

payout.frequency: per assignment; schedule varies by firm
payout.notes: MSPA Americas shopper FAQ: payment terms vary by firm, some pay within a week and others within 30 to 60 days; remuneration is stated before you accept a project; shoppers should never pay a company to work or to be listed in its database.

legality.notes: Legal. Some assignments involve call recording, which needs consent under local law.

availability.notes: MSPA has Americas, Europe/Africa and Asia-Pacific chapters. Online-only assignments are concentrated in the US/UK/EU.

strategies.evidence: MSPA is the trade association for mystery-shopping firms. Pay figures could not be verified against an official firm page (Market Force pages unavailable when checked), so treat them as approximate.

unitEconomics.notes: Typical online/phone shop fees reported by shoppers (estimated; MSPA publishes no pay figures); purchase reimbursements are excluded because they are pass-through.

breakEven.notes: No fixed costs, so every paid unit is profit; break-even equals the time to the first payout. Firms pay 30-60 days after report acceptance.

marketConditions.notes: Online and phone shops are a small share of mystery shopping, which is still mostly in-person. Volume is concentrated in the US/UK/EU and scams impersonating real firms are common. Regular shoppers with good ratings earn $20-50/month online; only about 5% reach $100/month without in-person shops. profitLikelihoodPercent here is the chance of receiving any real net-positive payout within 12 months (typical income is under $100/month), calibrated to the catalog's survey-panel anchor.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Fees are set per shop; accept only shops paying at least $10/hour and ask schedulers for bonuses on hard-to-fill assignments.
profitPath: Month 0: register with 5+ MSPA-member firms (cost $0)
Month 1-2: 1-3 online/phone shops; first pay arrives after 30-60 days
Month 3-6: build ratings to get more offers: $20-50/month
Month 6-12: plateau; add local in-person shops if you want more volume

strategies.name: Mobile apps on App Store/Google Play (IAP + AdMob)
strategies.summary: Publish utility or casual apps and earn via in-app purchases/subscriptions (15% store fee under $1M) and AdMob ads.
strategies.howItWorks: Build focused apps (utilities, trackers, niche tools, simple games) with cross-platform frameworks. Users pay via IAP/subscriptions; Apple and Google take 15% under small-business tiers. Free users generate ad revenue via AdMob. Ongoing work is ASO, updates for OS changes, and policy compliance. Google Play requires 12 testers for 14 days for new personal accounts.

methods: AdMob: EFT, wire, Western Union Quick Cash, check where EFT unavailable, PayPal Hyperwallet (US only)
payout.minimumPayout: Apple: $40 default (as low as $0.02 for US/EU banks); Google Play: not re-confirmed; AdMob: $100 / EUR70 / GBP60
payout.notes: Apple pays within 45 days of fiscal month end; AdMob pays on or around the 21st of the following month once the threshold is met. Google Play: 15% on first $1M/yr, 15% on subscriptions (10% + 5% billing fee in AU/EEA/JP/UK/US).

legality.notes: Legal; apps must meet local content rules and privacy laws.
complianceRequirements: Apple $99/yr and Google $25 one-time developer fees

availability.notes: Google Play merchant registration supported in ~200 locations; AdMob payments broadly available.

automationPlan: AI agent builds Flutter/React Native apps
Fastlane CI for builds and store uploads
Automated ASO experiments and screenshot generation
risks: Low ad eCPM in many regions
strategies.evidence: Apple Small Business Program (15%), Apple's minimum payment threshold table, Google Play's 15% tier, and AdMob's payment threshold ($100/EUR70/GBP60) and ~21st payment date are all documented on official help pages.

skills: handling review guidelines and privacy forms
equipment: laptop (a Mac is needed for iOS builds)

unitEconomics.notes: Utility app subscriptions typically run $2-$10/month; Apple/Google take 15% under small-business tiers; backend cost per user is a few cents (rounded to $0). Google Play subscriptions in the US/EEA/UK/JP/AU are 10% + 5% billing fee (still 15%).

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). Recurring cost is mainly the Apple fee amortised (~$8/mo) plus a small backend; ad revenue is excluded from break-even.

marketConditions.notes: Winners combine ASO with paid acquisition or an existing audience; AI-assisted building in 2025-2026 drove a surge in new submissions, raising discovery difficulty. The 2025 US court ruling allowing external payment links in US App Store apps cuts fees for those who can steer users to web checkout. Failure mode: new Google personal accounts need 12 testers for 14 days, and most apps get under 100 downloads.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Use a free tier with a paywall on one compelling feature and weekly/annual subscription options; test price increases with RevenueCat experiments after 1,000 installs.
profitPath: Month 0: build MVP, enroll in both stores (cost $125)
Month 1-2: closed testing, launch; $0-$20
Month 3-6: ASO iterations and paywall tests; $10-$100/month
Month 6-12: localise listings and add features; $30-$1,000/month for top quartile

strategies.name: 3D models and game assets on Fab, Unity Asset Store, CGTrader
strategies.summary: Sell 3D models, environments, scripts and tools to game developers and 3D artists through engine marketplaces.
strategies.howItWorks: You build assets (models, materials, VFX, editor tools, code systems) and list them on Fab (Epic, 88% to seller), Unity Asset Store (70% standard share) and CGTrader (tiered 55-80% based on rolling 365-day sales). Buyers are indie devs and studios saving production time. Code tools/editor extensions often outsell raw models. Fab requires the 'Created with AI' flag on products made with generative AI.

methods: Fab: third-party payment provider (bank/PayPal by region)
Unity: PayPal monthly or bank transfer quarterly (USD only)
CGTrader: regular payout method in USD
payout.minimumPayout: Fab $100 (rolls over; paid regardless after 12 months); Unity per provider agreement; CGTrader none stated for sales ($10 for subscription earnings)
payout.frequency: monthly (Fab, Unity PayPal), weekly on Wednesdays (CGTrader)
payout.notes: Fab pays ~30 days after month end; CGTrader pays sales 20 days after sale (first payout no earlier than 20 days after KYC). Refunds deducted from next payout; tax forms required; Unity requires 2FA for payout profile.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere.

availability.notes: All three marketplaces pay internationally; excluded only in sanctioned countries.

automationPlan: Coding agents write Unity/Unreal tools and docs
manualSteps: Publisher account, tax and payout setup
risks: Flooding by AI assets lowers prices
strategies.evidence: Epic's Fab documentation states 88% share, $100 threshold and ~30-day payment; Fab support requires the 'Created with AI' flag; Unity docs describe monthly PayPal / quarterly bank payouts; CGTrader's official schedule lists 55-80% tiers and weekly payouts.

tools: Fab, Unity Asset Store, CGTrader (no fee to list)
skills: 3D modelling, UVs and texturing to game-ready standards
equipment: laptop or desktop with a capable GPU
accounts: Fab / Unity publisher accounts + tax forms

unitEconomics.notes: Median $25 asset pack; blended fee ~20% between Fab (12%, publisher keeps 88% per Fab docs), Unity (30%) and CGTrader (20-45%).

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost on the free tiers, so break-even is the first sale; months shown are the typical ramp to the first sale.

marketConditions.notes: Publishers of editor tools, systems and complete themed environments earn most; single props rarely sell. Text-to-3D tools (2025-2026) and Fab's free-asset promotions have flooded the low end, while well-supported code tools retain pricing power. Store review rejections and long build time are typical failure modes.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Start with a modest launch price and a free sample asset to gather reviews; raise price after updates and bundle into larger packs.
profitPath: Month 0: build and submit 1-2 high-quality packs (cost $0)
Month 1-3: pass review, first sales
Month 3-6: release monthly, respond to reviews; $20-150/month
Month 6-12: bundles, sales events; median ~$50/month

strategies.name: Creator storefront affiliate (LTK, ShopMy)
strategies.summary: Curate shoppable product collections and earn commissions across thousands of retailers through LTK or ShopMy.
strategies.howItWorks: Creator affiliate platforms aggregate retailer programs: you apply, then build storefronts/collections (outfits, home, beauty, gear) and share links on Instagram, blog, YouTube or newsletter. When followers buy, the platform collects commission from retailers and pays you your share; brands also offer gifting and paid collabs inside the platform. Works best with an existing lifestyle audience.

payout.minimumPayout: ShopMy $11 (confirmed); LTK threshold not confirmed on an official page (third-party reports say $25-$100)
payout.notes: ShopMy: commissions pending 30-120 days until the retailer pays, then paid weekly on Fridays via Stripe or PayPal. LTK help center blocked automated access, so its terms are unverified.

legality.notes: Legal; disclosure needed on every post.

availability.notes: Strongest for US/UK/EU/AU audiences; retailers mainly ship to those countries; creators elsewhere can join but conversions are low.

strategies.evidence: ShopMy's official payment FAQ documents the $11 minimum, weekly Friday payouts and 30-120 day pending period; LTK pays thousands of creators but its payout terms could not be re-verified.

unitEconomics.unit: per attributed sale (your share of commission)
unitEconomics.notes: Estimate: retailers pay ~5-20% on $60-150 fashion/home orders; the platform keeps a share and the rest is shown as your earnings, so the price already nets out the platform cut.

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost, so any commission is profit; months count ramp-up to the first payable earnings. Commissions stay pending 30-120 days until retailers pay.

marketConditions.notes: Earnings concentrate in creators with engaged lifestyle audiences of 10k+; brand gifting and paid collabs inside the platforms are where most of their income comes from. AI does not replace the trust factor, but feeds are crowded. Failure: storefront with no audience gets no clicks.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: No commission control early; once you have conversion data, pitch brands for flat-fee collabs ($100-500) in addition to commissions.
profitPath: Month 0: apply to ShopMy (and LTK), build 5 collections (cost $0)
Month 1-2: post outfit/home content 4-5x/week; expect $0-20
Month 3-6: grow audience; expect $20-100/month
Month 6-12: add brand collabs; median ~$50/month

strategies.name: Fonts, icon sets and UI kits on Creative Market / UI8
strategies.summary: Sell design assets (fonts, icon packs, Figma UI kits, mockups) to designers via curated asset marketplaces.
strategies.howItWorks: You produce a polished asset pack and list it on Creative Market (shop application with portfolio) or UI8 (curated). Designers and agencies buy commercial licenses. Creative Market's commission varies per shop/product (not published) and it pays monthly via Tipalti with a $20 minimum. Figma Community is not approving new creators to sell paid files (15% fee for existing sellers), so sell Figma kits via these marketplaces or Gumroad. Fonts need real type-design skill; icons/UI kits are faster with AI-assisted ideation.

payout.frequency: monthly (request by month end or auto-payment)
payout.notes: Creative Market pays via Tipalti in the first five business days of the month, usually arriving by the 10th; 2.5% FX fee for local-currency payouts; not all methods in all countries.

legality.notes: Legal; respect font licensing and trademark law.

availability.notes: Creative Market pays globally via Tipalti (bank/PayPal/wire, country-dependent); Figma paid Community closed to new creators.

automationPlan: AI ideation and vector cleanup scripts
strategies.evidence: Creative Market's support center documents the $20 minimum, Tipalti payout methods and fees; Figma help center states 'We are not approving new creators to sell paid files on Community at this time.'

tools: Creative Market / UI8 / Gumroad (no monthly fee)
skills: professional-grade icon, UI or type design

unitEconomics.notes: Median $24 for an icon set/UI kit; Creative Market's commission is not published - 40% platform share is estimated (Creative Market help pages bot-blocked) (UI8 and Gumroad take less).

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost on the free tiers, so break-even is the first sale; months shown are the typical ramp to the first sale.

marketConditions.notes: Established shops with large catalogues and bundle deals take most sales; marketplaces like Creative Market reject many applicants. Generative AI icon/illustration tools and all-you-can-download subscriptions (Envato, Freepik) pushed per-item prices down in 2025-2026; fonts with real craft hold value better.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Launch with a discounted intro price and free sample pack, then move to standard $19-39 pricing and offer extended licences at 3-5x.
profitPath: Month 0: build a portfolio and 2 polished packs, apply to stores (cost $0)
Month 1-3: approval; first sales
Month 3-6: release one pack per month; $20-100/month
Month 6-12: bundles and extended licences; median ~$40/month

strategies.name: Paid open-source bounties (Algora, Opire, Gitcoin)
strategies.summary: Solve GitHub issues that companies have attached cash bounties to and get paid when the PR is merged.
strategies.howItWorks: Companies and maintainers post bounties ($50-$5,000+) on GitHub issues via Algora and similar platforms. You (often assisted by an AI coding agent) claim the issue, submit a quality PR, and once merged the bounty is paid out. Payers are funded OSS companies wanting features/fixes. Competition is fierce on popular bounties, and spammy AI PRs get banned, so quality and communication matter. Gitcoin-style bounties pay in crypto and are less relevant now.

payout.notes: Algora fee/timing figures (payer pays fee on top; contributor gets 100% in ~1-8 business days) could not be re-confirmed: algora.io/docs/payments and algora.io/pricing return 404 and the algora.io homepage now markets hiring/recruiting. Replit Bounties is discontinued (replit.com/bounties redirects to Contra). IssueHunt has pivoted to a Japanese security bug-bounty platform and is no longer an OSS issue-bounty site.

legality.notes: Fiat bounties are ordinary contractor income. Crypto-paid bounties (Gitcoin) are restricted where crypto is banned.

availability.notes: Algora pays through Stripe Connect including cross-border payouts; some countries without Stripe payout support cannot receive.

automationPlan: Watch Algora/GitHub bounty labels via API and rank by value vs. difficulty
AI coding agent drafts fixes and tests
manualSteps: Claiming issues and communicating with maintainers
fullCycle: Sign up on Algora with GitHub
risks: Low-quality AI PRs lead to bans
Bounty platforms keep closing or pivoting (Replit Bounties closed; IssueHunt pivoted; Algora now recruiting-first)
strategies.evidence: Algora's open-source repo (github.com/algora-io/algora) still describes a GitHub app for bounties and tips with a Stripe-based payout processor, and public GitHub issues show /bounty and /claim payouts. Payment probability lowered from 5 to 3: Algora's public pricing/docs pages are gone and its homepage now leads with recruiting, Replit Bounties closed, IssueHunt left OSS bounties, and popular bounties draw many competing (often AI) PRs.

skills: communicate with maintainers (AI assists but cannot replace review quality)

unitEconomics.notes: Algora bounties typically range $50-$500 with occasional $1k-$5k items; payer pays the platform fee; cost is AI-agent credits per attempt (estimate).

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). One median bounty a month covers the AI subscription; unpaid attempts (PRs not merged) are the real cost and are not counted here.

marketConditions.notes: Winners are experienced contributors who specialise in one or two codebases and get assigned bounties before posting PRs. Since 2025 AI agents let anyone file a PR in minutes, so popular bounties get dozens of attempts and maintainers increasingly ban low-quality AI PRs or close bounty programs. Failure mode: many hours of unpaid work on PRs that lose the race.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Not price-set by you: target $100-$500 bounties in a stack you know, comment with a plan before coding, and build reputation so maintainers assign you work directly or offer paid contracts.
profitPath: Month 0: set up accounts and pick 2-3 repositories you can learn deeply (cost $0-$20)
Month 1-2: fix small issues to build reputation; first bounty expected $0-$200
Month 3-6: claim 1-2 bounties/month in the same codebases; expected $100-$400/month
Month 6-12: convert maintainer relationships into retainers or contract work

strategies.name: Run an EULA-compliant Minecraft community server monetized via a Tebex webstore
strategies.summary: Run an EULA-compliant Minecraft server selling cosmetics/access through Tebex.
strategies.howItWorks: Run a community server and sell through a Tebex store. Mojang's Usage Guidelines allow a single access price for everyone, cosmetics (not capes), non-competitive perks, donations with only server-wide rewards, and virtual currency that cannot be cashed out. Everything must be all-ages, with no gambling. Tebex is merchant of record (VAT, chargebacks) for a flat 5%.

payout.minimumPayout: PayPal $5; bank transfer about $20; wire about $50
payout.notes: Tebex charges a flat 5% (15% for FiveM) on its Starter (free) and Plus (GBP 12.49/mo) plans. Payments settle after 14 days by default; then PayPal takes 1-2 working days, bank transfer up to 7 days, wire 5-10 working days (GBP 12 per wire). A new payout method has a 5-day hold, the first withdrawal is capped at $1,000, and Hyperwallet compliance reviews can add 1-2 days.

legality.notes: Legal if Mojang's Usage Guidelines are followed: no loot boxes, gambling or pay-to-win, and in-game currency must not be cashable. Consumer-protection rules for minors apply (the EU and UK are strict).

availability.notes: Tebex pays out by PayPal, local bank transfer or wire; wire covers 200+ countries, and Tebex's wire list includes 46 of the 50 reference countries (missing Lebanon, Zimbabwe, Libya, Iraq). Needs a small monthly server rental (from about $10-20).

automationPlan: Infrastructure-as-code server deploys and automatic restarts/backups
AI-written plugins/configs and Discord moderation bots
Tebex packages delivered automatically by in-game commands
risks: Most servers never reach a paying player base
Mojang enforcement and blocklisting for non-compliant monetization
Hosting cost before revenue; DDoS and griefing
strategies.evidence: Mojang's Usage Guidelines (fetched 2026-11) explicitly allow paid access, cosmetics and non-competitive perks. Tebex's official docs (fetched 2026-11) give the 5% fee, 14-day settlement and per-method withdrawal minimums.

unitEconomics.notes: Server stores typically price cosmetics and ranks at $5-50; Tebex charges a flat 5% as merchant of record.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurring $15/mo (startup cash not amortised). About 2 purchases a month cover hosting; most servers need months to build a regular player base.

marketConditions.notes: Large networks with unique game modes and creator partnerships dominate server lists; small servers struggle to retain players. EULA rules limit pay-to-win, so revenue depends on cosmetics and community. Failure modes: no players, hosting costs with no sales, and EULA violations.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Start with low-priced cosmetics ($3-5) and a supporter rank ($10), run seasonal events, and add higher tiers only when the community asks.
profitPath: Month 0: server, plugins, Tebex store (cost $15 hosting)
Month 1-3: recruit players via server lists and Discord; $0-30/month
Month 3-6: events and cosmetics; $20-100/month
Month 6-12: most small servers stay under break-even or barely above

strategies.name: Sample packs and synth presets on Splice, Loopmasters and Producer Loops
strategies.summary: Create royalty-free loops, one-shots, MIDI and synth presets and distribute them through sample-pack labels that pay per download or per sale.
strategies.howItWorks: You build themed packs (drums, vocal chops, Serum/Vital presets, MIDI progressions) and either apply as a provider/label on Splice, where subscribers spend credits per sound and creators are paid per download, or register as a vendor/label on stores such as Producer Loops (50% royalty) or pitch Loopmasters/ADSR, which sell whole packs and pay a royalty share. You can also sell packs directly on Gumroad/your own store. Producers pay because ready-made, cleared sounds save them time.

payout.minimumPayout: Producer Loops: £100 balance (smaller amounts roll over); Splice and Loopmasters: not published
payout.frequency: quarterly (Producer Loops from 1 Jan 2026); Splice/Loopmasters per label agreement
payout.notes: Verified from Producer Loops provider terms (register page): 50% royalty on the GBP list price after VAT and affiliate payouts; 50% pro-rata share of FL Cloud license fees (curated labels) and of an AI-training royalty pool; paid via PayPal or bank transfer within 30 days after quarter end, £100 minimum. Vendor registration is still linked from the site, so the earlier 410 on the old 'sell your samples' URL was just a moved page. Splice says creators are paid each time a sound is downloaded and has paid out over $25M in total, but does not publish its per-download rate. Loopmasters invites producers to contact info@loopmasters.com and publishes no split.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; you license your own recordings royalty-free. Must not contain uncleared third-party audio.
complianceRequirements: disclose AI generation where label requires

availability.notes: Producer Loops vendor registration is self-serve and pays by PayPal (bank transfer for UK providers); Splice and Loopmasters accept creators internationally, but only after curation. PayPal receiving is limited in a few reference countries (e.g. Bangladesh, Libya, Iraq); Payoneer/Wise or local alternatives may be needed.

automationPlan: Script batch export, naming, tempo/key tagging and demo rendering
Automated preset rendering/previews from synth patch files
fullCycle: Apply to Splice/label or open own store
risks: Producer Loops now pays quarterly with a £100 minimum, so small sellers may wait several quarters
strategies.evidence: Splice reports paying sound creators over $25M since launching Splice Sounds; Producer Loops' provider terms publish a 50% royalty with quarterly PayPal/bank payouts.

tools: Gumroad or Payhip free tier for direct sales
skills: clean editing, naming and tagging of samples

unitEconomics.notes: Packs retail $10-50 (Producer Loops/Loopmasters); Producer Loops pays a 50% royalty (fee 50%). Splice per-download rates are unpublished. Hours amortise pack creation over expected sales. Splice royalty is estimated; Producer Loops' 50% royalty is confirmed on its provider terms.

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost. No cash outlay; Producer Loops pays quarterly with a GBP 100 minimum, so cash can lag sales by 4-9 months.

marketConditions.notes: Established labels with distinctive genre packs and big producer names dominate Splice and the stores. Subscription models have lowered per-sound income, and AI sample generators add free supply in 2025-26. Failure modes: label rejection, packs that sell a handful of copies, piracy of direct-sold packs.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Give away a free mini-pack to build an email list, price the first full pack at $10-15 direct, and pitch labels only once you have a track record or a niche (e.g. specific regional genres).
profitPath: Month 0-1: produce a 150-300 sound pack and a free sampler (cost $0)
Month 2-4: direct sales plus vendor listing; $0-50/month
Month 4-8: second pack, label pitches; first quarterly royalty
Month 8-12: a back catalogue of 3-4 packs; most earn $20-100/month

strategies.name: Data science / ML competitions (Kaggle, DrivenData, AIcrowd, Zindi)
strategies.summary: Enter prize-paying machine-learning competitions and get paid if your model places in the top ranks.
strategies.howItWorks: Sponsors post a dataset and metric with a prize pool. You build models, submit predictions, and top finishers are paid after code review and eligibility checks, usually with tax forms. AI coding agents can automate much of the feature engineering and model search. Prizes go to a handful of people per contest, so for most entrants the realistic gain is a portfolio.

payout.notes: Prizes are paid after the winner verifies eligibility and hands over code/licence.

legality.notes: Prize competitions with skill-based outcomes are legal everywhere. Some competitions limit prizes by country (e.g. US-only).

availability.notes: Open globally except sanctioned countries. Individual contests may restrict prize eligibility.

accounts: bank or PayPal for prize payment + tax forms

Prizes go to experienced grandmaster teams far more often than to newcomers. The realistic return for most entrants is a portfolio and job leads, not cash.

strategies.name: Direct-upload platform monetization on SoundCloud and Audiomack
strategies.summary: Upload music directly to SoundCloud (paid Artist/Artist Pro plan, fan-powered royalties, 100% royalty share) or Audiomack (AMP monetization program) and earn per-listener royalties.
strategies.howItWorks: Unlike DSP distribution, these platforms let you upload directly and monetize on-platform plays. SoundCloud pays fan-powered royalties (based on each listener's actual listening time and the ad/subscription revenue they generate) on tracks monetized through a paid Artist or Artist Pro subscription; there is no minimum-stream requirement and approval takes about 5 business days. Audiomack's AMP is free for authenticated artists with 100+ followers and 50K plays in 6 months, or available immediately with an Audiomack Pro subscription; it is popular in Africa and the Caribbean. Only 100% original, fully owned music qualifies on both. You grow plays through reposts, playlists and community engagement.

payout.minimumPayout: SoundCloud: $25 (after processing fees, from $0.50); Audiomack: not published
payout.frequency: monthly (SoundCloud, last business day; Audiomack NET 90)
payout.notes: Verified (help centers, Nov 2026): SoundCloud monetization requires a paid Artist (2 monetized tracks/month, select territories) or Artist Pro (unlimited) plan; artists keep 100% of royalties since Nov 2025; payouts go to PayPal or bank once the balance reaches $25, about two months in arrears (first data after 45-60 days). Audiomack AMP: free entry needs an authenticated profile, 100 followers and 50K plays in the last 6 months, or an Audiomack Pro subscription; earnings post to balance about 90 days after month end; tracks with leased beats, uncleared samples or remixes are excluded. Plan prices and Audiomack's cash-out minimum/method are not published in the help centers.

legality.notes: Legal; only upload music you own or control. Fake streams/bots violate ToS.
complianceRequirements: own 100% of rights to monetized uploads (no leased beats or uncleared samples)

availability.notes: Audiomack lists all 50 reference countries as AMP territories. SoundCloud's Artist plan is only in select territories, and SoundCloud's monetization country list was not found; it pays to PayPal or bank. PayPal receiving is limited in a few reference countries (e.g. Bangladesh, Libya, Iraq).

automationPlan: Scheduled uploads and metadata via API
risks: Tiny per-play payouts; SoundCloud's $25 threshold may take months to reach
SoundCloud needs a paid plan; Audiomack's free route needs 50K plays in 6 months
strategies.evidence: SoundCloud's help center documents fan-powered royalties, a 100% royalty share, a $25 threshold and monthly payouts; Audiomack's help center documents AMP eligibility, its NET 90 schedule and its territory list.

tools: SoundCloud Artist plan (~$3/mo, price not published in help center)

unitEconomics.notes: Per-play rates are not published; $5-30 per 10k plays is an estimate (Audiomack at the low end, SoundCloud fan-powered at the high end). SoundCloud artists keep 100% since Nov 2025. Hours are promotion time. Artist plan price (~$3/mo) is estimated: SoundCloud's pricing and help pages could not be fetched.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurring $3/mo (startup cash not amortised). About 2,000 SoundCloud plays a month cover the Artist plan; few new artists reach that, and payouts start at a $25 balance about two months in arrears.

marketConditions.notes: Monetized plays pay fractions of a cent, so only artists with sizeable followings earn noticeable money; Audiomack is strongest in Africa and the Caribbean. AI-generated uploads flood both platforms. Failure modes: paying the plan without enough plays and AMP thresholds not reached.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: No pricing; use the cheapest Artist tier only once plays justify it and route listeners to higher-value channels (Bandcamp, merch, live).
profitPath: Month 0: upload catalogue, subscribe to Artist plan (cost $3/mo)
Month 1-3: weekly releases and repost groups; under $5/month
Month 3-6: reach $25 cumulative balance for first payout
Month 6-12: most stay under $20/month; growth comes from a breakout track

Ghost takes 0% of revenue (Ghost(Pro) Publisher $29/mo billed yearly, or self-host on a cheap VPS); Memberful Standard charges $49/mo plus 4.9%.

strategies.name: Remote contract customer-support and moderation work (ModSquad, Arise, LiveOps, Working Solutions)
strategies.summary: Sign on as an independent contractor with remote support or moderation vendors and get paid hourly or per minute for scheduled online shifts.
strategies.howItWorks: Companies outsource chat, email, phone support and community moderation to vendors who contract remote workers. ModSquad (mods in 90+ countries) pays hourly for moderation and support projects; Arise contracts independent micro-businesses in the US, Canada, UK, India, the Philippines, South Africa and parts of the Caribbean and Latin America; LiveOps (US) pays for talk time; Working Solutions (US/Canada only) pays contractors for time worked in 15-minute increments. After a background check and short unpaid training, you book shifts in a portal and are paid every two weeks or monthly by direct deposit or PayPal. This is work, not a business, and automation is minimal, but it is one of the most dependable ways to be paid online if you can commit scheduled hours.

payout.notes: Working Solutions (official): independent contractors paid for time worked in 15-minute increments; applicants must be in the US or Canada. ModSquad (official): hourly, 90+ countries, apply via join.modsquad.com; payment method not published. Arise (official): network of independent businesses; its fees and business-entity rules were not visible on public pages. LiveOps page blocks automated reading.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere as contractor work; some vendors require a registered sole proprietorship (Arise) or local tax registration.

availability.notes: ModSquad: 90+ countries. Arise: US, Canada, Mexico, Dominican Republic, Barbados, Jamaica, UK, India, Philippines, South Africa. Working Solutions: US and Canada only. LiveOps: US.

automationPlan: AI drafting of replies inside vendor tools where permitted.
Automate shift booking alerts and timesheet logging.
strategies.evidence: ModSquad, Arise and LiveOps have paid remote contractors for over 15 years; pay rates and schedules are published on their recruiting pages.

skills: customer service writing or phone skills

unitEconomics.notes: Working Solutions pays $0.25-0.31 per productive minute (about $11-14/hour at 45 productive minutes); other US vendors pay up to about $20/hour and ModSquad and non-US rates are lower (estimated).

breakEven.notes: No fixed costs, so every paid unit is profit; break-even equals the time to the first payout. About 40 hours of unpaid screening and training come before the first biweekly pay. Avoid vendors that charge certification fees (Arise requires a business entity and fees).

marketConditions.notes: AI chatbots and voice agents have replaced much tier-1 support since 2024, so vendors are hiring fewer agents, though moderation and complex support remain. Pay is reliable once you are working shifts, but unpaid training and shift availability cause many to quit. Those who commit 15-30 scheduled hours a week reliably clear $100/month.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Pay is set by the vendor; move to higher-rate programmes (technical support, bilingual, moderation leads) after good performance metrics.
profitPath: Month 0: apply to 2-3 vendors, pass checks and training (about 40 hours, cost $0)
Month 1-2: first shifts: $200-600/month
Month 3-6: secure regular shifts: $400-1,200/month
Month 6-12: move to higher-rate programmes: $500-2,200/month
