strategies.name: Paid online exam marking for international exam boards (IB, Cambridge International)
strategies.summary: Qualified teachers mark scanned exam scripts online during exam sessions, paid per script or component by the exam board.
strategies.howItWorks: International exam boards hire seasonal examiners to mark IB Diploma, IGCSE and A Level papers. Scripts are scanned and marked on screen (e.g. RM Assessor), so you can work from home in many countries. You pass standardization, mark your allocation by the deadline and get paid per script. Experienced examiners move up to team leader, setter, item writer or moderator roles. The payer is the exam board, not students.

payout.notes: Cambridge International's examiner FAQ says assessment specialists are usually paid GBP 1.00-5.00 per script, depending on syllabus and script type, and that travel to required meetings is reimbursed. It does not state payment method or timing. IB pages block automated fetches, so IB fees, payment method and timing are unverified.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; contractor fees are taxable.

availability.notes: Recruitment is worldwide for many subjects; some roles require teaching the syllabus. Unverified per country.

automationPlan: Keep mark schemes and standardization notes organized
manualSteps: Marking every script by hand (AI marking is not allowed)
risks: Pay per script can be low
strategies.evidence: Cambridge International publicly recruits assistant examiners, team leaders, setters, item writers and moderators via assessors.cambridge.org, and its FAQ gives GBP 1-5 per script. The IB runs a global examiner network.

tools: RM Assessor or board's on-screen marking tool (provided)
skills: degree and teaching background in the subject
equipment: laptop or desktop with large screen
accounts: examiner contract with Cambridge International or IB

marketConditions.notes: Boards regularly recruit examiners, and qualified teachers who pass standardisation are reliably paid. Income is lumpy: a session can pay $500-2,000, which averages to $100-300/month. AI-assisted marking is being trialled but does not yet replace human examiners. Failure modes: no allocation in your subject, failing standardisation, and burnout at deadline time. Fact-check: median month-12 net lowered from $250 to $60 so it agrees with the 25% profit likelihood (fewer than half of starters clear $100/month, so the median starter cannot).

strategies.name: Paid online mock juror (eJury, OnlineVerdict, JuryTest)
strategies.summary: Read a case summary and answer lawyers' questions as a mock juror for $5–$60 per online case (more for virtual mock trials); US-only, infrequent, but reliably paid.
strategies.howItWorks: Trial lawyers test arguments on mock juries before court. Sites such as OnlineVerdict and eJury email case summaries to registered adults in the relevant county or federal district; you read the materials (20–60 minutes), answer questions and are paid per case. OnlineVerdict also runs Zoom mock trials paying $75–$700. Cases are infrequent (a few per year unless you live in a large metro), so the income is tiny, but the payout is near-certain and the work is interesting.

payout.notes: OnlineVerdict (official): online case reviews $30–$60, virtual mock trials $75–$700; paid only by mailed cheque 1–2 weeks after completion (Venmo/Zelle/PayPal only if a cheque is lost). eJury's FAQ page is gone and its rates ($5–$10 via PayPal) are unconfirmed.

legality.notes: Legal; OnlineVerdict requires US citizens aged 18+ living in the county or federal district where the case is tried. Some sites also exclude people working in law or insurance.

availability.notes: United States only.

risks: Very few cases outside large metros

accounts: mailing address for cheques or PayPal

strategies.name: Expert-domain AI training (Alignerr, Mercor, Outlier expert tracks)

Exclusivity means the free web version is cut back before enrolment.

Still unconfirmed: Royal Road's own author-pay and AI-labelling rules (royalroad.com and its blog return 403).

strategies.summary: Find and responsibly report security vulnerabilities in in-scope assets of companies that run public bounty programs.
strategies.howItWorks: Companies publish a scope, rules and reward tables. You test only in-scope assets under the program's safe-harbour terms, write a reproducible report, and get paid when the finding is triaged and accepted. huntr runs AI/ML-focused challenges with prize pools. Recon and scanning can be scripted within rate limits the program allows. Exploitation and reporting need skill, and payouts follow a power law.

Intigriti funds arrive 1-3 working days in Belgium and 3-5 internationally; the previously reported €50 minimum is not in its knowledge base and is unconfirmed.

legality.notes: Legal only within authorized scope and safe harbour. Testing outside scope is a computer-crime offence. Payouts are blocked for OFAC-sanctioned banks and persons.
complianceRequirements: follow program rules on automation/rate limits

availability.notes: Open globally apart from sanctioned countries. HackerOne cannot pay HDFC Bank India accounts.

Alerts for new programs and scope changes

risks: Legal risk if out of scope

Payouts follow a power law: a few hundred full-time hunters take most of the money.

strategies.howItWorks: Join the Fortnite Developer Program (18+), build an island in UEFN and publish it. Islands can also sell items for V-Bucks: the creator gets 50% of the V-Bucks value, or 100% from 9 Jan 2026 to 31 Jan 2027. Discovery is winner-take-most.

Payee setup is a Tax Identity tax interview (W-9/W-8), then a Hyperwallet account invite. unitEconomics.notes: Epic pays from a pool of 40% of eligible net Item Shop revenue by engagement; per-island payouts are not published, and the median island earns almost nothing (estimate). In-island V-Bucks sales pay 50% (100% until 31 Jan 2027).

marketConditions.notes: Payouts concentrate in a few hundred top islands run by professional studios with marketing budgets and trend-following updates. The 2026 in-island 100% sales promotion helps creators who already have traffic. AI-assisted Verse coding speeds building, but discovery is winner-take-most. Failure mode: a published island with no players.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: No direct pricing; maximise engagement payout through rapid trend-following updates, and price in-island items low (a few hundred V-Bucks) to convert paying players.
profitPath: Month 0-2: learn UEFN and publish a small island (cost $0)
Month 2-4: iterate on retention data; payouts often $0-10
Month 4-8: join a creator team or build trend maps; first $50+ month for a minority
Month 8-12: most earn under $20/month; hits earn thousands

strategies.name: Minecraft Marketplace content (partner program or contract work for partner studios)
strategies.summary: Make Bedrock Marketplace content as an approved partner or a paid contractor for partner studios.
strategies.howItWorks: Only approved Partners can publish Bedrock skin packs, maps, add-ons and textures to the Marketplace, and Mojang wants a portfolio and a business-like operation. Mojang suggests starting by working with an existing partner, so for an individual the realistic path is paid contract work for a partner studio, then applying directly. Partners earn a share of Minecoin sales.

payout.minimumPayout: Not published (partner terms are under NDA)
payout.notes: Mojang does not publish the Marketplace revenue split (unverified). Contract rates are negotiated per studio. Unconfirmed: the partner revenue split, minimum payout and payment schedule (no public Mojang/Microsoft page states them).

legality.notes: Legal creative work. Content must be original and all-ages, and must follow Minecraft Usage Guidelines.
complianceRequirements: Partner application and agreement (business entity often expected)

availability.notes: Partner acceptance is selective, and the countries partners can be in are not published. Contract work for studios is available wherever the studio can pay by PayPal/Wise. Estimate unverified.

automationPlan: Generate skin variations and texture drafts with image models, then hand-finish them
Use AI to write Bedrock add-on JSON/scripts
Auto-render marketing screenshots with scripted camera paths
manualSteps: Build a public portfolio (free maps/packs on CurseForge/MCPEDL)
Pitch partner studios or apply to the Partner Program
Quality and art direction to pass Mojang review
fullCycle: Contract with a partner studio or apply as partner
Get paid per project or a share of revenue
risks: Gatekept: most applicants are not accepted
Crowded catalogue and falling per-pack sales
Revenue terms are opaque and under NDA
strategies.evidence: minecraft.net/partner (fetched 2026-11) sets out the criteria and names partners that grew from small portfolios (CrackedCubes: about 100 projects in 2020, 800+ now).

skills: Minecraft skin, texture, map or add-on creation
accounts: PayPal or Upwork for contract pay

unitEconomics.unit: per contract deliverable for a partner studio
unitEconomics.notes: Partner studios pay negotiated rates; $50 per skin pack to $2,000 for a map is an estimate from freelance postings. Mojang's Marketplace revenue split is unpublished. Contract rates are estimated.

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost. No cash outlay; first contract usually comes after a portfolio of 3-5 pieces.

marketConditions.notes: Established partner studios produce most Marketplace content and hire freelancers for maps, skins and add-ons. Becoming a partner directly is hard for individuals. Failure modes: no contracts without a portfolio and low per-piece rates. Fact-check: median month-12 net lowered from $100 to $60 so it agrees with the 15% profit likelihood (fewer than half of starters clear $100/month, so the median starter cannot).

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Take small skin-pack or texture jobs at modest rates to build a portfolio, then quote per map/add-on at higher project rates once you have credited Marketplace releases.
profitPath: Month 0-1: build 3-5 portfolio pieces (cost $0)
Month 2-3: first small studio contract, $50-300
Month 3-6: 1-2 contracts a month; $150-600/month
Month 6-12: repeat studio work or partner application; $200-1,000/month for active creators

strategies.name: Monthly STL subscription for tabletop miniatures (Thangs Memberships, MyMiniFactory Tribes, Printables Clubs)
strategies.summary: Release a themed set of printable miniatures every month to paying subscribers on 3D-printing-native membership platforms.
strategies.howItWorks: Tabletop gamers with resin printers subscribe ($5-15/month) for a monthly release of pre-supported miniatures and terrain. Thangs Memberships charges a 14% platform fee (+Stripe fees); Printables Clubs launched with a 10% fee and Stripe payments (tiers $3-100); MyMiniFactory Tribes earnings are withdrawn via PayPal on the 14th/28th. Unlike generic Patreon, files are delivered automatically to a 3D-print search audience. Back-catalogue sets are later sold as bundles.

methods: MyMiniFactory: payout request -> PayPal (14th and 28th for Pro/Studio; 28th only for Upcoming) or bank transfer (monthly, 28th)
payout.minimumPayout: No minimum stated by Thangs, Printables or MyMiniFactory; MyMiniFactory charges a $2 processing fee on payouts under $100
payout.frequency: Thangs monthly; MyMiniFactory twice-monthly on request; Printables via Stripe
payout.notes: MyMiniFactory Tribes requires the Pro ($24.99/mo) or Studio ($99.99/mo) creator plan (store commission 15/12.5/10% by tier + 3.49% + $0.49 processing); the Tribes-specific commission is not published on the creator help center. Thangs membership fee 14% and Printables Clubs 10% confirmed on official pages.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; sculpts must be original (no Games Workshop/Disney likenesses).

availability.notes: MyMiniFactory pays by PayPal (45/50 reference countries) or bank; Thangs memberships limited to its Stripe country list (~21/50 reference countries); Printables Clubs via Stripe (limited country list).

automationPlan: Blender batch renders for promo images
Scheduled monthly release posts and Discord announcements
LLM writes lore/stat cards per release
manualSteps: Sculpting each month's set (ZBrush/Blender) - heavy manual art work
risks: Monthly content treadmill; churn when releases slip
Paid MMF tier is a fixed cost
strategies.evidence: MyMiniFactory creator help center documents payout schedule, $2 fee under $100 and store fees; Thangs help center publishes the 14% membership fee and supported countries; Prusa blog announced Clubs with a 10% fee. Dozens of mini studios run 4-5 figure monthly subscriptions.

tools: Lychee or Chitubox (free tiers) for pre-supporting

unitEconomics.notes: Median $10/month tier; Thangs 14% fee plus ~$0.60 Stripe processing. Each monthly release is a fixed ~60-80 hours of work regardless of subscriber count.

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost on the free tiers, so break-even is the first sale; months shown are the typical ramp to the first sale.

marketConditions.notes: Established sculptors with recognisable styles and back-catalogues earn thousands monthly; newcomers struggle to get the first 20 subscribers. The workload is a monthly treadmill, and piracy of STL packs is common. AI sculpting still falls short of print-ready minis.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Launch at $5-7 with a generous first release, then add a $10-15 tier with commercial-print licences.
profitPath: Month 0-2: sculpt a 6-10 model launch release (cost $0)
Month 2-3: launch, first 5-20 subscribers ($40-150)
Month 3-6: monthly releases, free samples; 10-40 subscribers

strategies.name: Author a produced course for a curated publisher (LinkedIn Learning, Pluralsight, Domestika)
strategies.summary: Pitch and audition to make a course that the platform produces and distributes. You get paid by the publisher through fees and/or royalties, not per student sale.
strategies.howItWorks: Curated course publishers recruit experts by application. LinkedIn Learning wants a teaching video sample and proposal. Pluralsight asks for an audition video, and its video-course pay is partly based on viewership, paid quarterly. Domestika covers production for creative courses and pays via PayPal. Once accepted, the publisher handles editing, marketing and enterprise distribution. That's different from self-publishing on Udemy or Skillshare.

methods: per contract (LinkedIn Learning/Pluralsight; method not published)
payout.notes: Pluralsight's teach page says video-course pay is 'partially based on viewership' and paid quarterly. Domestika's page says you need a verified PayPal account and that it covers production costs. LinkedIn Learning's instructor page says only 'earn extra income'. None of the three publish royalty percentages, upfront fees or minimums; terms are set in the individual contract.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere; you sign an IP license/assignment contract.
complianceRequirements: contract with IP assignment or license

availability.notes: Applications are open worldwide (LinkedIn teaching languages: EN, DE, ES, FR, JA, PT-BR, ZH). Acceptance is selective and favors recognized experts.

automationPlan: AI-drafted outlines, scripts and exercise files
fullCycle: Apply with proposal and sample video
strategies.evidence: Official instructor pages for LinkedIn Learning, Pluralsight (quarterly viewership payments) and Domestika (PayPal, production covered) confirm the programs are open to apply.

skills: recognised expertise in a business, tech or creative topic
writing a course proposal and audition video
accounts: LinkedIn Learning / Pluralsight / Domestika instructor application

unitEconomics.notes: Publishers do not publish rates; $1k-15k per course in the first year is an estimate from instructor accounts (upfront fee and/or royalties). Figures are author receipts after the publisher's share.

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost. No cash outlay; most applicants are not accepted, and accepted authors usually wait 6-12 months from proposal to first payment.

marketConditions.notes: Enterprise learning libraries have cut new commissions and refreshed catalogues as AI-generated and AI-assisted training spreads in 2025-26. Known experts with existing audiences get accepted; average applicants are not. Failure modes: rejection, exclusivity clauses and courses retired after a few years.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Terms are set by contract; negotiate a higher upfront fee where available and keep rights to repurpose material elsewhere.
profitPath: Month 0: proposal and audition video to 2-3 publishers (cost $0)
Month 1-4: if accepted, script and record with publisher (no pay yet)
Month 5-9: course published; first fee or quarterly royalty, $500-3,000
Month 9-12: pitch a second course or update; most earn $0-200/month averaged

strategies.name: Building and selling micro-SaaS products and apps (Acquire.com)
strategies.summary: Build a small SaaS, browser extension or mobile app to modest recurring revenue, then sell it to an acquirer.
strategies.howItWorks: Acquire.com (formerly MicroAcquire) and Flippa connect founders with buyers of small software businesses, typically valued at 2-4x annual profit/ARR. With AI coding agents you build a focused tool, get to a few hundred dollars MRR, and sell when the buyer pool values it. Distinct from content-site flipping because buyers price recurring software revenue, churn and code quality. Acquire charges sellers a $25-100/month listing fee and 6-8% closing fee.

payout.notes: Closing fee 6-8% due only if the sale completes.

legality.notes: Selling a software business is legal everywhere; sanctions screening applies to buyers.

availability.notes: Acquire.com and Flippa accept global sellers; payout by escrow wire.

automationPlan: AI coding agents build and maintain product
strategies.evidence: Acquire.com states it has facilitated thousands of acquisitions; its help page (updated Nov 2024, checked Nov 2026) confirms a 6-8% closing fee payable only on sale and a $25-100/month listing fee.

skills: shipping software (AI covers much of the coding)

unitEconomics.notes: Micro-SaaS sells at ~2-4x annual profit; a $500/month MRR app sells for ~$10-$20k. Cost = infra and tools amortised; Acquire.com closing fee 6-8% plus a $25-$100/month listing fee while listed (included in cost).

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). Fixed cost ~$40/month for tools and hosting; startup cash recovered at sale.

marketConditions.notes: AI coding agents made building cheap, so supply of tiny apps exploded in 2025-2026 and acquirers now want proven MRR and low churn. Winners pick boring B2B niches with distribution. Most projects never reach $500 MRR, which is the minimum that sells.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Launch with a low price ($9-$19/month) to get first customers, raise for new users once retention is proven; sell at 3x annual profit.
profitPath: Month 0: build an MVP with AI coding agents ($100 + $40/mo)
Month 1-6: launch, first 5-20 paying users
Month 6-18: grow toward $500+ MRR
Month 18-24: list on Acquire.com at 2-4x annual profit

strategies.name: Online math tutor for Cuemath (India-based tutors, global students)
strategies.summary: Graduates with strong school math teach Cuemath's curriculum online to K-10 students in 80+ countries; Cuemath supplies students and lessons.
strategies.howItWorks: Cuemath recruits tutors (mostly in India) after a communication test, a math test, an interview and training. It matches students to your time slots and provides a ready curriculum and interactive platform, so you only teach. Evening/night slots for US, UK and Australian students pay best. The company says top tutors earn more than ₹1,00,000 a month.

payout.notes: Cuemath's recruiting pages (checked Nov 2026) publish no per-class rate, payout method or schedule, only 'transparent payouts' and top earnings above ₹1,00,000 a month; joining is free with no deposits or set-up fees. Unconfirmed: per-class rate, payout method, schedule and minimum payout (re-checked Nov 2026).

legality.notes: Legal; contractor income is taxable (Indian TDS may apply).

availability.notes: Earnings and FAQs are in rupees for tutors in India; hiring outside India is not stated, so treat it as India-only (1 of 50 reference countries).

risks: night shifts for overseas time zones
strategies.evidence: Cuemath's recruiting page cites 4,000+ tutors, 200,000+ students in 80+ countries and top earnings above ₹1 lakh/month.

equipment: headset; a pen tablet may be required (unverified)

unitEconomics.notes: Estimated: Cuemath's tutor pages publish no per-class or hourly rate, only that tutors can 'take home more than ₹1,00,000 a month'; ₹250-650/hour is inferred from that claim and typical Indian online tutoring rates.

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost, so any commission is profit; months count ramp-up to the first payable earnings. Onboarding takes 2-6 weeks before the first paid class.

marketConditions.notes: Cuemath supplies students and curriculum, so accepted tutors with evening/night availability for US/UK/AU time zones get steady classes. AI math tutors add price pressure on the parent side, but live tutors for young children still sell. Failure: failing onboarding tests or having few slots in peak hours.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Pay is set by Cuemath; raise earnings by offering late-night slots, retaining students long term, and qualifying for higher grade levels.
profitPath: Month 0: apply, pass tests and training (cost $0)
Month 1-2: first students; expect $50-150
Month 3-6: fuller schedule; expect $150-400/month
Month 6-12: retained students; median ~$300/month

strategies.name: Selling or buying royalty income streams (Royalty Exchange, SongVest)
strategies.summary: Creators sell a slice of future music/book/IP royalties for a lump sum; investors buy royalty streams for periodic payouts.
strategies.howItWorks: Royalty Exchange and SongVest run auctions and offerings where owners sell a share or term of their royalty income (music publishing, master, book, film). Sellers need at least three years of royalty statements; Royalty Exchange charges no listing fee and takes a commission agreed before listing (rate not published; third parties report ~12-15%). Buyers receive royalty distributions in proportion to the share bought. SongVest sells fractional 'SongShares' under SEC Regulation A. Without royalties you can only participate as an investor (capital, decay risk).

payout.minimumPayout: Auction proceeds; investor distributions with no stated minimum
payout.notes: Royalty Exchange buyers wire funds into escrow within two business days of signing; funds are released to the seller after rights transfer. Investors are paid as the platform collects royalties. Seller commission and investor minimums are not published (unverified).

legality.notes: Royalty contracts are legal everywhere; buying foreign assets may need approval under capital controls in the 5 listed countries (5/50 = 10% restricted, so 90%).
complianceRequirements: tax on royalty income and sale proceeds

availability.notes: US-based platforms; international users can participate subject to KYC and US tax forms. Sellers need existing royalty assets.

fullCycle: Have or buy a royalty asset
strategies.evidence: Royalty Exchange describes itself as the largest royalty marketplace and publishes completed auctions; it explains sellers can sell a portion and retain copyright.

tools: Royalty Exchange / SongVest accounts (free to browse)
skills: reading royalty statements and decay curves
judging catalogue age and term (10-year vs life-of-rights)
accounts: platform account + KYC (some offerings need accredited-investor status)

unitEconomics.notes: Annual distributions per $1,000 at typical 6-10x purchase multiples ($60-$180). Cost = estimated annual decay/amortisation of the purchase price because royalties decline and term deals expire. Profit depends on capital, not effort. Distributions and decay are estimated; investor-side fees are not published on the Royalty Exchange or SongVest FAQs (SongVest refers to its Offering Circular).

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). Purchase price is consumed as the stream decays; $1,000 at ~$10/month takes ~100 months to recover in cash (resale on the platform may shorten this).

marketConditions.notes: Institutional catalog buyers pushed multiples up in 2021-2024, leaving retail auctions with older or smaller catalogues. AI-generated music and streaming payout reforms add downside risk to royalty growth. Profit depends on capital and purchase price, not effort: distributions start quickly, but net of decay many buyers barely break even. Cross-catalog calibration: profitLikelihoodPercent lowered from 45 to 30. Capital-return peers (savings 95, robo-advisor 70, brokerage bonuses 70) have paymentProbability 8-10, while this one has 3 (auction pricing, catalogue decay, platform risk), so its odds must sit well below theirs.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Bid no more than ~7x trailing 12-month royalties for decaying catalogues; for creators selling, set a reserve near 8-10x LTM earnings.
profitPath: Month 0: study 5-10 past auctions and buy one small stream ($1,000)
Month 1-3: first quarterly distribution (~$25-$40)
Month 3-12: track decay versus model
Month 12+: expect ~$120 per $1,000 per year gross, ~$70 net of decay

strategies.name: Roblox game monetization cashed out via DevEx
strategies.summary: Build a Roblox experience, earn Robux from game passes, items and Premium engagement, and convert to USD through DevEx.
strategies.howItWorks: You build a game in Roblox Studio (Luau scripting) and monetize with game passes, developer products, UGC items and Premium Payouts. Players spend Robux; earned Robux can be exchanged via the Developer Exchange (DevEx) at $0.0038 per Robux once you hold 30,000+ earned Robux (~$114). Success is hit-driven; most games earn nothing, a few earn millions.

payout.minimumPayout: 30,000 earned Robux (~$114 at the standard rate)
payout.frequency: one cash-out request per calendar month
payout.notes: Requires age 13+, verified email, DevEx portal (Tipalti) account and W-8/W-9. Standard rate $0.0038/Robux; $0.0054/Robux for certain purchases in eligible games by ID/face-verified US players aged 18+; Robux earned before Sept 5, 2025 cash out at $0.0035. Processing ~10 business days first time, ~5 thereafter, plus bank time.

legality.notes: Legal; Roblox itself has been blocked by some governments (platform availability, not illegality of the activity).

availability.notes: DevEx available in most countries except sanctioned ones; Roblox access has been blocked in a few countries at times.

risks: Hit-driven; most games get no players
strategies.evidence: Roblox Creator Hub DevEx documentation confirms the 30,000 Robux minimum, $0.0038 standard and $0.0054 higher rates, Tipalti portal and monthly request limit; Roblox publicly reports hundreds of millions paid to creators annually.

skills: marketing to a young audience within Roblox rules

unitEconomics.notes: Players pay ~$10-13 per 1,000 Robux; creator keeps 70% (700 Robux) and DevEx pays $0.0038 per Robux = ~$2.66, i.e. ~22% of player spend.

breakEven.notes: No fixed costs, but cash only arrives after accumulating 30,000 earned Robux (~$114) for DevEx.

marketConditions.notes: Roblox engagement keeps growing, but revenue is extremely hit-driven: studios and experienced teams with marketing budgets dominate the charts. AI assistants make building faster, but discoverability is the bottleneck; most solo games never reach the DevEx threshold.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Use cheap optional game passes (25-100 Robux) and developer products; tune pricing with A/B tests once you have traffic.
profitPath: Month 0-2: build a small game in a proven genre (cost $0)
Month 3-4: launch, iterate on retention; Robux trickle in
Month 5-9: updates and sponsored ads funded by earnings; reach 30,000 Robux only if the game catches on
Month 9-12: first DevEx (~$114) for a minority; median $0

strategies.name: Sell short fiction and poetry to professional-rate magazines (Asimov's, Clarkesworld, etc.)
strategies.summary: Submit original short stories and poems to magazines that pay per word on acceptance or publication, with no entry fee.
strategies.howItWorks: You write original stories and send them through free submission portals to professional genre and literary magazines. Asimov's pays 8-10 cents a word for stories up to 7,500 words and $1 a line for poetry, with replies in about five weeks. Uncanny pays $0.10 a word and $40 a poem but was closed to all submissions in Nov 2026. Rejections are normal, so you keep a submission tracker and resend rejected stories. Pro markets ban AI-written or AI-assisted work, so AI is limited to market research and tracking. Fee-charging contests are excluded.

payout.notes: Payment timing and method per market vary and are not stated in the Asimov's or Uncanny guidelines; Clarkesworld rate still not verified (its submissions page did not render guidelines for our fetcher). Asimov's rates and AI ban re-verified Nov 2026.

legality.notes: Writing and selling original text is legal in all reference countries; royalties are taxable.

availability.notes: Submissions open worldwide; payment via PayPal or check.

risks: AI bans: lifetime ban if caught
strategies.evidence: Asimov's and Uncanny guidelines state rates; SFWA membership counts earnings ($100 associate, $1,000 full).

unitEconomics.notes: Asimov's pays 8-10 cents/word up to 7,500 words, so a 5,000-word story earns ~$400-$500; smaller pro/semi-pro markets pay less. Hours per unit include stories written that are rejected. Verified: Asimov's pays 8-10 cents/word up to 7,500 words; Uncanny pays $0.10/word but is currently closed to submissions.

breakEven.notes: No startup cash or fixed cost, so break-even = first payment received. Acceptance rates at pro markets are around 1%; many writers take 1-3 years to make a first pro sale.

marketConditions.notes: A small set of skilled writers sell several stories a year; pro markets ban AI writing, and AI submission floods have forced magazines to close temporarily (Clarkesworld 2023; Uncanny closed in Nov 2026). Income is lumpy and rarely averages $100/month even for selling writers. Net high raised from $400 to $500 so a single pro-rate sale named in profitPath ($50-$500) fits within it.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Submit to highest-paying markets first and work down the list; never pay reading fees.
profitPath: Month 0: write and polish 3 stories, set up tracker (cost $0)
Month 1-6: keep 5-10 submissions out at all times, expected $0
Month 6-12: possible first sale $50-$500; reprint sales add small amounts

strategies.name: TikTok Creator Rewards Program (1-minute+ videos)
strategies.summary: Get paid per qualified view on original TikTok videos longer than one minute.
strategies.howItWorks: Creators 18+ with 10,000 followers and 100,000 views in the last 30 days, in an eligible country, join Creator Rewards. TikTok pays from its own program budget for 'qualified views' on original videos over 60 seconds; RPM depends on originality, watch time, search value and engagement. AI-generated content must carry TikTok's AI label, and unoriginal/reposted content earns nothing.

payout.notes: Estimated rewards settle about a month after the view month; withdrawals usually take a few days.

legality.notes: Legal everywhere in the set; TikTok itself is blocked/banned in some countries (not in this reference list's majority), which is availability rather than illegality.

availability.notes: Most-cited list (reported as quoting TikTok's program page): US, UK, DE, FR, JP, KR, BR, MX = 8 of ~50 reference countries (16%). TikTok's official page is JS-only and could not be fetched, so the exact list is unverified; check TikTok Studio > Creator Rewards.

automationPlan: AI scripting + editing pipelines for 60-90s videos
Scheduled posting via TikTok Content Posting API / approved schedulers
manualSteps: Account in eligible country with real identity
On-camera or voice work usually needed for retention
strategies.evidence: TikTok's Creator Rewards replaced the Creator Fund in 2024 with higher per-view rates; multiple 2026 guides document payouts and eligibility.

accounts: TikTok balance payout to bank or PayPal

unitEconomics.unit: per 1,000 qualified views (Creator Rewards RPM paid by TikTok)
unitEconomics.notes: Creators report roughly $0.40-$1.00 per 1,000 qualified views for 60s+ original videos (rounded to integers here: low $0, median/high $1); only views from eligible regions and 5s+ watch count (estimate from creator reports, not an official rate).

breakEven.notes: No startup cash or fixed cost, so break-even = first payout received. Requires 10,000 followers and 100,000 views in 30 days before any earnings; typical successful accounts take 4-9 months.

marketConditions.notes: Payouts concentrate among accounts doing search-friendly, 60s+ educational or storytelling videos. Program is only open in a minority of reference countries (~16% platform availability). RPMs have drifted down as more creators qualify, and AI-labelled or reposted content earns little; most starters never hit the 10k-follower bar.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: TikTok sets the RPM; raise it by making 60-90s search-targeted videos with high completion. Use reach to sell brand deals (TikTok One) and affiliate products, which usually pay more than Creator Rewards.
profitPath: Month 0: define niche and 20 video formats (cost $0)
Month 1-3: post daily, iterate on hooks; aim for 10k followers, expected $0
Month 4-6: join Creator Rewards if eligible; first $10+ withdrawals
Month 6-12: shift to 60s+ search videos and add brand/affiliate income

strategies.name: YouTube/podcast sponsorship marketplaces
strategies.summary: List your channel or podcast on sponsorship marketplaces so brands pay for integrated reads or segments.
strategies.howItWorks: Once a YouTube channel or podcast has a consistent niche audience, list it on YouTube Creator Partnerships (formerly BrandConnect, requires YPP in eligible countries) and third-party marketplaces (ThoughtLeaders, Passionfroot; Podcorn has been sunset). Brands pay flat fees or CPM for integrations, with briefs and reporting handled in-platform. This is distinct from affiliate links: payment is guaranteed per delivered placement rather than per sale.

payout.notes: Typically paid 30-60 days after the content goes live and is approved.

legality.notes: Legal; paid promotion must be disclosed (YouTube paid-promotion checkbox, spoken disclosure in podcasts).

availability.notes: YouTube Creator Partnerships: 18+, YPP members in 24 countries/regions (incl. US, UK, CA, AU, DE, FR, IT, JP, KR, IN, ID, PH, SG, BR, MX); third-party marketplaces mostly English-language audiences.

automationPlan: AI-assisted script integration and show notes
strategies.evidence: YouTube's official help page documents Creator Partnerships (formerly BrandConnect) for YPP creators with its 24-country list; marketplaces publicly list paid campaigns.

skills: growing a niche channel or podcast
accounts: YouTube Partner Program membership (for Creator Partnerships)

unitEconomics.notes: Estimate: niche integrations sell at ~$20-50 CPM of expected views, so a 10k-view video earns ~$200-500; 10% is an estimated marketplace cut (most charge brands instead).

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost, so any commission is profit; months count ramp-up to the first payable earnings. Only possible after an audience exists (typically 5k+ subscribers or 1k+ downloads per episode), which most people need over a year to reach.

marketConditions.notes: Sponsorship budgets are moving to mid-size niche creators, but brands buy proven view counts, so payouts accrue to channels that already grew. AI makes editing cheap but faceless AI channels face YouTube's 2025 'inauthentic content' demonetisation. Failure: never getting enough views to be booked.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Accept 1-2 discounted first deals for case studies, then price at a fixed CPM on 30-day average views and raise it 20% each quarter.
profitPath: Month 0: list existing channel/podcast on marketplaces (cost $0)
Month 1-6: grow audience; usually $0 in sponsorships
Month 6-12: first 1-2 integrations if audience exists; $100-500 each
Month 12+: repeat sponsors; median at month 12 still $0

strategies.name: TikTok Shop affiliate creator
strategies.summary: Promote TikTok Shop products in short videos/lives and earn commission on in-app sales.
strategies.howItWorks: Once eligible (18+, 1,000+ followers in the US, 500+ in the UK, plus an account risk review), you add products from the TikTok Shop marketplace to your showcase and create demo/review videos or livestreams. Sellers set commissions (commonly 10-30%) and often send free samples. Sales happen inside TikTok, so conversion can be high, but it requires consistent on-camera content.

methods: bank transfer via TikTok Shop creator wallet
payout.minimumPayout: Low/no minimum per market (withdraw from creator balance)
payout.notes: Commission settles after delivery and the return window, then is withdrawable to a linked bank. Exact settlement days and withdrawal minimums per market were not confirmed on an official page.

restrictedIn: Markets where TikTok is banned or restricted (none in most reference countries; check local status)
legality.notes: Legal; product claims must be truthful, and sponsored/affiliate content must use TikTok's commercial content disclosure.

availability.notes: Official TikTok Shop seller region list (Nov 2026): US, Mexico, Brazil, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand, Vietnam, Indonesia, Malaysia, Japan, Germany, France, Spain, Ireland, Italy, Poland, Netherlands, Belgium, UK. About 13 of the ~50 reference countries are covered; creators elsewhere cannot participate.

automationPlan: AI scripting of hooks and product demos
Track trending products and commission rates
manualSteps: On-camera filming and handling samples (physical step)
strategies.evidence: Official TikTok Shop creator pages state the 18+ and follower requirements (US 1,000+, UK 500+); the official seller site lists 19 markets. Seller-set commissions of 10-30% are reported by third-party guides.

tools: TikTok app + TikTok Shop creator centre
accounts: TikTok Shop affiliate KYC + bank account

unitEconomics.notes: Estimate: commissions 10-30% set by sellers on mostly $10-40 items give ~$1-20 per sale; free samples mean ~$0 product cost.

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost, so any commission is profit; months count ramp-up to the first payable earnings. Getting to the follower threshold usually takes 1-3 months; commissions settle after the return window.

marketConditions.notes: A small share of creators earn most commissions, usually with daily videos or livestreams in beauty, home and gadgets. TikTok Shop GMV kept growing in 2025-2026 but creator supply grew faster, and sellers trimmed open-collaboration rates. Failure: never reaching the follower bar or posting without sales.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Start with open collaborations, then use sales history to request targeted collaborations at higher rates (20-30%) plus paid flat fees per video.
profitPath: Month 0: grow account in one niche to the follower threshold (cost $0)
Month 1-2: request samples, post 1-3 videos/day; expect $0-50
Month 3-6: double down on converting products, try live; expect $50-300/month
Month 6-12: negotiate targeted rates and flat fees; median ~$100/month

strategies.name: Building and flipping content websites and newsletters
strategies.summary: Build (or buy and improve) a small content site or newsletter with traffic/revenue, then sell it on Flippa or Empire Flippers.
strategies.howItWorks: Buyers pay roughly 25-45x monthly profit for established sites/newsletters. You build a niche site or newsletter (AI-assisted), grow it to verifiable revenue over 6-24 months, then list it on Flippa (small deals) or Empire Flippers (larger, vetted). Proceeds move through escrow to your bank. Alternatively buy undervalued sites and improve them, which needs capital. Starter sites without revenue sell for little.

payout.minimumPayout: Per sale; Flippa self-service 10% success fee + listing fee from $29; Empire Flippers flat $10,000 commission up to ~$66.7k sale price, 15% up to $700k
payout.notes: Escrow and asset migration typically 2-6 weeks; earn-outs possible. Empire Flippers' $10k minimum commission makes it unsuitable for small sites; use Flippa below ~$70k.

legality.notes: Selling a website/digital business is legal everywhere; misrepresenting traffic or revenue is fraud.

availability.notes: Flippa and Empire Flippers accept sellers from almost all countries; escrow pays by international wire.

automationPlan: Automated P&L and traffic reporting for buyers
risks: Google updates crushing AI content sites
strategies.evidence: Flippa reports thousands of completed deals annually; Empire Flippers publishes sold-listing data with multiples.

unitEconomics.notes: Small content sites sell for ~30-40x monthly profit; a $100/month site sells for ~$3,000. Cost = domain, hosting and listing fee; Flippa self-service success fee 10% plus $29+ listing fee.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). Startup cash is recovered only at sale; ongoing hosting/tools ~$25/month.

marketConditions.notes: Google's 2024-2026 core updates and AI Overviews cut traffic to small content sites, so buyers pay lower multiples and demand verified traffic. Newsletters with engaged lists hold value better. Most builders never reach the $100/month needed to sell at a meaningful price.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Ask ~35x verified monthly profit, accept 25-30x for a quick sale; seed buyers by sharing transparent analytics.
profitPath: Month 0: launch a niche site or newsletter ($100 + $25/mo)
Month 1-6: publish 50+ pieces, grow list; revenue near $0
Month 6-12: monetise to $50-$200/month
Month 12-18: list on Flippa at ~30x monthly profit

strategies.name: Crowdfunding a creative/digital project (Kickstarter, Indiegogo)
strategies.summary: Pre-sell a digital game, book, tool or course to backers on Kickstarter or Indiegogo; Kickstarter pays out only if the goal is met, minus 5% plus processing.
strategies.howItWorks: You build a campaign page with a video, reward tiers (digital copies, early access, credits) and a funding goal. Backers pledge; on Kickstarter you only collect if the goal is met (5% platform fee + 3-5% processing). Indiegogo allows flexible funding. Digital rewards avoid shipping costs.

methods: direct deposit to bank (Kickstarter via Stripe)
payout.notes: Kickstarter: 5% of funds + Stripe ~3-5%, only if funded. Payout starts 14 days after campaign ends and lands 3-14 business days later.

legality.notes: Reward-based crowdfunding is legal; equity crowdfunding excluded. Must deliver promised rewards.

availability.notes: Kickstarter creators must reside in one of 25 countries (AU, AT, BE, CA, DK, FR, DE, GR, HK, IE, IT, JP, LU, MX, NL, NZ, NO, PL, SG, SI, ES, SE, CH, UK, US) with local ID and bank account: only 10 of the ~50 reference countries. Indiegogo accepts more countries (not re-verified).

automationPlan: AI-drafted campaign copy and update posts
Automated backer surveys and digital reward delivery
strategies.evidence: Kickstarter has raised billions for creative projects; fee structure documented in help center.

tools: pre-launch page and email list tools (free tiers)
AI for video scripts and art
accounts: Kickstarter account in an eligible country + Stripe

unitEconomics.notes: Median pledge ~$30-$50; Kickstarter 5% + processing 3-5%; cost = digital reward delivery plus pre-launch ads per backer (estimate).

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). No fixed cost; revenue arrives as one lump sum ~2-4 weeks after a successful campaign.

marketConditions.notes: About 4 in 10 Kickstarter projects reach their goal, but first-timers without a pre-launch email list mostly fail, and funded projects often spend the money on delivery. Games and tabletop dominate; AI-generated art is controversial with backers.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Set a low funding goal you can deliver on, offer early-bird tiers 20-30% off retail, and add higher tiers with collectible extras.
profitPath: Month 0-2: build prototype and pre-launch list of 500+ (cost $0-$500)
Month 3: run 30-day campaign
Month 4: receive funds (if funded)
Month 4-12: deliver rewards; sell post-campaign via late pledges

strategies.name: Domain name investing (flipping) and parking
strategies.summary: Register or buy brandable/keyword domains and resell them to businesses through Buy-Now listings on Afternic and Sedo.
strategies.howItWorks: You register available domains (~$10/year) or buy expiring ones, list them with Buy-Now prices on Afternic (GoDaddy network; Dan.com is being folded into it) and Sedo, and wait for an end user to buy. Annual sell-through for typical portfolios is ~0.5-2%, so you need hundreds of names and years of renewals; a single sale can be $500-$5,000. Parking revenue has collapsed (Google changed AdSense-for-domains defaults), so treat parking as negligible.

payout.minimumPayout: Per sale after escrow; Afternic minimum commission $15
payout.notes: Escrow and domain transfer take 1-4 weeks. Commissions: Afternic 15% (Basic) or 20% (Boost) with GoDaddy Aftermarket nameservers, otherwise 25%/30%; Sedo 10% (parked Buy Now), 15% (offers/auctions/unparked), 20% via SedoMLS partners.

legality.notes: Domain trading is legal everywhere; registering names containing others' trademarks is cybersquatting (UDRP/ACPA) and must be avoided.

availability.notes: Registrars and marketplaces accept customers from nearly all reference countries; payouts via wire, PayPal or Payoneer.

automationPlan: AI brainstorming and trademark screening of names
Auto-listing and price updates on Afternic/Sedo
Renewal pruning script based on inquiries
risks: Very long time to first sale
strategies.evidence: NameBio records thousands of public sales weekly; established investors report 1% annual sell-through with 10-30x markup.

unitEconomics.notes: Aftermarket sales of small investors cluster at $500-$5,000 (NameBio); cost = acquisition of the sold name; commission 15-30% on Afternic (25% Basic, 30% Boost, 15-20% with GoDaddy nameservers; $15 minimum) and 10-20% on Sedo. Sell-through is only ~1-2% of a portfolio per year.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). Fixed cost is renewal of ~50 domains (~$45/month); one sale covers ~3 years of renewals, but the first sale often takes 1-2 years.

marketConditions.notes: Profits concentrate among portfolio investors holding thousands of names bought years ago. AI startups create some demand for brandables, but AI name generators flood marketplaces and buyers increasingly pick available alternatives. Parking revenue is negligible. Failure mode: paying renewals for years on names that never sell.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: List with Buy Now prices in the $1,000-$3,000 band for brandables (fast lane on Afternic), accept offers above 3x acquisition cost, and drop names that get no inquiries after two renewals.
profitPath: Month 0: hand-register or buy 30-50 names (~$500)
Month 1-6: list on Afternic/Sedo with Buy Now prices; no sales expected
Month 6-12: prune non-performers before renewal; first inquiries
Month 12-24: first sale (if any) $500-$3,000

strategies.name: Reddit Contributor Program and Quora creator monetization
strategies.summary: Earn cash from awards/gold on Reddit and ad/subscription share on Quora Spaces for helpful answers.
strategies.howItWorks: On Reddit, redditors 18+ in supported countries with 100+ karma (5,000+ for Top Contributor) earn from Gold that other users spend on awards for their content (reported $0.009-$0.01 per Gold, $10 minimum; unused Gold cannot be cashed out). On Quora, Space owners can earn ad revenue share and Quora+ subscription revenue proportional to member reading. Both reward genuinely helpful, human contributions; automated or AI-spam posting violates rules and gets accounts banned, so automation is limited to research.

payout.notes: Reddit: program reported active Aug 2026, paid via Stripe 30-45 days after the earning month with Stripe fees (~$2.25 + 0.25%), per CloudsPress (Sep 2026) citing Reddit Help; Reddit pages block automated fetching. Quora monetization status in 2026 could not be verified.

legality.notes: Legal across the set.
complianceRequirements: Subreddit/Quora content policies (no spam, AI disclosure)

availability.notes: Reddit cash-out in ~35 countries (mostly North America/Europe); Quora monetization launched in ~25 countries.

automationPlan: Topic monitoring and AI research notes (human writes)
risks: Bans for promotional or AI content
strategies.evidence: Reddit launched the Contributor Program in 2023; a Sep 2026 summary of Reddit Help reports it still active with lower per-Gold rates. Quora creator monetization covered by TechCrunch (2021) but not re-verified for 2026.

tools: LLM only for research, never for posting
accounts: Reddit account (18+, 100+ karma, supported country) + Stripe

unitEconomics.notes: Reddit reportedly pays ~$0.009-$0.01 per Gold received ($9-$10 per 1,000 Gold); awards are rare, so it takes many hours of contributions to earn 1,000 Gold (estimate). Quora Space revenue is unpublished.

breakEven.notes: No startup cash or fixed cost, so break-even = first payout received. Reddit's $10 minimum means ~1,000 Gold before the first payout, which most contributors take many months to reach.

marketConditions.notes: Only highly active Top Contributors earn noticeable sums. AI-generated posting violates both platforms' rules and leads to bans, so automation is minimal. Quora's monetization has shrunk since its 2021 launch; treat this as a side effect of community work, not a business.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: No price setting; the useful play is using the reputation to drive traffic to your own newsletter, product or services.
profitPath: Month 0: join communities in your expertise, reach 100 karma (cost $0)
Month 1-6: answer daily, expected $0
Month 6-12: possible first $10 payout; route reputation to own offers

strategies.name: Interactive fiction for Choice of Games / Hosted Games
strategies.summary: Write branching text games in ChoiceScript, either commissioned by Choice of Games for an advance or self-written under the Hosted Games label for a 25% royalty.
strategies.howItWorks: Choice of Games commissions interactive novels: you pitch, get an outline accepted, and receive a $10,000 advance against 25% royalties, or $15,000 against 10%, paid in milestones that start with $100 for an invited pitch. On the Hosted Games route you write a game of at least 30,000 words, run a public beta for a month, and receive 25% of revenue from app, Steam and web sales. Players pay for the game, and in-app purchases add revenue. AI-generated prose, code and art are banned.

payout.minimumPayout: milestone advances; royalties per publisher schedule
payout.notes: Royalty payment frequency not stated on official pages (re-checked Nov 2026). PayPal only in supported countries.

legality.notes: Writing and selling original text is legal in all reference countries; royalties are taxable.

availability.notes: Contracts open to writers worldwide; paid via electronic deposit, PayPal or cheque. Authors in countries without a US tax treaty must contact Choice of Games before submitting.

strategies.evidence: Official pages give advance milestones and the 25% Hosted Games royalty.

tools: Choice of Games forum for beta

unitEconomics.notes: Hosted Games authors receive 25% of revenue from app, Steam and web sales; typical prices $3-$8. The commissioned route instead pays $10,000-$15,000 advances in milestones. Hosted Games 25% royalty verified.

breakEven.notes: No startup cash or fixed cost, so break-even = first payment received. A Hosted Game needs 30,000+ words plus a month of public beta; commissioned games pay a $100 first milestone after an invited pitch.

marketConditions.notes: Commissioned authors with strong samples earn the advances; most Hosted Games sell modestly. AI-generated prose/code/art is banned, so production stays manual. Long development times mean many writers see no income in the first year.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Publisher sets price; aim for a longer game with replay value, since length and reviews drive sales and price tier.
profitPath: Month 0: learn ChoiceScript, draft outline (cost $0)
Month 1-9: write 30k-100k words, public beta
Month 9-12: release; typical first-year Hosted Game royalties $20-$300/month at launch, fading

strategies.name: Indie games on Steam and itch.io
strategies.summary: Make small games or game assets and sell them on Steam (70/30) or itch.io (open revenue share, default 10%).
strategies.howItWorks: Build a small, polished game or tool (or asset packs) and sell to players. itch.io lets you set your own revenue share and pays via PayPal/Payoneer; Steam requires a $100 Steam Direct fee (recouped after $1,000 adjusted gross) and takes 30%, but offers vastly more traffic. Payers are gamers. Results are hit-driven; most games earn under $1,000 lifetime.

payout.notes: Steam pays monthly ~30 days after month end; itch.io pays out after a holding period on request. NOT re-confirmed in Nov 2026: Steamworks partner docs were unreachable and itch.io docs returned 403, so the Steam ~$100 threshold remains third-party reported.

legality.notes: Legal; observe age ratings and local content rules; avoid gambling mechanics (loot boxes restricted in some countries).

availability.notes: Steam pays to bank accounts in most countries; itch.io via PayPal/Payoneer globally.

automationPlan: AI generates art/code/sound assets (disclose AI use on Steam)
strategies.evidence: Valve's Steamworks docs describe the $100 recoupable fee; itch.io documents PayPal/Payoneer payouts to creators in its official forum announcements.

skills: art/audio (AI use must be disclosed on Steam)

unitEconomics.notes: Small indie games usually sell at $5-$15; Steam takes 30%; cost covers VAT/refund leakage (estimate). Steam 30% and the $100 recoupable fee are estimated; the Steamworks and itch.io pages were unreachable at check time.

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). No recurring cost; development time is the real investment. Steam recoups the $100 fee after $1,000 adjusted gross.

marketConditions.notes: Hits come from strong hooks and wishlist marketing; Steam saw roughly 19,000+ releases in 2025 and the median game earns under $1,000 lifetime. AI art is controversial with players and must be disclosed. Failure mode: a year of development and fewer than 100 sales.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Launch at $5-$10 with a 10-20% launch discount and wishlist-driven festival timing; avoid deep discounts until after the first major sale.
profitPath: Month 0-3: prototype, Steam page and wishlists (cost $100)
Month 4-8: demo, festivals; $0
Month 9-10: launch; $50-$500 one-off
Month 10-12: updates and sales; $0-$300/month long tail

strategies.name: Webcomics on WEBTOON CANVAS and Tapas (ad share, Super Likes, Ink tips)
strategies.summary: Self-publish a webcomic or illustrated serial and earn ad-revenue share and reader micro-payments once subscriber thresholds are met.
strategies.howItWorks: You publish episodes on WEBTOON CANVAS and/or Tapas. WEBTOON pays 50% of ad revenue once a series has 1,000 subscribers and 40,000 global monthly page views, and fans can send paid Super Likes once a series has 500 likes. Tapas shares about 70% of ad revenue from 100 subscribers and passes on 100% of Ink tips (after third-party fees) from 250 subscribers; creators must be 18+. Writers without drawing skill can partner with an artist; the platforms' AI-art rules should be checked first.

payout.notes: Eligibility thresholds re-verified Nov 2026 on both official creator pages (WEBTOON: 50% of static and video ad revenue, 1,000 subscribers + 40,000 monthly page views; Super Likes at 500 likes. Tapas: ad program at 100 subscribers, Ink support at 250, 18+). Payout minimums, rails and supported countries are only in the help centers (webtooncanvas.zendesk.com, help.tapas.io), which returned 403.

legality.notes: Writing and selling original text is legal in all reference countries; royalties are taxable.

availability.notes: Ad revenue programs may be limited by country (unverified).

strategies.evidence: Official WEBTOON and Tapas creator pages describe the programs and thresholds.

tools: check platform AI-art rules before using AI
skills: comic art or a partnered artist

unitEconomics.unit: per 1,000 page views (ad revenue before platform share)
unitEconomics.notes: Ad revenue per page view is unpublished; gross ~$1-$6 per 1,000 is an estimate. WEBTOON shares 50% (Tapas ~70%), and Super Likes/Ink tips add fan income. Verified: WEBTOON pays 50% of ad revenue once a series has 1,000+ subscribers and 40,000 global monthly page views; Tapas gives ~70% of ad revenue and 100% of Ink tips after third-party fees.

breakEven.notes: No startup cash or fixed cost, so break-even = first payment received. WEBTOON ad share needs 1,000 subscribers + 40,000 monthly page views; Tapas ad share starts at 100 subscribers.

marketConditions.notes: Earners are comics with large weekly readerships that combine ad share, Super Likes, Patreon and merch. A weekly comic is labour-intensive, and readers and platforms are hostile to AI art. Most series never reach WEBTOON's ad-revenue thresholds.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Enable tips/Super Likes early; use Patreon for advance episodes at $3-$5 once there is a loyal readership.
profitPath: Month 0: buffer of 10 episodes, launch on both platforms (cost $0)
Month 1-3: weekly updates, expected $0
Month 4-9: reach Tapas ad share and Super Likes; first $10-$50
Month 9-12: add Patreon; typical series $10-$100/month

strategies.name: Inkitt / Galatea serialized fiction revenue share
strategies.summary: Post novels free on Inkitt; stories that test well can be offered a contract to appear in the paid Galatea app with a revenue share.
strategies.howItWorks: You upload complete or ongoing genre novels (romance, fantasy, werewolf) to Inkitt. Inkitt uses reader data to pick stories and offers authors contracts to publish them in Galatea, a pay-per-episode reading app, paying a revenue share or royalties. There is no open monetization; payment needs selection and a signed contract.

payout.notes: inkitt.com returned 403 again (Nov 2026) and galatea.com shows no author terms; revenue-share percentages, advances and payout rails remain unverified. Read contract rights clauses carefully.

legality.notes: Writing and selling original text is legal in all reference countries; royalties are taxable.

availability.notes: Online globally; contract availability by country unverified.

strategies.evidence: Galatea sells many Inkitt-sourced titles; terms not publicly posted.

unitEconomics.notes: Inkitt/Galatea do not publish royalty rates; per-novel monthly royalties are an estimate from scattered author reports and highly uncertain. Galatea homepage publishes no author rates; Inkitt pages are bot-blocked.

breakEven.notes: No startup cash or fixed cost, so break-even = first payment received. Payment requires Inkitt to select the book from reader data and sign a contract; most uploads are never selected.

marketConditions.notes: A small number of high-engagement romance/werewolf novels get Galatea contracts. Contract terms have drawn criticism (rights scope), so read them carefully. Output is effort-heavy with no guaranteed pay.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: No pricing control; finish books and serialize consistently to generate reader data for selection.
profitPath: Month 0: upload completed opening arc (cost $0)
Month 1-6: finish the novel, update regularly, expected $0
Month 6-12: if offered a contract, negotiate rights; otherwise reuse the book on KDP

strategies.name: Wattpad Originals (successor to Paid Stories / Creators Program)
strategies.summary: Grow a following on Wattpad's free fiction app; selected or successfully pitched writers join Wattpad Originals, where some chapters are paywalled for Coins/Premium+ and writers get an undisclosed revenue share and sometimes an advance.
strategies.howItWorks: You publish serialized original fiction free on Wattpad and build reads, votes and comments. In October 2023 Wattpad replaced Paid Stories with Wattpad Originals, a freemium model: some chapters stay free, others are unlocked with Coins or a Premium+ subscription. Originals is invite-only by editorial selection, and from September 2024 Wattpad also took pitches, with accepted pitches eligible for up to $5,000 in advances plus an ongoing revenue share. Wattpad has not published the revenue-share percentage. Wattpad Studios/Webtoon Productions may also option rights.

payout.notes: Program status confirmed via TechCrunch (Oct 2023) and Wattpad's Sept 2024 BusinessWire release; revenue-share %, payout method, minimum and frequency still unverified because wattpad.com and support.wattpad.com fail TLS from this environment and the Wayback Machine is blocked.

legality.notes: Writing and selling original text is legal in all reference countries; royalties are taxable.

availability.notes: App is global; Originals is invite- or pitch-only and country eligibility is unverified.

strategies.evidence: Wattpad says creator opportunities paid authors nearly $10M over five years (TechCrunch, Oct 2023); Originals launched with 1,600+ titles; 2024 pitch call offered advances up to $5,000. Payout terms unverified.

unitEconomics.notes: Wattpad states accepted pitches can receive up to $5,000 in advances plus an unpublished revenue share; low/median are estimates. Hours per unit counts the writing needed to be selected. Wattpad pages could not be fetched (TLS error), so terms are estimated.

breakEven.notes: No startup cash or fixed cost, so break-even = first payment received. Selection is editorial and invite/pitch-only; most writers are never contracted, so 18+ months is typical for those who are.

marketConditions.notes: Paid Stories ended in 2023; only a small number of Originals are selected from millions of writers, usually stories with very large read counts. There is no open monetization, so effort rarely converts to money within a year. Use Wattpad mainly as audience-building for other channels.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: No pricing control; build read counts with frequent updates and tags, then pitch with traction data.
profitPath: Month 0: publish opening chapters with strong tags (cost $0)
Month 1-6: update 2-3x/week, grow reads/comments, expected $0
Month 6-12: pitch to Originals if reads are strong; most receive no offer

strategies.name: Amazon Influencer Program shoppable product videos
strategies.summary: Upload short product review videos that Amazon shows on product pages; earn commission when shoppers buy after viewing.
strategies.howItWorks: After acceptance (social account review) and onsite approval of test videos, you record honest 1-3 minute reviews of products you own and upload them to Amazon. Amazon places them on product detail pages; purchases attributed to your video earn onsite commissions, plus storefront/link commissions. Income comes from a growing video library without needing your own traffic. Payer is Amazon via the Associates payment system.

payout.notes: Same Associates payment cycle (~60 days after month end); onsite earnings use a separate Onsite Store ID that needs its own payment and tax info. Official US onsite rates (Table A) are 0-4% by category, mostly 0.5-3% (e.g. home 3%, beauty 2%, apparel 1%, books/toys/electronics 0.5%); Creator Ads (Table B) pay 0.5-5%. UK onsite table runs 0-6%.

legality.notes: Legal; videos must be genuine reviews of products you have used (no fake/incentivized reviews).

availability.notes: Most mature in Amazon US; also UK, DE, CA, IN and other stores with smaller programs. Shoppers must be in the store's market.

automationPlan: Shot lists and scripts drafted by AI from product specs/reviews
Track which ASINs have few videos
manualSteps: Physically handle and film products (unavoidable physical step)
risks: Onsite rates are low (mostly 0.5-3%) and change
Product costs if not already owned
strategies.evidence: Amazon's official help publishes the onsite commission tables (US Table A 0-4%, Creator Ads up to 5%; UK up to 6%), well below standard Associates rates. Creator reports range from hundreds to thousands per month for large libraries, though data is mostly self-reported.

skills: picking products with high search volume and few videos
equipment: products you already own or buy
accounts: Amazon Influencer Program acceptance (social account review)
separate Onsite Store ID with tax and payment info

unitEconomics.notes: Estimated (Amazon's help pages publish the onsite rate tables, but not per-video sales): creator-reported libraries average roughly $0.5-5 per video per month at 0.5-4% onsite rates; median assumes ~$10/video/year. Products already owned cost $0.

breakEven.notes: No fixed monthly cost, so any commission is profit; months count ramp-up to the first payable earnings. Earnings start once videos are approved and placed; payment ~60 days after month end. Startup recovery assumes about $30/month net at month 6.

marketConditions.notes: Winners upload hundreds of honest videos on products with many searches and few existing videos. Amazon has cut onsite rates (now mostly 0.5-3%) and the US carousel is crowded, so per-video earnings keep falling. Failure: low approval of test videos or a library of under 100 videos earning cents each.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: No pricing control; raise income per hour by targeting high-ticket home and kitchen products and being first to review new listings.
profitPath: Month 0: apply, film test videos, buy basic gear (cost ~$100)
Month 1-2: upload 30-60 videos of owned products; expect $5-30
Month 3-6: 20+ videos/week on new-release products; expect $30-150/month
Month 6-12: 300-500 video library; median ~$100/month

strategies.name: Online and retail arbitrage on Amazon FBA and eBay
strategies.summary: Buy discounted branded products (clearance, online deals) and resell them at higher prices on Amazon FBA or eBay.
strategies.howItWorks: Using tools like Keepa and SellerAmp you find products whose Amazon/eBay sell price exceeds retail-clearance or online-deal cost by enough to cover fees (Amazon US referral 15% in most categories, 8% electronics, FBA fees, $39.99/mo Professional plan or $0.99/item Individual; eBay ~13.6% + $0.30-0.40/order). You buy units, ship them to an Amazon warehouse (FBA) or list on eBay, and Amazon handles fulfillment. Amazon pays out every ~14 days. Margins are thin (~15-30% ROI).

methods: Amazon disbursement to bank (direct or via Payoneer)
payout.notes: Amazon disburses roughly every 14 days and may hold funds for new accounts (delivery-date-based reserve); disbursement cadence could not be confirmed on a public official page (Seller Central help requires login).

legality.notes: Reselling genuine goods is legal (first-sale/exhaustion doctrine); some brands gated, counterfeits prohibited.

availability.notes: Amazon lists ~27 store countries and accepts sellers from many more (needs an internationally chargeable card and a bank account; Payoneer for unsupported banks); exact registration-country list not confirmed. Works best for residents of US/UK/EU/CA/JP/AU. PHYSICAL STEP: buying and shipping inventory.

automationPlan: Automated deal scanning (Keepa API, Tactical Arbitrage)
manualSteps: Packing/shipping to FBA (or paying prep center)
strategies.evidence: Jungle Scout's annual State of the Amazon Seller survey reports most sellers are profitable, with many earning $1k-$25k/month; Amazon reports millions of active third-party sellers.

skills: prep and shipping to FBA; AI helps with listing but not sourcing judgement

unitEconomics.notes: Median $30 sale: ~$15 cost of goods + ~$5 FBA fulfilment/prep/inbound; Amazon referral fee ~15%; gives ~$5.50 contribution (~30% ROI target).

breakEven.notes: Fixed cost = recurringMonthlyUsd only (startup cash not amortised). Startup cash is inventory that turns over; recovery assumes ~$80/month median net (inventory cash keeps turning over).

marketConditions.notes: Experienced sellers with good sourcing software and ungated categories still profit, but deal-finding tools are commoditised so margins compress within weeks. 2025-2026 changes (inbound placement fees, low-inventory fees, stricter brand/IP enforcement) hurt beginners most. Common failures: IP complaints and suspensions, stuck inventory, underestimating fees and returns. Verifier: median month-12 net lowered from $150 to $80 so it agrees with a 30% chance of reaching $100/month; Professional plan $39.99/mo and 15% referral fee confirmed on sell.amazon.com/pricing.

businessPlan.pricingStrategy: Buy only at 30%+ ROI after all fees; price at or just below the Buy Box and reprice automatically, raising when competitors stock out.
profitPath: Month 0: open seller accounts and subscribe to tools ($80/mo), buy first $300-$500 of test inventory
Month 1-2: first sales; expect break-even to -$100 while learning fees
Month 3-6: reinvest profit, get ungated in 1-2 categories, ~150-300 units/month
Month 6-12: $100-$500/month net for those who survive; add wholesale accounts
